operations.specification: 1) Validate request body: email must be non-empty and contain '@' symbol; password must be non-empty. 2) Check hrm_time_tracking_members for duplicate email via unique constraint — if a member with the same email exists, return 409 Conflict with message 'This email is already registered'. 3) Hash the password using a secure one-way hashing algorithm (bcrypt, cost factor 10+). 4) Create hrm_time_tracking_member record: id (new UUID), email (trimmed/lowercased), password_hash (hashed output), display_name (default from email prefix before '@'), avatar as null, phone_number as null, created_at (now), updated_at (now), deleted_at as null. 5) Capture HTTP context: read client IP from request, current page href, and HTTP Referer header (may be null). 6) Create hrm_time_tracking_member_session record: id (new UUID), hrm_time_tracking_member_id (the new member's id), ip, href, referrer (may be empty string if null), created_at (now), expired_at (now + 30 days). 7) Generate JWT access token (15-minute expiry) containing member_id and session_id claims, and a refresh token (30-day expiry, containing session_id claim). 8) Return IHrmTimeTrackingGuest.IAuthorized with both tokens. Edge cases: empty email/email missing '@' → 400 Bad Request; empty password → 400 Bad Request; duplicate email → 409 Conflict.
operations.description:
Register a new user account and transition from anonymous guest to authenticated member.

The guest submits their email address and password to create a platform account. The email serves as the unique identifier across the entire system, as enforced by the unique constraint on the hrm_time_tracking_members table. The system validates the email format (must contain an '@' symbol), ensures no duplicate account exists with the same email, and confirms the password meets minimum requirements before hashing and storing it securely using a one-way hashing algorithm.

Upon successful validation, a permanent member record is created in hrm_time_tracking_members with the provided email and hashed password. A member session is established in hrm_time_tracking_member_sessions capturing the HTTP context at registration time — the client IP address, the current page URL (href), and the HTTP referrer (referrer) — for basic security auditing. The system issues a short-lived JWT access token (15 minutes) for authenticated API requests and a long-lived refresh token (30 days) for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

This operation is the entry point for all new users. The guest actor's anonymous device fingerprint record in hrm_time_tracking_guests is preserved for audit, while the new member identity becomes the primary actor for all subsequent interactions. Error handling follows the sign-up error specification: missing email, invalid email format, missing password, and duplicate email each produce appropriate error responses — the guest remains unauthenticated until successful registration completes.

Security considerations: passwords are never stored in plaintext; session expiry is enforced via the non-nullable expired_at timestamp; the email serves as a platform-wide unique identifier preventing account duplication; and token signatures prevent forgery of authentication credentials.

requestBody.description: Registration credentials containing the guest's email address and desired password for creating a new member account.

responseBody.description: JWT authentication tokens issued upon successful registration. Contains a short-lived access token for authenticated API requests and a long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-entering credentials.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: 1) Extract and decode the refresh token from the request body. 2) Verify the JWT signature using the server's secret key — if invalid or malformed, return 400 Bad Request with 'Invalid refresh token'. 3) Extract the session_id claim from the JWT payload. 4) Look up the corresponding hrm_time_tracking_member_session record by id. 5) If session not found, return 401 Unauthorized with 'Session not found'. 6) If session.expired_at < current timestamp, return 401 Unauthorized with 'Session expired'. 7) Extract the member_id from the JWT or from the session record, verify the corresponding hrm_time_tracking_members record exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL). 8) Generate a new JWT access token (15-minute expiry) with member_id and session_id claims. 9) Optionally rotate the refresh token — issue a new refresh token (30-day expiry), updating the session's expired_at to now + 30 days. 10) Return IHrmTimeTrackingGuest.IAuthorized with new tokens. Edge cases: malformed token → 400 Bad Request; expired or invalid session → 401 Unauthorized; deleted member account → 401 Unauthorized.
operations.description:
Refresh authentication tokens using a valid refresh token to obtain new access credentials without re-authentication.

Users who have previously registered through the join operation can use this endpoint to obtain a fresh access token by providing their refresh token. The refresh token was originally issued during the join operation and encodes the member session identifier (session_id) within its JWT payload.

The system validates the refresh token's cryptographic signature, confirms the referenced session record in hrm_time_tracking_member_sessions exists and has not yet expired (the expired_at timestamp must be in the future), and verifies the associated member account in hrm_time_tracking_members is still active (deleted_at is null). Upon successful validation, a new short-lived JWT access token (15 minutes) is issued, and the refresh token may be rotated for enhanced security.

This operation supports the two-token authentication pattern: the access token (short-lived) is used for everyday API calls, while the refresh token (long-lived, 30 days) is stored securely by the client and used only to request new access tokens when the current one expires. If the refresh token itself expires or the session is revoked, the user must re-authenticate through the join flow.

Security considerations: token signature verification prevents forgery; server-side session expiry enforcement via the expired_at column provides an additional security layer beyond token lifetime; soft-deleted member accounts cannot obtain fresh tokens; and expired sessions are rejected regardless of token validity to prevent indefinite token reuse.

requestBody.description: The refresh token obtained from a previous join or refresh response, used to request a new access token without re-entering credentials.

responseBody.description: New JWT authentication tokens issued upon successful refresh. Contains a fresh short-lived access token and an updated long-lived refresh token.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Create a new member account. Validate email is not empty and contains '@'. Validate password is not empty (minimum 8 characters recommended). Check email uniqueness in hrm_time_tracking_members table — if email already exists (including soft-deleted), return 409 Conflict. Hash the password using bcrypt. Insert a new hrm_time_tracking_members record with provided email, password_hash, and display_name. Create a hrm_time_tracking_member_sessions record storing IP, href, referrer from request context. Generate JWT access token (short-lived) and refresh token (long-lived). Return tokens and member identity in the response body.
operations.description:
Register a new user account on the platform.

Creates a new member account using the provided email address and password. The email address serves as the unique identifier across the entire platform — no two accounts can share the same email address. The display name is part of the global profile shared across all organizations the user later joins.

Upon successful registration, the system creates an authentication session recording the client's IP address, current page URL, and HTTP referrer for audit purposes, and issues JWT access and refresh tokens. The member is then authenticated and can proceed to select or create an organization context.

Security considerations: The password is hashed using bcrypt and never stored in plaintext. Email uniqueness is enforced at the database level via a unique constraint. Duplicate email registration attempts return a conflict error.

requestBody.description: Credentials and profile information required for new member registration.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and member identity returned upon successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticate a member using email and password. Look up member by email in hrm_time_tracking_members (exclude soft-deleted records where deleted_at IS NOT NULL). If not found, return 401 with generic 'Invalid email or password'. Compare provided password against stored password_hash using bcrypt.compare(). If mismatch, return 401 with same generic message (prevent account enumeration). Create hrm_time_tracking_member_sessions record with IP, href, referrer from request context. Generate JWT access token and refresh token. Return tokens with member identity.
operations.description:
Authenticate a member using email and password credentials.

Validates the provided email and password against stored credentials for an existing member account. On successful authentication, creates a new session recording the client IP address, current page URL, and HTTP referrer for security auditing, and returns JWT authentication tokens.

The system returns a generic 'Invalid email or password' error for both non-existent email and incorrect password to prevent account enumeration attacks. Soft-deleted accounts (deleted_at is set) cannot log in.

Upon successful authentication, the member receives tokens that must be included in the Authorization header of subsequent API requests to access protected features within their organization context.

requestBody.description: Member credentials — email address and password for authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and member identity returned upon successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refresh an expired or soon-to-expire access token using a valid refresh token. Extract refresh token from request body. Verify the JWT refresh token signature and check expiration. Decode the token to extract the session ID and member ID. Look up the associated hrm_time_tracking_member_sessions record. If session not found, expired (expired_at < now), or invalid, return 401. Verify the hrm_time_tracking_members record exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL). Issue a new JWT access token. Optionally rotate the refresh token. Return new tokens.
operations.description:
Refresh authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

Issues a new access token when the current one expires, using a valid refresh token obtained during a previous login or registration. This enables long-lived sessions without requiring the member to re-enter credentials periodically.

The refresh token is validated against the stored session record — the session must not be expired (expired_at must be in the future) and the associated member account must be active (not soft-deleted).

This operation is essential for maintaining continuous authenticated access while keeping access tokens short-lived for security. The new access token should be used for subsequent API requests until it expires.

requestBody.description: The refresh token previously issued during authentication, used to obtain a new access token.

responseBody.description: New JWT access and refresh tokens returned after successful token refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Search and list guest records with pagination and filtering.

Guest records represent anonymized, unauthenticated visitors identified by their device fingerprint. The system automatically creates a guest record when an anonymous visitor first accesses the platform, and soft-deletes it upon guest-to-member transition or administrative cleanup.

This endpoint supports paginated search with optional filters including device fingerprint text search, registration date range, and soft-delete inclusive query. Results are ordered by creation date descending by default.

Only authenticated members with appropriate permissions may access this endpoint. Guests themselves cannot list or search other guest records.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_tracking_guests table with the following implementation details:

1. **Base query**: SELECT from hrm_time_tracking_guests, respecting soft-delete semantics. By default (when includeSoftDeleted is false or unset), filter WHERE deleted_at IS NULL.

2. **Search filter**: When search text is provided, match against device_fingerprint using case-insensitive partial matching (LIKE/ILIKE).

3. **Date range filter**: When created_at_from and created_at_to are provided, filter created_at within the inclusive range.

4. **Pagination**: Standard page-based with page (1-indexed) and limit parameters. Return total count for UI pagination display.

5. **Sorting**: Default sort by created_at descending. Support sort field and direction overrides.

6. **Soft-delete inclusion**: When includeSoftDeleted is true, exclude the deleted_at IS NULL filter to show all records including soft-deleted ones. This is useful for administrative review.

7. **Relationship eager-loading**: Optionally include the count of guest sessions for each guest record when a load.sessionsCount flag is set.

8. **Security**: Enforce member-only access. Reject requests from unauthenticated callers. No organization-scoping needed since guests are tenant-agnostic.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of guest summary records containing identifying information, creation metadata, and optional session statistics. Results are sorted by creation date descending by default.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination criteria for listing guest records. Supports text search on device fingerprint, date range filtering on creation timestamp, pagination controls, sort configuration, and an option to include soft-deleted records.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single guest record by its unique identifier.

A guest represents an anonymous visitor who has not yet authenticated. Each guest is identified by a device fingerprint and may have multiple active sessions across different browsers. This endpoint returns the complete guest record including timestamps and soft-delete status.

Once a guest transitions to a member identity through successful sign-up or login, the guest record is soft-deleted (deleted_at is set) and subsequent lookups by ID will still return the record with the deletion timestamp populated.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the hrm_time_tracking_guests table by primary key (id). Return the full entity including soft-delete status (deleted_at may be populated). No authentication required beyond standard member token validation. The guest record is always returned regardless of deleted_at status — the caller can determine if the guest is active by checking if deleted_at is null.

responseBody.description: The complete guest record including device fingerprint, creation and update timestamps, and optional soft-delete timestamp.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the guest record to retrieve.
parameters.name: guestId

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member's global profile.

The global profile consists of the display name, avatar image, and phone number. These fields are shared across all organizations the member belongs to — updating a field here immediately reflects the change in every organization context.

Only the authenticated member's own profile can be updated via this endpoint. System-managed fields (email, password, timestamps) cannot be modified through this operation.

When the update succeeds, a user-profile-updated event is delivered to all organizations where the member has an active employee record, including back to the member themselves as confirmation.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the authenticated member's global profile in the hrm_time_tracking_members table.

1. Retrieve the authenticated member's ID from the JWT session token.
2. Validate the request body:
   - display_name: required, must be a non-empty string. Reject with clear error if empty.
   - avatar: optional (nullable string), URL of the avatar image.
   - phone_number: optional (nullable string).
3. Update the member record: set display_name, avatar, phone_number, and updated_at to current timestamp.
4. Do NOT update: id, email, password_hash, created_at, deleted_at — these are system-managed.
5. Return the full updated member record (IHrmTimeTrackingMember) as confirmation.
6. After successful update, trigger a user-profile-updated real-time event to all organizations where the member has an active employee record. The event payload includes the member ID and the updated profile fields.

responseBody.description: The updated member record with all fields, including the newly applied profile changes and updated timestamp.

requestBody.description: Updated global profile fields for the authenticated member. Only the fields to be changed need to be provided. display_name is required.

operations.description:
List the current member's active sessions.

Returns a paginated list of the authenticated member's active session records. Sessions represent authenticated browser/device sessions created when the member logs in. This operation enables members to review their active sessions, see which devices and browsers are connected, and monitor session metadata including IP address and creation timestamps.

Session records are append-only — each login creates a new session entry. Expired sessions (past their expired_at timestamp) are filtered out from results. Sessions are scoped to the authenticated member automatically; cross-tenant access is prevented by design.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_member_sessions table filtered by the authenticated member's ID (from JWT token).

Filter out expired sessions where expired_at < current timestamp to show only active sessions.

Support pagination with cursor-based or offset pagination in the IRequest body. Support sorting by created_at (default descending, newest first) and expired_at.

Apply search filters if provided: date range filter on created_at (from, to), ip address substring search, and href/referrer substring search.

Return IPageIHrmTimeTrackingMemberSession.ISummary with session id, ip address, href, referrer, created_at, and expired_at fields.

No JOINs needed — this is a single-table query on the sessions table. Respect data isolation: always scope to the authenticated member's ID from the JWT token context.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of the member's active session records, each containing session identifier, client IP address, page URL, HTTP referrer, creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering member sessions, including optional IP address search, date range filter on creation timestamp, sorting preferences, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single member authentication session by its unique identifier.

Provides detailed session metadata including the client IP address at session creation, the page URL where authentication occurred, the HTTP referrer indicating the navigation source, and the session validity window defined by creation and expiration timestamps. This enables security auditing, access pattern analysis, and session lifecycle monitoring.

Session records follow an append-only lifecycle — once created, they are never modified. Expired sessions remain in the database but are filtered out during authentication validation. Each session belongs to exactly one authenticated member, and a single member may have multiple concurrent sessions across different devices or browsers.

Only available to authenticated members with appropriate administrative permissions.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query hrm_time_tracking_member_sessions table by primary key (id) with the provided sessionId UUID. Return 404 Not Found if no session exists with the given ID. The session is returned regardless of its expiration status — expired sessions can still be retrieved for audit purposes. No joins needed unless caller requires the associated member details.

responseBody.description: The full member session record including authentication metadata (IP, page URL, referrer) and session validity timestamps.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the member session to retrieve, in UUID format (global scope).
parameters.name: sessionId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of user accounts with search and filtering capabilities.

This endpoint enables administrators to browse and search registered user accounts across the platform. Each user account represents a global identity with email, display name, avatar, and phone number that is shared across all organizations the user belongs to.

Search results are paginated and can be filtered by email address, display name, account creation date range, and account status (active vs. deleted). Results are ordered by account creation date by default, with support for custom sort fields.

The summary response contains core profile information sufficient for member listing displays, user selection components, and administrative user management interfaces.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_members table with pagination and filtering.

Implementation:
- Apply search filters on email (partial match), display_name (partial match), phone_number (partial match)
- Support date range filtering on created_at
- Support deleted_at filter: active-only (deleted_at IS NULL), deleted-only (deleted_at IS NOT NULL), or all (no filter)
- Default to active-only (deleted_at IS NULL) when no status filter specified
- Order by created_at descending by default, support custom sort by email or display_name
- Apply cursor-based pagination for large result sets
- Exclude password_hash from response for security
- Return total count when requested

Edge cases:
- Empty search criteria returns all active members
- Invalid email format in search returns empty results
- Combined filters use AND logic

responseBody.description: Paginated list of user account summaries containing core profile information: email, display name, avatar URL, and account metadata. Optimized for member listing and user selection displays.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering user accounts. Supports partial text matching on email and display name, date range filtering on creation date, account status filtering, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single member's full profile by their unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete public profile of a registered platform member, including their display name, email address, avatar URL, phone number, and account timestamps. The member represents a user account that spans all organizations the user belongs to.

The response excludes sensitive authentication data such as the password hash. If the specified member does not exist or has been deleted, the operation returns a not-found error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_tracking_members table by primary key id matching the provided memberId parameter.

Exclude the password_hash field from the response DTO for security — it must not be exposed through the API.

If no record is found with the given memberId, return a 404 Not Found error.

The query should include soft-deleted records (deleted_at is not a filter condition here), allowing administrators to view member details even after account deletion. Use "not found" semantics — if the record does not exist at all, return 404 regardless of deleted_at state.

responseBody.description: The full public profile of the requested member, including display name, email, avatar, phone number, and account lifecycle timestamps.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the member to retrieve.
parameters.name: memberId

operations.description:
Search and list organizations that the authenticated user has access to.

This endpoint returns a paginated list of organizations the user belongs to, either as an owner (organization creator) or as an employee member. Each organization is a fully isolated multi-tenant unit containing its own employees, projects, tasks, departments, roles, and time tracking data.

Search and filter capabilities include partial name matching, status filtering (active or deleted), currency filtering by ISO 4217 code, and timezone filtering by IANA identifier. Results are paginated and sorted alphabetically by organization name by default.

The response includes summary information for each organization: unique identifier, display name, description, currency, timezone, fiscal start month, and lifecycle status. This endpoint is typically used during initial login or organization context switching to allow the user to select which organization to work within.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query hrm_time_tracking_organizations joined with membership associations to determine which organizations the authenticated user can see. The user is associated with an organization either as the owner (via hrm_time_tracking_members join on hrm_time_tracking_member_id) or as an employee (via hrm_time_tracking_employees join on organization_id linked back to the user's member record). Apply search and filter criteria from the request body: search by name (partial match), filter by status (active/deleted), filter by currency, filter by timezone. Support pagination with page number and limit parameters. Return a paginated list of organization summaries sorted by name alphabetically by default, with optional sort field and direction overrides. Exclude soft-deleted or terminated organizations unless explicitly requested with status filter.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of organization summary records containing key identifying information (id, name, description, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month, status) for all organizations accessible to the authenticated user.

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for organization listing, including text search on name, status filter, currency/timezone filters, and pagination parameters (page number and limit).

operations.description:
Retrieves a single organization by its unique identifier.

Returns the full organization profile including display name, description, operational settings (currency, timezone, fiscal start month), and lifecycle status. Organizations serve as tenant boundaries that isolate all employee, project, task, timesheet, and other business data.

Only users who are members of the requested organization can access this endpoint. Membership is validated through the user's employee record within the organization. This ensures strict multi-tenant data isolation - users cannot access organizations they do not belong to.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_organizations table by primary key (id = organizationId UUID).

Validate that the requesting user belongs to this organization:
- Look up the employee record (hrm_time_tracking_employees) where hrm_time_tracking_member_id = authenticated user's member id AND hrm_time_tracking_organization_id = organizationId.
- If no such employee record exists, reject with 404 Not Found (data isolation - user cannot discover organizations they don't belong to).

Return all fields: id, name, description, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month, status, created_at, updated_at, hrm_time_tracking_member_id.

The owner's member ID (hrm_time_tracking_member_id) is included in the response so the caller can identify the organization owner.

Do NOT include related entities (employees, projects, departments, etc.) in this response - this is a single-entity retrieval only.

responseBody.description: The full organization record containing identity, configuration, and lifecycle fields.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the organization to retrieve. The requester must be a member of this organization.
parameters.name: organizationId

operations.description:
Create a new organization.

Creates a new organization owned by the currently authenticated member. The organization serves as the multi-tenant boundary within which all employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, timesheets, departments, roles, and related data are managed. Each organization operates as an independent tenant with strict data isolation from all other organizations.

Required fields include a globally unique organization name, a three-letter ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW), an IANA timezone identifier (e.g., America/New_York, Asia/Seoul), and a fiscal start month (1-12). An optional description may be provided.

On successful creation, the organization's status is set to "active" and the authenticated member is assigned as the organization owner with full control over settings, configuration, and lifecycle management.

Validation rules: organization name must be unique across all organizations; currency must be a supported ISO 4217 code; timezone must be a valid IANA identifier; fiscal start month must be an integer between 1 and 12 inclusive.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Query: Insert into hrm_time_tracking_organizations with the provided fields. Derive hrm_time_tracking_member_id from the authenticated member's session/user context. Auto-set status to 'active'. created_at and updated_at are managed by the database.

Validation rules:
1. Name uniqueness: @@unique([name]) on the table — catch Prisma unique constraint violation and return a human-readable error (duplicate name).
2. Currency: validate the provided ISO 4217 code against a supported set (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW, JPY, GBP). Return descriptive error listing accepted values if unsupported.
3. Timezone: validate against IANA timezone database. Return descriptive error for invalid/unrecognized identifiers.
4. Fiscal start month: must be integer 1-12. Return error if outside range.
5. Name: required, non-empty string.

Edge cases:
- The authenticated member must be a valid registered user (hrm_time_tracking_members record must exist). No guest access allowed.
- Duplicate name attempts: the @@unique constraint will throw — catch this and convert to a 409 Conflict response.

After creation, the organization's owner is automatically assigned the built-in Owner role via hrm_time_tracking_roles. The organization is immediately operational — the owner can invite employees, create projects, etc.

responseBody.description: The newly created organization with all its attributes including the generated id, owner reference, status (set to active), and timestamps.

requestBody.description: Organization creation payload containing the required name, currency, timezone, and fiscal start month, with an optional description.

operations.description:
Update organization settings.

Only the organization owner can update organization settings. This endpoint allows modification of the organization name, description, currency, timezone, and fiscal start month. The organization name must remain globally unique across all organizations.

**Ownership**: The authenticated user must be the organization owner (the user who created the organization). Non-owner members receive a permission error.

**Validation**: The system validates ISO 4217 currency codes, IANA timezone identifiers, and fiscal start month range (1-12). Duplicate organization names are rejected with a conflict error.

**Response**: Returns the complete updated organization record with all fields.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Verify the requesting user is the organization owner (hrm_time_tracking_member_id matches the authenticated user's id). Reject with 403 Forbidden if not the owner.

Validate uniqueness of the new `name` — query for any other active organization with the same name (excluding the current organization's id). Reject with 409 Conflict on duplicate.

Validate `currency` is a 3-letter ISO 4217 code.

Validate `timezone` is a valid IANA timezone identifier.

Validate `fiscal_start_month` is an integer between 1 and 12.

If `description` is provided, accept as free-form text; if null/omitted, retain existing value (optional field).

Update the organization row via Prisma: set name, description, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month, and update updated_at to now().

Return the fully updated organization record.

responseBody.description: The fully updated organization record reflecting all applied changes.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the organization to update (UUID, global scope).
parameters.name: organizationId

requestBody.description: Organization settings to update. Includes name (globally unique), optional description, ISO 4217 currency code, IANA timezone identifier, and fiscal start month (1-12).

prerequisites.description: The organization must exist before its settings can be updated. POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/organizations creates the organization, establishing the record that PUT subsequently modifies.

operations.description:
Permanently deletes an organization and all its associated data.

This operation removes the organization identified by the given unique identifier. Only the organization owner — the member who created the organization — is authorized to perform this deletion. The system enforces business prerequisites before allowing deletion: all timesheets across the organization must be in a resolved state (approved or rejected), and there must be no active employee contracts. If either condition is not met, the operation is rejected.

Upon successful deletion, the organization record and all related data including employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, timesheets, timers, departments, roles, invitations, and activity logs are permanently removed from the system through cascade deletion. This action is irreversible.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Verify that the requesting authenticated member is the organization owner by comparing the authenticated user's ID with `hrm_time_tracking_organizations.hrm_time_tracking_member_id`. If not the owner, reject with a 403 Forbidden error indicating only the owner can delete the organization.

Check business prerequisites before allowing deletion:
1. No pending (unapproved/unrejected) timesheets exist across all employees in the organization. Query `hrm_time_tracking_timesheets` joined through employee records. Timesheets with status other than 'approved' or 'rejected' are considered pending.
2. No active employee contracts exist. Query `hrm_time_tracking_employee_contracts` for contracts with `end_date IS NULL` (active/ongoing) belonging to employees in this organization. Also check contracts whose `end_date` is in the future.

If any prerequisite fails, reject with a 409 Conflict error detailing the specific blocking conditions.

If prerequisites pass, delete the organization record. The Prisma schema has `onDelete: Cascade` on relationships, which will cascade-delete all associated data (employees, projects, tasks, departments, roles, invitations, timelogs, timesheets, timers, activity logs, etc.).

After deletion, return the deleted organization record as confirmation in the response body.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization to delete (UUID). Must reference an existing organization record.
parameters.name: organizationId

prerequisites.description: The organization must exist before it can be deleted. POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/organizations creates the organization record that is referenced by the organizationId path parameter in this delete operation.

operations.description:
Search and list file attachments within an organization.

Organization files store metadata about uploaded files such as logo images and report attachments. Each file record contains the original filename, extension, MIME type, size, and storage URL. The type field categorizes the file's purpose (e.g., 'logo'). This endpoint returns a paginated, filterable list of files scoped to the specified organization.

Supports filtering by file type, name pattern, extension, MIME type, upload date range, and file size range. Results are ordered by creation date (newest first) by default. Soft-deleted files are excluded from results unless explicitly requested.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_organization_files table with organizationId filter and pagination.

Apply search filters:
- type: exact match on file purpose/category (e.g., 'logo')
- name: case-insensitive substring match
- extension: exact match (e.g., 'png', 'jpg', 'pdf')
- mime_type: exact or prefix match
- size: range filter (min/max bytes)
- created_at: date range filter

Default sort by created_at descending (newest first). Support sorting by name, size, type, and created_at.

Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL) unless includeDeleted flag is set in request.

Use the existing composite index on (hrm_time_tracking_organization_id, created_at) for efficient pagination with the organization scope filter. Use the index on (hrm_time_tracking_organization_id, type) when filtering by type.

Return cursor-based or offset-based pagination with total count.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of organization file summary records optimized for file management list displays. Each summary includes the file name, extension, MIME type, size, type category, version, and upload timestamp.

parameters.description: Target organization's unique identifier (UUID). All file records are strictly scoped within this organization boundary.
parameters.name: organizationId

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for organization files. Supports filtering by file type (e.g., 'logo'), name substring match, extension, MIME type, upload date range, and file size range. Includes standard pagination, sorting, and soft-delete inclusion controls.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single organization file by its ID, scoped within an organization.

Returns the full file metadata record including the original filename, extension, MIME type, file size in bytes, storage URL, file type/purpose category, and optional version number for tracking updates such as logo changes. The response does not contain the actual file binary content; use the returned `url` field to access the file from external storage.

The operation is scoped to the specified organization — the file must belong to the organization identified by `organizationId`. Cross-tenant access is prevented: only files belonging to the active organization context can be retrieved. Soft-deleted files (with a non-null `deleted_at` timestamp) are excluded from results.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_organization_files table with WHERE id = {fileId} AND hrm_time_tracking_organization_id = {organizationId} AND deleted_at IS NULL.

Apply organization context filtering — the {organizationId} must match the authenticated member's active organization context. Return 404 NOT FOUND if the file does not exist or belongs to a different organization (including soft-deleted files). Return 404 rather than 403 to avoid leaking information about file existence across organizations.

Only active (non-deleted) files are returned. The response contains all fields from the organization_files table: id, name, extension, mime_type, size, url, type, version, created_at, updated_at.

responseBody.description: The full organization file metadata record including filename, extension, MIME type, file size, storage URL, type category, and version tracking information.

parameters.description: UUID of the organization that owns the file (global scope). The authenticated member must have this organization as their active context.
parameters.name: organizationId

parameters.description: UUID of the organization file record to retrieve (scoped to organization). Must belong to the specified organization.
parameters.name: fileId

prerequisites.description: Organization must exist as the tenant boundary for file scoping. The file record references the organization via a foreign key (hrm_time_tracking_organization_id) and cannot exist without it.
The file record must exist before it can be retrieved by ID. This POST creates the file metadata record that the GET operation reads.

operations.description:
Upload or register a new file attachment for the specified organization.

Files serve as organizational attachments for purposes such as logo images or report attachments. Each file is categorized by a `type` field that determines its purpose and applicable validation rules. The actual file content must be uploaded to external storage (e.g., S3, CDN) prior to calling this endpoint — the `url` field in the request body should contain the storage URL or path where the file content resides.

This operation requires the authenticated user to have appropriate permissions within the organization context. For logo uploads, the `org:manage` permission is required. The system validates file size, format, and type-specific constraints before creating the record. When replacing an existing file of the same type (e.g., updating the organization logo), the `version` field is automatically incremented to support cache invalidation and version tracking.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Verify the organization exists and the requesting user has appropriate permissions (org:manage for logo uploads, or appropriate project/report permissions for other file types).
Validate file constraints based on the `type` field:
- For 'logo' type: validate MIME type is an image format (image/png, image/jpeg, etc.) and file size is within the supported maximum.
- For other types: validate against any type-specific constraints.
Validate that `name`, `extension`, `mime_type`, `size`, `url`, and `type` are all provided in the request body.
Set `version` to 1 for new files; increment version if an existing file of the same `type` already exists in the organization (e.g., replacing an old logo).
The `hrm_time_tracking_organization_id` is taken from the path parameter, not the request body.
Create the record and return the full file entity with generated id and timestamps.
Handle duplicate file type constraints (e.g., only one active logo at a time per organization).

responseBody.description: The newly created file attachment record with system-generated UUID identifier, auto-managed version number, and creation/update timestamps.

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the organization that will own this file attachment (global scope).
parameters.name: organizationId

requestBody.description: File metadata including the original filename, file extension (without leading dot), MIME type, file size in bytes, storage URL from external upload, and the purpose type (e.g., 'logo', 'report_attachment'). The optional version field can be specified for version tracking, but is typically auto-managed by the system.

prerequisites.description: Organization must exist before a file can be attached to it. POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/organizations creates the organization and returns the organizationId UUID required in the file upload path.

operations.description:
Soft-delete an organization file attachment.

This operation permanently deletes a file record from the organization by marking it as removed via soft deletion. The file's metadata such as original name, type, size, and storage URL are preserved in the database for potential recovery before permanent cleanup. The actual file content in external storage (e.g., S3, CDN) is not affected by this API operation.

Security: Only the organization owner or users with appropriate `file:manage` permission can delete files. File access is strictly scoped to the owning organization — cross-tenant access is prevented.

Once deleted, the file record is no longer returned in list results and cannot be used for its original purpose (e.g., as an organization logo). If the file being deleted is the current organization logo, the organization's logo should be reset to the default.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Perform soft deletion on hrm_time_tracking_organization_files by setting deleted_at to the current timestamp.

1. Verify the organization exists and the requester has permission (organization owner or file:manage permission).
2. Verify the file exists and belongs to the specified organization by matching both organizationId and fileId.
3. If the file's type is 'logo' and it is the current active logo, handle the organization's logo reference (reset to default or null).
4. Set deleted_at = now() on the record; do NOT physically remove the row.
5. Return the deleted file entity in the response body with the updated deleted_at field.
6. Throw 404 if the file is not found within the organization. Throw 403 if the requester lacks permission.

parameters.description: UUID of the organization that owns the file (global scope).
parameters.name: organizationId

parameters.description: UUID of the file to delete (scoped to the organization).
parameters.name: fileId

prerequisites.description: Organization must be created before a file within that organization can be deleted. The soft-delete operation verifies organization existence as its first validation step — the operation fails with 403/404 if the organization does not exist.

The file record must be created before it can be soft-deleted. The operation verifies the file exists and belongs to the specified organization — the operation fails with 404 if the file has not been created or does not belong to the organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of organization snapshot audit trail records.

Organization snapshots are immutable point-in-time records that capture the complete state of an organization whenever a significant lifecycle event occurs — such as creation, settings updates, ownership transfers, or deletion. Each snapshot preserves the organization's name, description, logo, currency, timezone, fiscal start month, owner identity, and status at the moment of the event, along with the actor member who triggered it and the event type classification. This table is append-only — entries are never modified or deleted, ensuring a reliable audit trail for organizational governance.

This endpoint allows organization administrators to browse the full audit trail of changes. Results can be filtered by event type (e.g., "created", "settings_updated", "ownership_transferred", "deleted"), by date range of when snapshots were created, and by the member who performed the action. Results are sorted by creation timestamp in descending order by default, showing the most recent changes first.

All operations are strictly scoped to the organization identified by the path parameter — data isolation is enforced across tenants, and only snapshots belonging to the specified organization are accessible.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_tracking_organization_snapshots table with strict organization scoping.

1. **Data isolation**: WHERE hrm_time_tracking_organization_id = {organizationId}. Never allow cross-organization access.

2. **Filters** (all optional, from requestBody):
   - `event_type`: exact match filter — one of 'created', 'settings_updated', 'ownership_transferred', 'deleted'
   - `created_at`: date range filter (from/to timestamps)
   - `hrm_time_tracking_member_id`: exact match against the actor member who triggered the event
   - Free-text search on `event_details` (LIKE/contains pattern)

3. **Sorting**: Default sort by created_at DESC (newest first). Support sort field and direction from request body.

4. **Pagination**: Support page/limit parameters from request body for cursor-based pagination.

5. **Response**: Return IPageIHrmTimeTrackingOrganizationSnapshot.ISummary with total count, pagination metadata, and snapshot summary records.

6. **Edge cases**: Append-only table — no write operations applicable. Return empty page if no snapshots exist for the organization.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of organization snapshot summary records, each containing the event type, creation timestamp, organization attributes captured at snapshot time (name, description, currency, timezone, fiscal start month, status), and actor identity (member ID, display name). Optimized for audit trail browsing with chronological display.

parameters.description: The UUID of the organization whose snapshot audit trail is being queried (scoped to this organization).
parameters.name: organizationId

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering the organization snapshot audit trail. Supports filtering by event type (e.g., 'created', 'settings_updated', 'ownership_transferred', 'deleted'), date range (created_at from/to timestamps), actor member ID, free-text search on event details, and pagination parameters (page, limit) with sorting options.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single organization lifecycle snapshot by its unique identifier.

Organization snapshots are immutable point-in-time records that capture the complete organizational state at the moment a significant lifecycle event occurred. These events include organization creation, settings changes (name, description, currency, timezone, fiscal start month), ownership transfers, and organization deletion. Each snapshot preserves a full copy of all organization attributes as they were at that moment, along with the identity of the user who triggered the event and contextual details about what changed.

The snapshot includes the organization's name, description, logo URI, currency setting, timezone, fiscal start month, the owner's member ID and display name at that time, the organization status at that moment, the event type classification, and any additional event details. This endpoint is restricted to organization members with appropriate access rights within the active organization context.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_tracking_organization_snapshots table filtering by the composite of organization ID and snapshot ID.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate that the requesting user belongs to the organization identified by {organizationId} (via their employee record).
2. Query: SELECT * FROM hrm_time_tracking_organization_snapshots WHERE id = {snapshotId} AND hrm_time_tracking_organization_id = {organizationId}.
3. If no record found, return 404 Not Found — the snapshot either does not exist or does not belong to the specified organization.
4. Return the full snapshot record as the response body.

Edge cases:
- The organization may be in 'deleted' status — snapshots are still accessible for audit purposes.
- The requesting user's employee record may be deactivated — consider whether to allow access based on business rules.
- The snapshot is immutable and append-only; no record locking or version conflict handling needed.

responseBody.description: The full organization snapshot record including all denormalized organization attributes at the time of the event, the actor who triggered it, event classification, and event details.

parameters.description: UUID of the organization that owns the snapshot (scoped to active organization context).
parameters.name: organizationId

parameters.description: UUID of the organization snapshot to retrieve.
parameters.name: snapshotId

prerequisites.description: Organization must exist before any organization snapshots can be created or retrieved, as the snapshot record has a foreign key dependency on the organization.
The organization snapshot must have been previously created before it can be retrieved by its unique identifier.

operations.description:
Creates a manual point-in-time snapshot of the organization's current state, preserving all configuration attributes and ownership information for historical reference.

When an organization owner needs to capture the current configuration before making significant changes — such as updating settings, transferring ownership, or restructuring — this operation creates a complete archival record. The snapshot stores a denormalized copy of all organization attributes (name, description, logo, currency, timezone, fiscal start month), the owner's identity and display name, and the current status, along with the acting user and optional contextual notes.

This supplements the system's automatic snapshots created during lifecycle events (creation, settings updates, ownership transfers, deletion), providing on-demand capture flexibility for audit and governance purposes. Snapshots are immutable once created and provide a reliable historical record for organizational accountability.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Validate organization exists and is 'active' — reject with 404 if not found or status is 'deleted'.
2. Verify authorization: only the organization owner (organization.hrm_time_tracking_member_id matches authenticated user) may create manual snapshots.
3. Enforce organization data isolation — ensure the organization belongs to the authenticated user's context.
4. Read the full current state from hrm_time_tracking_organizations for the given organizationId.
5. Resolve the actor's display name from hrm_time_tracking_members (owner_display_name).
6. Construct the snapshot record:
   - hrm_time_tracking_organization_id: organizationId
   - hrm_time_tracking_member_id: authenticated user's member ID
   - name, description, logo_uri, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month: from current organization
   - owner_member_id: from organization.owner
   - owner_display_name: resolved from owner's member record
   - status: current organization status
   - event_type: 'snapshot'
   - event_details: from request body (optional)
7. Create the snapshot record (append-only).
8. Return the created snapshot with 201 status.

responseBody.description: The created organization snapshot containing the complete denormalized organization state at the moment of capture, including the actor who triggered it and the event classification.

parameters.description: The target organization's unique identifier (UUID). The snapshot will capture this organization's current attributes, owner information, and status at the time of creation.
parameters.name: organizationId

requestBody.description: Optional contextual details to annotate the snapshot. The remaining snapshot fields (organization attributes, owner info, status) are automatically populated from the current organization state, and the actor is resolved from the authenticated user.

prerequisites.description: The organization must exist and be in 'active' status before a snapshot can be created. The snapshot operation reads the complete current organization state (name, description, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month, owner info, status) to build the archival record. Without a prior organization creation, there is no organization to snapshot.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, searchable list of departments within the current organization.

This endpoint provides all employees with visibility into the organizational structure. Departments are organized in a single-level hierarchy where top-level departments may have child sub-departments, but sub-departments cannot have their own children. The response includes parent department information to describe the hierarchy.

Search and filtering capabilities allow narrowing results by department name, parent department, or description text. Results are paginated for efficient browsing of large organizational structures. Each department entry includes summary information suitable for list displays and hierarchy navigation.

Access to this endpoint is available to all employees within the organization — no special permissions are required. Soft-deleted departments are excluded from results by default.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_departments table scoped to the authenticated user's organization (hrm_time_tracking_organization_id from session context).

Support the following search/filter capabilities from IHrmTimeTrackingDepartment.IRequest:
- name: partial text search on department name (case-insensitive LIKE)
- parentId: filter by parent department (null for top-level only)
- description: partial text search on description
- Include/exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL by default)

Apply pagination using standard cursor/offset pagination fields from the request body. Sort by name, created_at, or updated_at.

Return IPageIHrmTimeTrackingDepartment.ISummary with: id, name, description, parentId, parentName (if parent exists), createdAt, updatedAt. Count children for each department to indicate nesting depth.

Exclude soft-deleted records by default (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL). If a search parameter for including deleted records is provided, include them.

Edge cases:
- Organization has no departments → return empty page
- Search yields no results → return empty page with total = 0
- Request includes invalid sort field → fall back to default sort (name ascending)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of department summary records with hierarchy information, including department name, description, parent department details, and child department counts.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering departments including name search, parent department filter, description search, pagination parameters, and sort options.

operations.description:
Retrieve the full details of a specific department within the organization by its unique identifier.

Departments are organizational units that group employees by function, team, or business area. Each department has a unique name within the organization, an optional description explaining its purpose, and an optional parent department establishing a single-level hierarchy (child departments grouped under a parent).

The response includes the department's name, description, parent department information, creation and update timestamps, and the total count of child departments. All employees within the organization can access this endpoint without special permissions — department visibility is available to all organization members.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the hrm_time_tracking_departments table by id, filtering out soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL). Must scope the query to the authenticated user's organization context via hrm_time_tracking_organization_id — join with employee record or organization membership to verify the user belongs to the owning organization. Include the parent department's name in the response for hierarchy display (join with self-referential parent relation). Optionally include a count of child departments. Return 404 Not Found if the department does not exist, has been soft-deleted, or belongs to a different organization. Return 403 Forbidden if the requesting user is not a member of the owning organization.

responseBody.description: The full department entity including name, description, parent department reference, child department count, and system timestamps (created_at, updated_at). Excludes soft-deleted departments.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the department to retrieve.
parameters.name: departmentId

prerequisites.description: The department must be created first via the create department operation so that it exists in the database and can be retrieved by its unique identifier.

operations.description:
Create a new department within the organization.

Creates a new organizational unit identified by a unique name within the organization. Each department belongs to a single organization and can optionally be placed under a parent department to form a two-level hierarchy (parent department with child departments). The department name must be unique — no two departments within the same organization can share the same name.

A description can be provided to document the department's function or purpose. If a parent department is specified, the system validates that the parent exists within the same organization and that it is a top-level department (departments cannot be nested deeper than one level).

After successful creation, a real-time department-created event is emitted to notify organization members of the new department.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new department within the member's current organization context.

Implementation steps:
1. Extract the organization ID from the authenticated member's session context (not from request body).
2. Validate that `name` is non-empty string.
3. Validate uniqueness: query `hrm_time_tracking_departments` for existing record with same `name` AND same `hrm_time_tracking_organization_id`. If exists, reject with 409 Conflict.
4. If `parentId` is provided:
   a. Query the parent department by `id`. If not found within the same organization, reject with 422 Unprocessable Entity.
   b. Verify the parent department has no parent itself (parent_id must be null) — enforce one-level nesting rule. If parent has a parent, reject with 422.
   c. Verify the parent is not the same department being created (circular reference prevention — though this is a create, so circular can only be validated at update).
5. Create the department record with:
   - `id`: generated UUID
   - `hrm_time_tracking_organization_id`: from session
   - `parent_id`: from request body (optional, UUID from parentId field)
   - `name`: from request body
   - `description`: from request body (optional, may be null/undefined)
   - `created_at`: current timestamp
   - `updated_at`: current timestamp
   - `deleted_at`: null
6. Emit `department-created` event for real-time notification.
7. Return the created department record as response.

Edge cases:
- Name uniqueness violation → 409 Conflict.
- Parent department not found → 422 Unprocessable Entity.
- Parent department is already a child (has parent_id set) → 422 Unprocessable Entity (one-level nesting violation).
- Empty name → 400 Bad Request (validation).
- Name exceeding reasonable length → 400 Bad Request (string maxLength).

responseBody.description: The newly created department record with all fields including server-generated identifiers and timestamps.

requestBody.description: Department creation payload containing the department name (required), optional description, and optional parent department identifier for hierarchy placement.

operations.description:
Update an existing department's properties including its name, description, and parent department assignment.

All employees within an organization can view departments, but only authorized members (Manager/Owner role or custom role with department edit permission) can update department records.

When updating the parent department assignment, the system enforces a single-level hierarchy constraint — only top-level departments (those without an existing parent) can be assigned as child departments. The parent department must belong to the same organization. Setting parentId to null promotes the department back to a top-level unit.

The department name must be unique within the organization. Soft-deleted departments cannot be updated.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate that the department exists and is NOT soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL); reject with 404 if not found or soft-deleted.

Validate the organization context from the authenticated member's session matches the department's hrm_time_tracking_organization_id — reject with 404 if cross-org access.

Validate the new name is unique within the organization (query for existing department with same name, different id, same org_id, deleted_at IS NULL).

If parentId is being set to a non-null value:
  - Validate parent department exists in the same organization and is NOT soft-deleted
  - Validate the parent is not the same department (no self-reference)
  - Validate that the target department is currently a top-level department (parent_id IS NULL) — only top-level departments can become child departments per the one-level nesting rule (Section 255)
  - The target department CAN have children of its own; the constraint only prevents a department that ALREADY has a parent from being assigned another parent

If parentId is being set to null (removing parent), this is always allowed — promotes to top-level. No further validation needed.

Update fields: name, description, parent_id. Set updated_at to current timestamp.

Return the updated full department record.

responseBody.description: The fully updated department record including all fields (id, organization_id, parent_id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at).

parameters.description: The UUID of the department to update (global scope).
parameters.name: departmentId

requestBody.description: Updated department fields: name (required, must be unique within the organization), description (optional free-text), and parentId (optional UUID of the parent department, set null to promote to top-level).

prerequisites.description: The department being updated (departmentId) must already exist in the system. Additionally, if a parentId is specified in the request body, the referenced parent department must also exist. Both are created via POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/departments prior to the update operation.

operations.description:
Soft-delete a department from the organization.

This operation soft-deletes the specified department by setting its `deleted_at` timestamp. The department record is not physically removed from the database to preserve audit trail integrity. When a department is deleted, all employees previously assigned to that department have their department reference set to null — employee records are preserved and remain active. If the deleted department has child departments, those child departments become top-level departments (their parent reference is cleared, promoting them).

Only the organization owner or users with organization management permission may delete a department. Department deletion has no effect on projects, tasks, timelogs, timesheets, or contracts belonging to affected employees.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement as a soft-delete operation within a database transaction.

1. **Lookup and validate**: Find the department by UUID primary key. Verify it exists and `deleted_at IS NULL` (not already deleted).
2. **Authorization**: Verify the authenticated user has organization management permission for the department's organization. Only organization owner or users with appropriate role permissions can delete departments.
3. **Transaction**: Execute all updates in a single database transaction:
   - Set `deleted_at` to the current timestamp on the department record.
   - Update all employees referencing this department: set `hrm_time_tracking_department_id = NULL` where `hrm_time_tracking_department_id = {departmentId}`.
   - Update all child departments: set `parent_id = NULL` where `parent_id = {departmentId}`, promoting them to top-level.
4. **Response**: Return the soft-deleted department entity with `deleted_at` populated.

**Edge cases**:
- Department already deleted (`deleted_at` not null) → return 404 Not Found.
- User lacks permission → return 403 Forbidden.
- Department not found → return 404 Not Found.
- No employees assigned → employee update step affects zero rows; operation succeeds.
- Department has no children → parent update step affects zero rows; operation succeeds.

parameters.description: The universally unique identifier (UUID) of the department to delete. This is the department's primary key, globally unique across all organizations.
parameters.name: departmentId

prerequisites.description: The department must exist in the system before it can be deleted. POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/departments creates the department entity that DELETE /hrmTimeTracking/member/departments/{departmentId} later removes.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable history of department snapshots for a specific department.

Each department snapshot is an immutable point-in-time record that captures the complete state of a department (its name, description, and parent department relationship) at the moment a change occurred. Snapshots are automatically generated by the system whenever a department is created, updated, or soft-deleted, providing a comprehensive audit trail of all department modifications over time.

This endpoint supports filtering by the type of change that triggered the snapshot (creation, modification, or deletion), by date range to narrow results to a specific period, and by the actor who performed the change. Results are sorted by timestamp with the most recent changes first by default, and support cursor-based pagination for efficient browsing of large histories.

Department snapshots are read-only records and cannot be created, modified, or deleted through the API. Access is available to all employees within the organization that owns the department.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query hrm_time_tracking_department_snapshots filtered by hrm_time_tracking_department_id matching the {departmentId} path parameter. Support pagination with page number and limit. Support filtering by: change_type (enum: 'created', 'updated', 'deleted'), date range on created_at (from/to), actor_member_id. Support sorting by created_at ascending or descending (default descending, most recent first). Join with hrm_time_tracking_members to resolve actor_member_id to member name/email for display purposes. Return paginated results with total count metadata. Consider that snapshots can be numerous for frequently-modified departments, so cursor-based pagination may be beneficial for large datasets. No write operations allowed — this is a read-only endpoint.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of department snapshot summary records, each containing the department state at a point in time (name, description, parent department), the change type that triggered the snapshot, the actor who performed the change, and the timestamp when the snapshot was recorded.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the department whose snapshot history is being retrieved. All returned snapshots will belong to this department.
parameters.name: departmentId

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and pagination criteria for browsing department snapshot history. Supports filtering by change type (created, updated, deleted), date range on the snapshot creation timestamp, and the actor who performed the change. Includes pagination parameters (page, limit) and sorting options.

prerequisites.description: The department must exist before its snapshot history can be queried, since snapshots are automatically generated by the system when the department is created, updated, or deleted. Without a department, no snapshots exist to retrieve.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific department snapshot by its ID.

A department snapshot is an immutable point-in-time record that captures the complete state of a department (name, description, parent department) at the moment a create, update, or delete event occurred. Snapshots preserve historical department data even after the department is subsequently modified or removed, providing a full audit trail of all department changes.

The response includes the department snapshot fields such as name, description, parent department ID, change type (created/updated/deleted), and the timestamp when the snapshot was recorded. Use this endpoint to inspect historical department states or to audit organizational changes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query hrm_time_tracking_department_snapshots table by the snapshotId (id field). Verify that the snapshot belongs to the specified department by checking that hrm_time_tracking_department_id matches the departmentId path parameter. Ensure organization-scoped access by verifying the snapshot's hrm_time_tracking_organization_id is within the authenticated member's organization. Return 404 Not Found if no snapshot matches both parameters or if the snapshot belongs to a different organization. The snapshot record is immutable — no update logic required.

responseBody.description: The complete department snapshot record including the name, description, parent department ID, change type, actor member ID, and creation timestamp as they existed at the time of the snapshot.

parameters.description: The UUID of the department whose snapshot is being retrieved (scoped to organization).
parameters.name: departmentId

parameters.description: The UUID of the snapshot record to retrieve (global scope).
parameters.name: snapshotId

prerequisites.description: The department must exist before its snapshot can be retrieved. Department snapshots are automatically created by the system as a side effect when a department is created, updated, or deleted. POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/departments creates the department that the snapshot belongs to.

operations.description:
Search and list roles within a specific organization with paginated results.

This endpoint returns a paginated list of role records belonging to the specified organization. Each role is a named permission set — either a system-protected built-in role (Owner, Manager, Employee) or a user-created custom role with configurable permissions. Built-in roles are seeded automatically at organization creation and cannot be deleted; custom roles are managed by organization owners.

Results can be filtered by role name (partial match) and role type (built_in or custom). The response includes role metadata such as name, type, creation and update timestamps, and the number of employees currently assigned to each role. Results are scoped to the organization identified by the path parameter, enforcing strict multi-tenant data isolation — roles from other organizations are never visible.

operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_roles table filtered by hrm_time_tracking_organization_id matching the organizationId path parameter. Apply multi-tenant isolation — never return roles from other organizations.

Apply optional search filters from request body:
- name: partial/fuzzy match against the role name column
- type: exact match filter ('built_in' or 'custom')
- Include pagination (page, limit) and sorting (by name, created_at, type)

Join with hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions and hrm_time_tracking_employees to compute the employee count for each role. Return only roles where deleted_at IS NULL (active roles).

Built-in roles (type='built_in') should always be returned in search results as they are immutable and always active. Custom roles with deleted_at set should not appear in results.

Response uses cursor-based or offset pagination. Include total count metadata in the response for UI pagination controls.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single role by its unique identifier within a specific organization.

Each role belongs to exactly one organization and represents a named permission set (either one of the three immutable built-in roles — Owner, Manager, Employee — or a user-created custom role). The response includes the role's metadata (name, type classification) along with all assigned permission codes through the associated hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions junction records.

Multi-tenant data isolation is enforced at the path level via the organizationId parameter — only roles belonging to the specified organization are accessible. Soft-deleted custom roles are excluded from results. If the requested role does not exist, has been soft-deleted, or belongs to a different organization, a 404 Not Found error is returned.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_roles table filtering by id (roleId) AND hrm_time_tracking_organization_id (organizationId).

- Exclude soft-deleted records: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
- Include associated permissions via LEFT JOIN on hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions (filter out soft-deleted permission records where deleted_at IS NULL)
- Return 404 NotFound if no matching role is found
- The organizationId parameter inherently enforces multi-tenant isolation
- No special handling needed for built-in roles vs custom roles — both are returned identically when queried
- Edge case: if organizationId does not match any hrm_time_tracking_organization_id associated with the given roleId, treat as 404 (the role doesn't exist in this organization context)

responseBody.description: The full role entity including its name, type classification (built_in or custom), and associated permission codes. Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) are always returned when queried. Soft-deleted custom roles (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are excluded from results. The response includes nested permission records showing each assigned permission code.
