The role must exist before it can be retrieved. Roles are either built-in (seeded at organization creation) or custom (created via this POST operation). Custom roles require explicit creation, and built-in roles are only available after organization creation. This POST ensures the target role record exists in the database for the GET operation to return.

operations.description:
Create a new custom role within an organization.

The Organization Owner can define custom permission sets beyond the three built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee). Each custom role requires a unique name within the organization and a selection of permissions from the available system permissions.

Available permissions include: org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, and report:view. The selected permissions determine what employees assigned to this role can do within the organization.

Role names must be unique within the organization to prevent ambiguity. Built-in role names ('Owner', 'Manager', 'Employee') are reserved and cannot be used for custom roles.

Upon creation, the role type is automatically set to 'custom'. Associated permission mappings are created via the role_permissions junction table. The created role is immediately available for employee assignment.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a record into hrm_time_tracking_roles with:
- hrm_time_tracking_organization_id: from path parameter organizationId
- name: from request body (validate uniqueness within organization before insert)
- type: set to 'custom'
- created_at, updated_at: current timestamp

Validate that the organization exists and is active. Validate that no role with the same name already exists within this organization (composite unique constraint on [organization_id, name]). Validate that name is not one of the reserved built-in role names ('Owner', 'Manager', 'Employee').

For each permission_code in request body permissions array, insert a record into hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions with:
- hrm_time_tracking_role_id: the newly created role's id
- permission_code: from the request
- created_at, updated_at: current timestamp

Validate each permission_code is one of the 9 valid system permissions. Wrap role creation and permission inserts in a transaction. Return the created role with its associated permissions. On duplicate name, return a conflict error. On invalid permission code, return a validation error.

responseBody.description: The newly created custom role with its assigned permissions, including system-generated fields such as id, type (set to 'custom'), created_at, and updated_at.

parameters.description: UUID of the organization where the custom role will be created. The organization must be active.
parameters.name: organizationId

requestBody.description: Required role name and set of permissions to assign to the new custom role. The name must be unique within the organization and not conflict with built-in role names. Permissions must be a non-empty array of valid system permission codes.

prerequisites.description: The organization must exist and be active before a custom role can be created within it. The role references the organization via its organizationId foreign key (hrm_time_tracking_roles.hrm_time_tracking_organization_id) and the system validates organization existence and 'active' status at creation time.

operations.description:
Updates an existing role within a specific organization. This operation allows organization owners or users with org:manage permission to modify custom role details, including renaming the role and adjusting its permission set.

Custom roles can have their name changed to any unique name within the organization. Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) cannot be renamed under any circumstances — attempting to change a built-in role's name will result in an error.

The permission set is updated by providing the full list of permission codes to assign to the role. This replaces the existing permission set entirely. Built-in roles (Manager, Employee) have predefined permission sets and changes to their permissions are restricted. The Owner role always holds all permissions and cannot be modified.

This operation requires that the caller has the org:manage permission within the organization. Cross-organization role updates are not permitted — the role must belong to the same organization identified in the path.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate that the role exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null) within the specified organization. Verify that the organizationId in the path matches the role's hrm_time_tracking_organization_id — return a 404 Not Found if the role doesn't belong to the organization.

Check the caller's permissions — only users with org:manage permission (Owner role) can update roles.

If the role type is 'built_in':
- Reject any attempt to change the name field with a 422 Unprocessable Entity error explaining that built-in roles cannot be renamed.
- For the Owner role, reject any permission changes as the Owner always holds all permissions.
- For Manager and Employee built-in roles, permission changes may be restricted per business rules.

If the role type is 'custom':
- Validate the new name is unique within the organization (query for existing roles with the same name but different ID).
- Update the role name in hrm_time_tracking_roles.
- Replace permission assignments: delete all existing entries in hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions for this role, then insert new entries for each permissionCode in the request.

Return the updated role with its current permission set. Use a database transaction to ensure atomicity of the name update and permission replacement.

responseBody.description: The updated role record including its metadata and associated permission assignments after the update has been applied.

parameters.description: UUID of the organization that owns the role. Used to scope the operation within a specific tenant for multi-tenant data isolation.
parameters.name: organizationId

parameters.description: UUID of the role to update. The role must belong to the organization specified by organizationId.
parameters.name: roleId

requestBody.description: Updated role data including an optional new name (for custom roles only) and the complete list of permission codes to assign to the role. The permissionCodes array replaces the existing permission set entirely.

operations.description:
Soft-deletes a custom role within an organization.

This operation permanently removes a custom role by setting its deleted_at timestamp, making it inactive and unavailable for future employee assignments. Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) are system-protected and cannot be deleted under any circumstances. Only custom roles with no active employees currently assigned may be deleted.

When a role is deleted, all its associated permission mappings in hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions are automatically cascade-deleted by the database constraint, preserving referential integrity. Historical employee records and activity log entries that reference this role are preserved through the soft-delete mechanism.

**Role Isolation**: Each organization operates with its own independent role set. The role must belong to the organization identified by {organizationId}. Roles from one organization are never visible or applicable to any other organization.

**Permissions**: Requires the `org:manage` permission within the organization.

**Error Handling**: Returns 404 if the role or organization is not found. Returns 403 if attempting to delete a built-in role. Returns 409 if the custom role still has active employee assignments.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Look up the role by roleId. Verify it exists and that hrm_time_tracking_organization_id matches organizationId. Return 404 if not found.
2. Check the role's `type` field.
   - If `built_in`: reject with 403 Forbidden — built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) are system-protected and cannot be deleted.
3. For custom roles: query hrm_time_tracking_employees to check if any active employees (deleted_at IS NULL) have hrm_time_tracking_role_id = this roleId. If ≥1 active employee exists, reject with 409 Conflict.
4. Perform soft-delete: SET deleted_at = NOW() on the role record.
5. Cascade deletion of associated hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions entries is automatic via FK constraint (onDelete: Cascade) — no manual cleanup needed.
6. Return the updated IHrmTimeTrackingRole entity with deleted_at now populated.

parameters.description: The UUID of the organization that owns the role (scoped within multi-tenant boundary).
parameters.name: organizationId

parameters.description: The UUID of the role to soft-delete (scoped to the specified organization).
parameters.name: roleId

prerequisites.description: The organization must exist before any role can be created or deleted within it. The role record references the organization via the hrm_time_tracking_organization_id foreign key.
The role must be created before it can be soft-deleted. The erase operation looks up the role by roleId and performs a soft-delete, which requires the role record to exist in the database.

operations.description:
Replaces the entire permission set assigned to a role within an organization.

This endpoint performs a full, atomic replacement of the role's permission set. The caller provides an array of permission codes, and the system deletes all existing role-permission mappings for the role, then inserts new mappings for each provided code. The operation is idempotent — invoking it multiple times with the same input yields the same result.

Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) have fixed, immutable permission sets that are seeded at organization creation. Any attempt to modify a built-in role's permissions is rejected with a 403 Forbidden response. Only custom roles support configurable permission sets.

The 9 available system permission codes are: org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, report:view. An empty array is permitted, creating a role with zero functional permissions — this is an explicit business requirement.

Each organization maintains its own independent set of roles and permissions. Roles and permissions from one organization are neither visible nor applicable to any other organization.

**Authorization** — Requires the org:manage permission within the target organization. Only the organization owner or users with org:manage permission can modify role permissions.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Replace all role-permission mappings for the given role within a single database transaction:

1. **Validate organization existence** — Look up the organization by organizationId. Return 404 if not found or if status is 'deleted'.

2. **Validate role existence and ownership** — Look up the role by roleId, verify it belongs to the specified organization (hrm_time_tracking_organization_id matches organizationId). Return 404 if not found or if deleted_at is not null (soft-deleted roles are considered deleted).

3. **Validate role type** — If role.type === 'built_in', return 403 Forbidden. Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) have fixed, non-modifiable permission sets.

4. **Validate permission codes** — Each code in the request body must be one of the 9 fixed values. Reject invalid codes with 400 Bad Request and a descriptive message identifying the invalid code.

5. **Deduplicate and replace atomically** — Remove duplicate codes from the input. Within a Prisma transaction: (a) Delete all existing hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions rows where hrm_time_tracking_role_id = roleId. (b) Insert new rows for each unique permission code. Each row gets a new UUID id, current timestamp for created_at and updated_at, and null for deleted_at. Allow empty array (role with zero permissions).

6. **Return updated role** — Return the role entity with its current set of permission codes. Fetch the role by ID, joining hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions where deleted_at IS NULL, and return the role with id, name, type, and the array of permission codes.

7. **Edge case — soft-deleted role** — If role.deleted_at is not null, treat as 404 (soft-deleted roles cannot be modified).

8. **Edge case — multiple calls** — The operation is idempotent; calling it twice with the same codes produces identical results.

responseBody.description: The role record including its updated set of permission codes after the replacement operation completes.

An empty array clears all permissions from the role, which is explicitly allowed by the system.

operations.description:
Assign a permission code to a role within an organization.

This operation creates a new permission assignment by linking one of the nine fixed system permission codes to the specified role. Permission codes include: org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, and report:view. Each assignment is scoped to a specific role within an organization, enforcing multi-tenant data isolation.

Only custom roles can receive new permission assignments via this operation. Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) have fixed, immutable permission sets that are seeded automatically at organization creation time and cannot be modified. If a permission code is already assigned to the role (including soft-deleted records), the system will either reject the duplicate or restore the previously deleted assignment.

The operation requires the caller to hold the org:manage permission within the organization. System-generated fields including the record ID, creation timestamp, and update timestamp are set automatically by the server and should not be provided in the request body.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Verify the caller holds org:manage permission within the organization identified by organizationId.
2. Verify the role identified by roleId exists and belongs to the given organizationId — if not found or organization mismatch, return 404 Not Found.
3. Verify the role type is 'custom' — if the role type is 'built_in', return 403 Forbidden as built-in roles have immutable permission sets.
4. Validate permission_code from the request body is one of the 9 valid values: org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, report:view — if invalid, return 400 Bad Request.
5. Check for existing assignment: query hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions where hrm_time_tracking_role_id = roleId AND permission_code = provided value.
   - If a non-deleted row exists (deleted_at IS NULL), return 409 Conflict — permission already assigned.
   - If a soft-deleted row exists (deleted_at IS NOT NULL), restore it by setting deleted_at = NULL and updated_at = now, then return the restored record with 200 OK.
6. If no existing row, create a new record with auto-generated UUID for id, hrm_time_tracking_role_id from path, permission_code from request body, and auto-set created_at and updated_at.
7. Return 201 Created with the full IHrmTimeTrackingRolePermission entity.

operations.description:
Remove a permission mapping from a role within an organization.

This operation removes a single permission assignment from a role's permission set by soft-deleting the role-permission mapping record. When a permission is removed, employees assigned to this role lose the corresponding capability immediately.

Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) have fixed, immutable permission sets — removing permissions from these roles is blocked by the system. This operation is only applicable to custom roles whose permission sets are configurable by organization owners. Custom roles can only have their permission sets modified if the organization owner holds the org:manage permission.

The permission must be currently assigned to the role. Removing a permission that has already been removed (or was never assigned) results in a not-found error. The removal is permanent — once deleted, the permission mapping cannot be restored.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Validate that the role exists and belongs to the specified organization. Check that the role is of type 'custom' — built-in roles (type: 'built_in') have immutable permission sets and the operation MUST be rejected with a business rule violation error.

Verify the permission mapping exists: query hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions where id = {permissionId} AND hrm_time_tracking_role_id = {roleId} AND deleted_at IS NULL. Return 404 if not found.

Perform soft delete by setting deleted_at to the current timestamp. Do NOT hard-delete the record — the deleted_at column preserves referential integrity with historical data.

Authorization: Only users with org:manage permission (or organization owner) may remove permissions from roles. The requesting user must belong to the same organization.

No response body on success (204 No Content) is acceptable, but return the deleted IHrmTimeTrackingRolePermission if the API consumer needs confirmation of what was deleted.

Edge cases: If the role itself is soft-deleted (deleted_at set), return 404 since the role is considered inactive. If the last permission is removed from a custom role, the role still exists but has an empty permission set — employees assigned to it will have no capabilities.

operations.description:
Search and list employees within the organization with pagination and filtering.

This endpoint returns a paginated list of employee records matching the specified search criteria. Each employee record includes their display name (from the associated user account), role name, department name (if assigned), position, employment type classification (full-time, part-time, contractor, intern), and current status (active or deactivated).

The list supports filtering by department, employment type, and employee status, as well as search by employee display name. Filters can be combined — for example, showing only active employees in a specific department. The response is paginated for efficient browsing of large organizations.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_tracking_employees table scoped to the current organization (from auth context).

Join with:
- hrm_time_tracking_members for the employee's display name (via hrm_time_tracking_member_id)
- hrm_time_tracking_roles for the role name (via hrm_time_tracking_role_id)
- hrm_time_tracking_departments for the department name (via hrm_time_tracking_department_id)

Support filters:
- departmentId: filter by hrm_time_tracking_department_id (optional UUID)
- employmentType: filter by employment_type field (optional, values: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern)
- status: filter by status field (optional, values: active, deactivated)
- search text: search by member's display_name (case-insensitive LIKE or ILIKE)

Support combined filters (e.g., active employees in a specific department).
Support pagination with page and limit parameters.
Sort by created_at descending by default.
Exclude soft-deleted employees (deleted_at IS NULL) from results.

Return IPageIHrmTimeTrackingEmployee.ISummary with employee summary data.

Retrieves a single employee record by its unique identifier.

The response includes the employee's complete profile information: their display name, email, and avatar from their global user account, their assigned role with permissions, their optional department assignment, employment type classification, current status (active or deactivated), and position title.

This operation requires the 'employee:view' permission within the organization context. The returned data is scoped to the requesting user's active organization — employees from other organizations are not accessible.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_employees table by id (UUID).

Authorization: Verify the requesting user has 'employee:view' permission within their active organization context. Reject with 403 Forbidden if permission is missing.

Organization scoping: The employee must belong to the same organization as the requesting user's active organization context (hrm_time_tracking_organization_id). This ensures multi-tenant data isolation.

Joins required:
1. INNER JOIN hrm_time_tracking_members ON employees.hrm_time_tracking_member_id = members.id — to include user profile data (display_name, email, avatar, phone_number)
2. INNER JOIN hrm_time_tracking_roles ON employees.hrm_time_tracking_role_id = roles.id — to include role name
3. LEFT JOIN hrm_time_tracking_departments ON employees.hrm_time_tracking_department_id = departments.id — to include department name (may be null)

Include employees with any status (active or deactivated). Do not filter by deleted_at — soft-deleted employees are accessible for viewing.

Edge cases:
- If no employee found with the given id within the organization, return 404 Not Found
- If the employee's department was soft-deleted, return null for department info (department reference is already set to null on employee when department is deleted)

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of employment contracts for a specific employee.

This endpoint returns the employee's compensation history, including current and past contracts. Each contract record displays the pay rate, pay period type, working hours per week, start and end dates, and any notes. The list is ordered by start date descending by default, showing the most recent contract first.

Access control: The employee can view their own contracts. Users with the employee:view permission within the same organization can view any employee's contracts. Requests from unauthorized users are rejected.

Filtering is available by contract status (active contracts where end_date is null, or past contracts with a set end date), pay period type, and date ranges. Results are paginated with configurable page size and sorting options.

Query hrm_time_tracking_employee_contracts joined with hrm_time_tracking_employees (for organization scope and authorization).

Authorization: Verify the authenticated member's employee record exists in the same organization as the target employee. Allow access if the authenticated member is the same as the target employee OR has the employee:view permission.

Default filtering: Exclude soft-deleted contracts (deleted_at IS NULL).

Request body fields for filtering:
- status: 'active' (end_date IS NULL) or 'past' (end_date IS NOT NULL)
- pay_period: filter by pay period type (hourly, daily, weekly, monthly)
- start_date_range: filter contracts starting within a date range
- end_date_range: filter contracts ending within a date range

Sort by start_date descending (most recent first) by default. Support cursor or offset-based pagination.

Return paginated results with contract summary fields: id, start_date, end_date, pay_rate, pay_period, working_hours_per_week, notes, created_at.

Employees can view their own contracts to review current and past compensation details. Users with the employee:view permission can view any employee's contracts within the organization for compensation reviews, budget planning, and employment verification.

Resolve the organization from the employee record (hrm_time_tracking_organization_id).

Return 403 if the requesting user lacks authorization. responseBody.description: The full employment contract record containing compensation details including pay rate, pay period, working hours, contract dates, and optional notes.

parameters.description: UUID of the employee who owns the contract (global scope).
parameters.name: employeeId

parameters.description: UUID of the contract to retrieve (global scope).
parameters.name: contractId

prerequisites.description: The specific contract must exist in the system before it can be retrieved. This POST operation creates the contract with its compensation terms (pay rate, pay period, working hours, contract dates, notes) under the specified employee, making it available for subsequent retrieval via GET.

operations.description:
Creates a new employment contract for the specified employee.

This operation records a new contract documenting the employee's compensation terms, including pay rate, pay period, working hours per week, contract duration, and optional notes. The contract becomes effective on the specified start date.

When a new contract is created and the employee already has an active contract (end_date IS NULL), the system automatically ends the previous active contract by setting its end_date to one day before the new contract's start_date, ensuring a gapless compensation history. Only one active contract per employee is permitted at any time.

Active contracts (end_date IS NULL) remain editable. Past contracts (end_date IS NOT NULL) become immutable historical records.

Access control: This operation requires the employee:manage permission within the organization.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new contract record in hrm_time_tracking_employee_contracts for the employee identified by {employeeId}.

1. Validate that the employee exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL).
2. Verify the requesting user has employee:manage permission within the employee's organization.
3. Check that no existing contract has the same (hrm_time_tracking_employee_id, start_date) combination (enforced by @@unique constraint).
4. If the employee has an active contract (end_date IS NULL), automatically set its end_date to one day before the new contract's start_date (start_date - 1 day). Update the previous contract's updated_at timestamp.
5. Create the new contract with:
   - hrm_time_tracking_employee_id = {employeeId}
   - start_date from request body
   - end_date from request body (nullable)
   - pay_rate from request body
   - pay_period from request body (validate against enum: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly)
   - working_hours_per_week from request body
   - notes from request body (nullable)
   - id = auto-generated UUID
   - created_at = current timestamp
   - updated_at = current timestamp
   - deleted_at = null
6. Return the created contract with all fields.

responseBody.description: The newly created employment contract with all computed fields including the system-generated ID, timestamps, and the automatically calculated end_date of the previous active contract if one was ended.

parameters.description: The UUID of the employee for whom the contract is being created. This employee must belong to the requester's organization and must not be deactivated.
parameters.name: employeeId

requestBody.description: Contract creation payload containing compensation terms including pay rate, pay period type (hourly, daily, weekly, monthly), working hours per week, start date, optional end date for fixed-term contracts, and optional notes.

prerequisites.description: The employee must first exist in the organization before a contract can be created for them. The invitation operation creates an active employee record (either by auto-adding an existing member or by creating a pending invitation that becomes an employee upon acceptance), establishing the required Employee entity that the contract's employeeId path parameter references.

operations.description:
Update an active employee contract's compensation terms.

This operation modifies the terms of an employment contract that is currently active (has no end date). Authorized users can update the pay rate, pay period, working hours per week, end date, and notes. Past contracts that have already ended are immutable and cannot be modified.

Only users with the employee:manage permission within the organization can perform this operation. The contract must belong to the specified employee — the employeeId path parameter ensures proper organizational scoping. When the end_date is set on an active contract, the contract becomes a past contract and can no longer be updated. The system automatically updates the updated_at timestamp on successful modification.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate the contract exists and belongs to the specified employee (hrm_time_tracking_employee_id matches employeeId).
2. Validate the contract is active: end_date IS NULL. If end_date IS NOT NULL, reject with 422 and a message indicating past contracts are immutable.
3. Validate that the requesting user has employee:manage permission within the organization.
4. Update allowed mutable fields from request body: pay_rate, pay_period, working_hours_per_week, end_date, notes.
5. Validate pay_period value is one of: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly.
6. Validate pay_rate > 0 and working_hours_per_week > 0.
7. If end_date is being set, validate it is not before start_date.
8. Set updated_at to current timestamp.
9. Return the full updated contract record as the response.

responseBody.description: The full updated employee contract record with all fields including system-managed timestamps.

parameters.description: UUID of the employee who owns the contract (scoped to organization).
parameters.name: employeeId

parameters.description: UUID of the contract to update.
parameters.name: contractId

requestBody.description: Updated compensation terms for the active contract. Only active contracts (end_date is null) can be modified.

prerequisites.description: The contract must be created first via the createContract operation. The update operation modifies an existing contract that is active (end_date IS NULL), and the contract must already exist in the database with a specific contractId. The POST operation creates this contract record, establishing the compensation terms that the PUT operation subsequently modifies.

operations.description:
Soft-delete an employee contract, marking it as deleted while retaining the record for historical and audit purposes.

The contract is retained in the database with its deleted_at timestamp set, excluding it from standard active listings and queries. Both active contracts (with null end_date) and past contracts (with an end_date set) can be soft-deleted. This operation does not affect the employee's other contracts, pay history, timelogs, timesheets, or any related data.

Once soft-deleted, the contract can no longer be retrieved through standard queries. It remains accessible only for audit and historical record-keeping. If the contract was the employee's active contract, the employee will have no active contract after this operation.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Soft-delete a contract by setting its deleted_at column to the current server timestamp.

Validation steps:
1. Verify the contract exists by contractId. If not found, return 404 Not Found.
2. Verify the contract belongs to the specified employee (hrm_time_tracking_employee_id matches employeeId). If not, return 404 Not Found (do not reveal whether the contract exists but belongs to a different employee).
3. Verify the employee belongs to the caller's organization (authorization handled by auth middleware).
4. Check if the contract is already soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL). If already deleted, the operation is idempotent — return the already-deleted contract or a 404 since the resource is no longer accessible.
5. Set deleted_at to the current timestamp.
6. Update the updated_at timestamp as well.
7. Return the updated IHrmTimeTrackingEmployeeContract with deleted_at populated.

Business rules:
- Past contracts (end_date IS NOT NULL) are immutable for edits but CAN be soft-deleted.
- Active contracts (end_date IS NULL) can be soft-deleted. After deletion, the employee will have no active contract.
- This operation does NOT cascade to any other records.
- Soft-deleted contracts are excluded from list queries (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL).

parameters.description: UUID of the employee who owns the contract. The contract must belong to this employee.
parameters.name: employeeId

parameters.description: UUID of the contract to soft-delete. Must belong to the specified employee.
parameters.name: contractId

prerequisites.description: The contract must be created before it can be soft-deleted. POST /hrmTimeTracking/employees/{employeeId}/contracts creates a new contract and returns the contractId that is then used in this DELETE operation to identify which contract to soft-delete.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of historical snapshots for a specific employee.

Employee snapshots are immutable point-in-time records automatically generated by the system whenever significant changes are made to an employee record. Each snapshot captures the employee's full state at the moment of change, including the field that was modified and the before/after values. Snapshots are created automatically on events such as status transitions (active ↔ deactivated), role reassignments, employment type changes, position updates, and department reassignments.

Results can be filtered by the type of field that was changed (changed_field) and by a date range on the snapshot creation timestamp (created_at). Results are sorted by creation date in descending order by default, showing the most recent changes first. This endpoint requires the employee:view permission.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query the hrm_time_tracking_employee_snapshots table filtered by hrm_time_tracking_employee_id matching the {employeeId} path parameter. Apply permission checks: verify the requesting member belongs to the same organization as the employee identified by {employeeId}. Require employee:view permission. Support filtering by changed_field (exact match on string enum values: status, role_id, employment_type, department_id, position). Support date range filtering on created_at with from and to timestamps. Support pagination with page/limit/sort parameters. Default sort by created_at descending (most recent first). Join with hrm_time_tracking_members table to include the actor's display name in each snapshot record. Join with hrm_time_tracking_roles and hrm_time_tracking_departments tables to include denormalized role and department names from the snapshot's foreign keys.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of employee snapshot summary records optimized for audit trail viewing. Each summary includes the snapshot id, changed field name, old and new values, creation timestamp, and actor information.

parameters.description: The UUID of the employee whose historical snapshots to retrieve. (global scope)
parameters.name: employeeId

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering employee snapshots. Supports filtering by changed_field, date range on created_at, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific employee snapshot record from the audit trail.

Employee snapshots capture point-in-time states of employee records whenever significant changes occur — status transitions (active ↔ deactivated), role re-assignments, department changes, employment type updates, or position modifications. Each snapshot includes the full employee state at the moment of change (status, employment type, position) along with foreign key references to the role and department assignments at that time, plus change metadata identifying what was modified and the before/after values.

This operation requires the `employee:view` permission within the organization context to access snapshot history.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_tracking_employee_snapshots table filtering by both hrm_time_tracking_employee_id (matching employeeId parameter) and id (matching snapshotId parameter).

Join with hrm_time_tracking_members to include the actor's display name who performed the change.
Join with hrm_time_tracking_roles to include the role name at the time of snapshot.
Optionally join with hrm_time_tracking_departments for the department name (may be null).

Verify the requesting user has access to the organization of the employee. If the user does not have the employee:view permission, deny access. If the snapshot or employee is not found, return 404 Not Found. If the snapshot does not belong to the specified employee (hrm_time_tracking_employee_id mismatch), return 404 Not Found.

responseBody.description: The full employee snapshot record including the captured employee state, change metadata, and timestamp.

parameters.description: UUID of the employee whose snapshot record to retrieve.
parameters.name: employeeId

parameters.description: UUID of the specific employee snapshot to retrieve.
parameters.name: snapshotId

operations.description:
Creates a manual point-in-time snapshot of an employee's current record state.

This operation allows authorized users to record a checkpoint capturing the employee's current status, employment type, position, role, and department assignments at a specific moment. The user provides metadata describing what changed (changed field and optional before/after values), while the system automatically captures the employee's full current state.

Use cases include documenting a notable change, creating an audit checkpoint before a modification, or recording compliance-related observations. The snapshot preserves the employee's state at the time of creation, providing an immutable record for historical review.

Requires `employee:manage` permission. The requesting user is recorded as the actor who created the snapshot.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Verify the authenticated user has `employee:manage` permission within the current organization context.
2. Verify the employee identified by {employeeId} exists, belongs to the current organization, and is not deleted.
3. Read the employee's current state: status, employment_type, position, hrm_time_tracking_role_id (current role), hrm_time_tracking_department_id (current department, may be null).
4. Validate the request body: changed_field is required (string), old_value is optional (string|null), new_value is optional (string|null).
5. Create the snapshot record with:
   - hrm_time_tracking_employee_id = employeeId (from path)
   - hrm_time_tracking_member_id = authenticated user's member ID
   - hrm_time_tracking_role_id = employee's current role ID
   - hrm_time_tracking_department_id = employee's current department ID (null if unassigned)
   - status = employee's current status
   - employment_type = employee's current employment type
   - position = employee's current position (null if unset)
   - changed_field = provided value
   - old_value = provided value (may be null)
   - new_value = provided value (may be null)
6. Return the created snapshot with all fields populated.
7. On validation failure (employee not found, no permission), return appropriate 404 or 403 errors.

responseBody.description: The created employee snapshot record, including the employee's captured state at the time of creation, the change metadata, the actor who created it, and the timestamp.

parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the employee to create a snapshot for. The snapshot captures this employee's current record state at the time of creation.
parameters.name: employeeId

requestBody.description: Change metadata describing the reason for this manual checkpoint snapshot. The user provides which field changed and optional before/after values. The employee's current state (status, employment_type, position, role, department) is captured automatically by the system.

operations.description:
Search and list projects within the current organization.

This endpoint returns a paginated, filterable list of projects for the authenticated user's active organization context. It is designed for project management interfaces, project selector dropdowns, and dashboard widgets that need to display project summaries.

Supports filtering by project name (partial match), lifecycle status (active, archived, completed), date ranges on start and end dates, and budget hour ranges. Results are sorted by creation date by default (newest first) with configurable sorting options. Soft-deleted projects are excluded from results.

Each project summary includes the project's identity attributes (name, color code), lifecycle status, and planning attributes (budget hours, start/end dates) for efficient list rendering without loading full project details.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_projects table scoped to the authenticated user's current organization (hrm_time_tracking_organization_id from session context).

Apply search and filter criteria from the request body:
- name: partial match search on the project name field (case-insensitive LIKE/ILIKE)
- status: filter by project lifecycle status (active, archived, completed) — may be a single value or array to allow multi-status filtering
- startedAtRange: date range filter on started_at (gte/lte)
- endedAtRange: date range filter on ended_at (gte/lte)
- budgetHoursRange: numeric range filter on budget_hours (gte/lte)
- colorCode: exact match filter on color_code

Exclude soft-deleted records (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL).

Support pagination via page/limit parameters in the request body. Default sorting by created_at descending. Support sortable fields: name, status, created_at, started_at, ended_at, budget_hours.

Include total count for pagination metadata. Return summary fields only (id, name, status, color_code, budget_hours, started_at, ended_at, createdAt) — exclude full description for listing performance.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of project summary records containing identity attributes, status, and planning metadata for efficient UI rendering in lists, dropdowns, and dashboards.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering and paginating projects within the organization. Supports partial name search, status filtering, date range filters on planning dates, budget hour range, sorting, and cursor/offset-based pagination.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single project by its unique identifier.

Returns the full project record including name, description, color code, current status, optional budget hours, and optional start/end dates. The project status indicates the current lifecycle stage: 'active' (accepting new timelogs and tasks), 'archived' (data preserved but no new entries), or 'completed' (finished state with data preserved for historical reference).

The response includes the organization ID for context, but the operation automatically scopes to the authenticated user's organization.

Soft-deleted projects are excluded from this endpoint and return a not-found response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_projects by primary key id matching {projectId}.

1. Scoped to the authenticated user's selected organization — hrm_time_tracking_organization_id must match the user's current organization context.
2. Respect soft deletion: if deleted_at is non-null, treat as not found (return 404 or equivalent).
3. Return the complete project record including: id, organization_id, name, description, color_code, status, budget_hours, started_at, ended_at, created_at, updated_at.
4. The status field contains one of: 'active', 'archived', 'completed'.
5. No JOINs needed for the base response — this returns the raw project entity.

responseBody.description: The full project entity with all fields including name, description, color code, status, budget hours, date range, and timestamps.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the project to retrieve.
parameters.name: projectId

prerequisites.description: A project must first be created via POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/projects before it can be retrieved by its projectId. The POST response returns the project's UUID, which is then used as the {projectId} path parameter in the GET operation.

operations.description:
Creates a new project within the user's currently selected organization.

The project serves as a container for time tracking, task management, and reporting activities. When created, the project defaults to 'active' status, allowing employees assigned as project members to log time, create tasks, and manage project activities. Optional fields include a description for project scope, a budget_hours value for planned vs. actual hour comparisons, and start/end dates for timeline and scheduling views.

The authenticated user's current organization context determines which organization the project belongs to. The color_code (hex format, e.g., '#FF5733') enables visual differentiation in project selection dropdowns and timelog entry displays. System-generated fields such as id, created_at, updated_at, and status are populated automatically and returned in the response.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Query: Insert a new record into hrm_time_tracking_projects table with the provided fields.

Fields to include in insert:
- id: auto-generated UUID
- hrm_time_tracking_organization_id: derived from the authenticated user's current organization context (not from request body)
- name: required from request
- description: optional from request
- color_code: required from request (hex color string)
- status: defaults to 'active' (not accepted from request body)
- budget_hours: optional from request (double precision)
- started_at: optional from request
- ended_at: optional from request
- created_at: current timestamp
- updated_at: current timestamp
- deleted_at: null (not soft-deleted on creation)

Validation rules:
- Name must be a non-empty string
- Color_code must be a valid hex color code (e.g., '#FF5733')
- If provided, budget_hours must be a non-negative number
- If provided, started_at and ended_at must be valid ISO 8601 timestamps; ended_at must not be before started_at
- The organization must exist and be 'active'; if the organization is 'deleted', reject the creation

The created project record is returned as the response body with all populated fields.

responseBody.description: The newly created project record with all system-generated fields including id, status (defaulting to 'active'), created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at (null).

requestBody.description: Project creation payload with the new project's display name, hex color code for UI differentiation, optional description, optional budget hours for planning, and optional start/end dates for project timeline.

operations.description:
Update an existing project's attributes within the current organization context.

The authenticated member must hold the `project:manage` permission within the organization to perform this operation. Only projects belonging to the member's currently selected organization can be updated — cross-organization access is strictly prevented.

The following project attributes are editable: name, description, color code, status, budget hours, start date, and end date. Status transitions follow the project lifecycle flow: projects can be archived or completed from active status. Archived and completed projects cannot receive new timelogs but this endpoint only updates project metadata. Budget hours must be zero or a positive number. If both start and end dates are provided, the start date must be on or before the end date. The operation validates the target project exists and is not soft-deleted before applying changes.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_projects by id and verify the project belongs to the currently selected organization (hrm_time_tracking_organization_id from member's session context).

Verify the authenticated member has project:manage permission within the organization.

Check that the project is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL) — if deleted, return 404 Not Found. If no project exists with the given id, return 404 Not Found.

Validate the request body fields:
- name: required, non-empty string
- color_code: required, valid hex color string (e.g., '#FF5733')
- status: must be one of 'active', 'archived', 'completed'
- budget_hours: must be null or >= 0 (reject negative values)
- started_at / ended_at: if both provided, started_at must be <= ended_at
- description: optional, free-form text

Status transition rules:
- Active projects can transition to 'archived' or 'completed'
- Archived/completed projects can only update other non-status fields (status remains unchanged) — transitions back to 'active' from 'archived'/'completed' are not supported per lifecycle rules

Update the record with new values, set updated_at to current timestamp.

Return the complete updated project record including all fields.

Error cases:
- 403 Forbidden: member lacks project:manage permission
- 404 Not Found: project does not exist or is already deleted
- 422 Validation Error: invalid field values (bad status, negative budget, date conflict, missing required fields)

responseBody.description: The fully updated project record with all fields populated after the successful update operation.

parameters.description: UUID primary key of the project to update. Must correspond to an existing non-deleted project within the current organization context.
parameters.name: projectId

requestBody.description: Updated project attributes. Only editable fields are accepted — system-managed fields (id, organization_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are ignored or rejected.

prerequisites.description: The project must already exist before its attributes can be updated. POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/projects creates the project record that is then referenced by projectId in the update operation.

operations.description:
Soft-delete a project within the organization.

This operation removes a project from active use while preserving its historical data — including associated timelogs, tasks, timesheets, and project member records — for audit and reporting purposes. The project's `deleted_at` timestamp is set to the current time, marking it as inactive without permanent data loss.

Deletion is only permitted when the project has no timelogs associated with it. If any timelogs exist, the system rejects the deletion to protect logged time entries. Archived and completed projects can be deleted as long as they have no timelogs.

Only users with the `project:manage` permission can delete projects. Built-in roles with this permission include Owner and Manager; custom roles may also be granted this permission. When deletion succeeds, a project-deleted event is fired and delivered to all users with `project:view` permission or higher, as well as to all project members, notifying them that the project no longer exists.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Verify the authenticated user has `project:manage` permission within the current organization session. Look up the project by `projectId` where `hrm_time_tracking_organization_id` matches the current org — return 404 if not found or if `deleted_at` is already non-null (already deleted). Check for associated timelogs: query `hrm_time_tracking_timelogs` where `hrm_time_tracking_project_id` = project's id and `deleted_at` is null. If any timelogs exist, reject with 422 status explaining that projects with existing timelogs cannot be deleted. Perform soft deletion: set `deleted_at` to current timestamp and update `updated_at` accordingly. Fire a project-deleted real-time event with the project details for notification delivery to authorized users and project members. Return the soft-deleted project entity (with `deleted_at` populated) as confirmation.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the project to delete, scoped to the authenticated user's organization.
parameters.name: projectId

prerequisites.description: The project to be deleted must first exist. POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/projects creates the project and returns its id, which is then used as the {projectId} path parameter for the delete operation.

operations.description:
Search and list project members assigned to a specific project.

This operation returns a paginated list of employees who are members of the specified project. Each member record includes the employee's assigned role (member or project-lead) within the project context. Supports filtering by employee name and role type, as well as standard pagination and sorting.

Requires the `project:view` permission to access. Members can only view projects they are assigned to. Users with `project:manage` permission can view all project members within their organization. Results are scoped to the organization context of the authenticated member.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_project_members table filtered by hrm_time_tracking_project_id matching the projectId path parameter.

Join with hrm_time_tracking_employees and hrm_time_tracking_members to resolve employee display information (name, position, email). Exclude soft-deleted members (deleted_at IS NULL) by default unless the search request explicitly requests archived records.

Apply search filters:
- employeeName: partial match on employee name via member table
- role: exact match on 'member' or 'project-lead'
- includeDeleted: boolean flag to include soft-deleted members

Support standard pagination (page, limit) and sorting (by created_at, employee name, role). Return cursor-based pagination metadata.

Validate the projectId exists and belongs to the current organization. Enforce permission checks: users need project:view permission; users without it must be project members (checked against hrm_time_tracking_project_members for the current employee).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of project member summary records. Each summary includes the member's unique identifier, the employee's name and position, the project role (member or project-lead), and the timestamp when the membership was created.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the project whose members to list. This parameter scopes the member listing to a specific project within the organization. All returned members belong to this project.
parameters.name: projectId

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for listing project members. Supports filtering by employee name (partial match), role (member or project-lead), and an option to include soft-deleted (archived) members. Standard pagination with page index, limit, and sort fields.

prerequisites.description: The project identified by projectId must exist before its members can be listed. The list operation validates that the projectId belongs to the current organization and will reject requests referencing non-existent projects.

operations.description:
Retrieve all active members assigned to a specific project.

Returns the list of employees who are members of the specified project, including their assigned role (member or project-lead) and employee identity information. Only active (non-deleted) project memberships are returned — employees who have been removed from the project are excluded from the results.

Each member record includes the employee's identifier, name, position, employment type, status, and their role within the project context. This endpoint is used in project management interfaces to display team composition, and in task assignment workflows where only existing project members are eligible for task assignment.

If the project has no active members, an empty array is returned. If the specified project does not exist, a 404 Not Found error is returned. Access to this endpoint requires the requesting user to have visibility into the project's organization.
operations.name: get
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_project_members table filtered by hrm_time_tracking_project_id = projectId (UUID) and deleted_at IS NULL (active memberships only).

Join with hrm_time_tracking_employees to retrieve employee details: id, hrm_time_tracking_member_id, position, employment_type, status.

Join through the employee's member relation (hrm_time_tracking_members via hrm_time_tracking_member_id) to access the user's display name (to be exposed as 'name' in the response).

For each active project member, return:
- id (project member record UUID)
- role ('member' or 'project-lead')
- employee: { id, memberId, name, position, employmentType, status }
- createdAt, updatedAt

Edge cases:
- If no project exists with the given projectId, return 404 Not Found.
- If the project exists but has no active members, return empty array [] — not an error.
- Authorization: the requesting user must be a member of the project's organization. Employees can only see members of projects they have access to.
- Hard-deleted or soft-deleted memberships (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are excluded from results.

responseBody.description: Array of active project member records. Each entry contains the member's project role and associated employee identity information.

parameters.description: UUID of the project whose active members are being retrieved. The project must belong to the authenticated user's current organization context.
parameters.name: projectId

prerequisites.description: The project must exist before its members can be listed. Without a project, the endpoint returns 404 Not Found.

operations.description:
Add an employee as a member of a project with a specified role.

Creates a new project membership record that establishes the employee's access to the project for time logging, task viewing, and task management (based on role). Each employee can have at most one membership per project — adding the same employee twice will result in a conflict error.

Project members can log time against the project and view project tasks. Employees assigned the "project-lead" role additionally gain the ability to manage tasks (create, edit, update status) within the project. The employee must belong to the same organization as the project.

If a previous membership for this employee was soft-deleted, the system restores and updates the existing record rather than creating a duplicate.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Validate the project exists by projectId (UUID), is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL), and belongs to the authenticated user's organization.
2. Validate the employee exists by employeeId (UUID), is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL), and belongs to the SAME organization as the project (compare hrm_time_tracking_organization_id).
3. Check the composite unique constraint: look for an existing ProjectMember with matching project_id and employee_id.
   - If found AND soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL): restore by setting deleted_at = NULL, update the role field, and return the restored record.
   - If found AND active (deleted_at IS NULL): return 409 Conflict (employee is already a member of this project).
   - If not found: create a new ProjectMember record.
4. Validate role is exactly "member" or "project-lead" (case-sensitive).
5. Set hrm_time_tracking_project_id from the path parameter.
6. System-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at) are auto-generated — never accepted from input.
7. Return the created/restored ProjectMember with all fields: id, projectId, employeeId, role, createdAt, updatedAt.

operations.description:
Updates the role of an existing project member within a project.

This operation allows users with `project:manage` permission to change an employee's role on a project between 'member' and 'project-lead'. The role determines the level of authority the employee has: members can log time and view tasks, while project-leads additionally gain task management capabilities including creating, editing, and assigning tasks within the project.

The endpoint requires both the project UUID and the specific membership UUID to identify the exact record to update. Only the role field can be changed through this operation; changing which employee is assigned requires removing the existing membership and creating a new one.

Role changes are only allowed on active projects. Projects with 'archived' or 'completed' status will reject the update request. Soft-deleted memberships (employees previously removed from the project) return a 404 Not Found response.

If the member is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null), reject with a 404 Not Found since the membership no longer exists.

If the project is archived or completed (status is not 'active'), reject with a 422 Unprocessable Entity since role changes on non-active projects should not be permitted.

Remove an employee from a project by deleting their project membership record.

After removal, the employee can no longer log time against the project, view the project in their assigned projects list, or access project tasks. Any open tasks assigned to the removed employee within this project have their assignment cleared upon removal. Historical timelogs previously logged by the employee against this project are preserved for reporting and audit purposes.

Preserve all historical timelogs associated with this employee+project combination unchanged. No cascade deletion to timelogs, tasks, or timesheets.

operations.description:
Search and list tasks within a specific project with pagination, filtering, and sorting support.

Returns a paginated list of task summary records belonging to the specified project. This endpoint allows project members to browse tasks with flexible filtering and sorting options. Tasks returned are limited to those visible to the requesting employee based on their project membership (employees can only view tasks from projects they are assigned to).

Filtering is supported by task status (open, in-progress, completed, closed), priority level (low, medium, high, urgent), and assigned employee. Sorting is available by due date, priority level, and creation date in either ascending or descending order. Soft-deleted tasks are excluded from results.

The parent project's status affects availability: active projects return all matching tasks; archived and completed projects still return tasks for historical reference but no new timelogs or task updates are permitted through other endpoints.

Implement sorting from the request body:
- due_date: sort by due_date field (ascending/descending), null values handled appropriately
- priority: sort by mapped numeric value (urgent=4, high=3, medium=2, low=1)
- created_at: sort by created_at field (ascending/descending)

- 403 if the requesting employee is not a member of the project and lacks project:view permission

Reject with 404 if the project doesn't exist, 404 if the task doesn't exist or doesn't belong to the specified project, and 403 if the employee lacks project membership. Return the full IHrmTimeTrackingTask DTO. Include the task's subtasks relation if needed by the DTO. Include assigned employee details via the assignedEmployee relation. operations.description:
Create a new task within a project.

Creates a discrete work item in the specified project with a required title and optional description, priority, estimated hours, due date, assigned employee, and parent task. The new task is initialized with status set to 'open' and priority defaulting to 'medium'.

Task creation requires the requesting user to hold the project:manage permission at the organization level or be assigned as a project-lead within the target project. If an employee is assigned to the task, they must be an active member of the project. If a parent task is specified, it must belong to the same project and nesting is limited to one level (the parent task cannot itself be a subtask).

Upon successful creation, the system returns the full task record including server-generated fields such as id, status, and timestamps. A task history entry recording the initial status is automatically created.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate that the requesting user has project:manage permission OR is a project-lead of the project. Verify the project exists and belongs to the current organization context. If employeeId is provided, verify the employee exists, is active, and is a member of the project (has an active project membership record). If parentTaskId is provided, verify the parent task belongs to the same project and that the parent task does not itself have a parent task (enforce single level of nesting). Set default status to 'open' and default priority to 'medium'. Create the task record with provided fields and auto-generated id, createdAt, updatedAt. Create a task history entry recording the initial status change (previous_status: null, new_status: 'open'). Return the created task object.

responseBody.description: The newly created task record with all fields, including server-generated values such as id, status, and timestamps.

operations.description:
Updates an existing task's attributes within a project.

This operation allows project-leads and users with organization-level project:manage permission to modify task details. The caller can update the title, description, status, priority, estimated hours, due date, and assigned employee. The task must belong to the specified project — the projectId parameter is verified against the task's actual project association, and mismatches are rejected.

Status transitions follow a linear lifecycle: open → in-progress → completed → closed. Statuses cannot be skipped (e.g., open → completed) or regress (e.g., completed → in-progress). When the status is changed, an immutable TaskHistory entry is automatically created to record the transition for full audit trail coverage.

Employee assignment is validated against the project's active membership list — the assigned employee must have an active (non-deleted) project membership record. The task's project association is immutable; tasks remain in their original project throughout their lifecycle. Soft-deleted tasks return a 404 not found response.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting user as a member of the organization.
2. Look up the task by taskId in hrm_time_tracking_tasks table; return 404 if not found or deleted_at is not null (soft-deleted).
3. Verify task.hrm_time_tracking_project_id matches the provided projectId; return 422 Unprocessable Entity if mismatched.
4. Verify the requesting employee has project-lead role (role == 'project-lead') in hrm_time_tracking_project_members for this project where deleted_at is null, OR has organization-level project:manage permission; return 403 Forbidden if unauthorized.
5. Parse and validate the IHrmTimeTrackingTask.IUpdate request body:
   - title: optional, must be non-empty string if provided
   - description: optional free-text string
   - status: optional, must be one of ['open', 'in-progress', 'completed', 'closed']; if provided, must follow linear forward-only transition from current status (no skipping or regression)
   - priority: optional, must be one of ['low', 'medium', 'high', 'urgent']
   - estimated_hours: optional non-negative float
   - due_date: optional timestamp
   - hrm_time_tracking_employee_id: optional UUID or null (to unassign); if set to an employee, verify the employee has an active membership in hrm_time_tracking_project_members where hrm_time_tracking_project_id matches and deleted_at is null; return 422 if not found.
6. If status field value is changed from its current value, create a new hrm_time_tracking_task_histories record capturing the previous status and new status for immutable audit trail.
7. Update the task record with provided field values and set updated_at to the current timestamp.
8. Return the complete updated IHrmTimeTrackingTask entity as the response body.

responseBody.description: The fully updated task entity reflecting all applied changes, including updated_at timestamp.

operations.description:
Deletes (soft-deletes) a task within a project. The task record is marked as deleted by setting its `deleted_at` timestamp, but the database record is preserved to maintain historical integrity of associated timelogs, task history entries, and subtask references.

After deletion, the task is no longer visible in task lists or project boards. Associated timelogs that referenced this task are preserved — they remain visible in reports with their task reference intact (showing the soft-deleted task). Task history entries are preserved as an immutable audit trail.

**Authorization**: Requires `project:manage` permission at the organization level, or a project-lead role for the specified project. Regular project members cannot delete tasks.

**Subtasks**: If the task has subtasks, their `parent_task_id` is cleared, promoting them to top-level tasks within the same project so no work records are lost.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. **Existence & Scope Check**: Verify the task with the given `taskId` exists and belongs to the project identified by `projectId`. If not found, return 404. Also ensure the task is not already soft-deleted (deleted_at is null).

2. **Authorization**: Check that the authenticated employee has `project:manage` permission OR is a project-lead member of the specified project. Use the hrm_time_tracking_project_members table to verify project-lead role (role = 'project-lead'). Regular members without project-lead or project:manage permission are denied (403).

3. **Soft Delete**: Set `deleted_at` to the current timestamp on the hrm_time_tracking_tasks record. Update `updated_at` as well.

4. **Subtasks Handling**: For any subtasks (tasks whose `parent_task_id` references this task), clear their `parent_task_id` to null, promoting them to top-level tasks. This prevents loss of subtask data and ensures they remain visible and manageable within the project.

5. **Data Preservation**: Do NOT modify associated timelogs (hrm_time_tracking_timelogs) or task histories (hrm_time_tracking_task_histories). Their FK references to the task remain valid as the record is only soft-deleted.

6. **Response**: Return the updated task entity (IHrmTimeTrackingTask) with the deleted_at field populated, confirming successful deletion.

7. **Edge Cases**:
   - If the task is already deleted (deleted_at is not null), return 404 as if it doesn't exist.
   - If the project itself is soft-deleted (deleted_at not null on project), reject with 404 — cannot operate on deleted projects.
   - Clearing subtask parent_task_id should be done within a transaction alongside the soft-delete to ensure atomicity.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of task history entries for a specific task within a project.

Task history entries are immutable audit trail records automatically created by the system each time a task's status changes. Each entry captures the previous status, the new status, the timestamp of the change, and the employee who performed the change. This provides a complete, chronological record of all status transitions throughout the task's lifecycle.

This endpoint supports searching by employee who performed the change, filtering by previous and new status values, date range filtering on the change timestamp, and sorting by creation date. Results are returned in chronological order by default (most recent first).

Only users with task viewing access to the parent project can view task history entries. The data is organization-scoped via the project's owning organization, enforcing multi-tenant data isolation.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query `hrm_time_tracking_task_histories` filtered by `hrm_time_tracking_task_id = taskId`.

Verify accessibility:
- Join through `hrm_time_tracking_tasks` on `hrm_time_tracking_task_id` to confirm the task belongs to the specified project (`hrm_time_tracking_project_id = projectId`)
- Then join through `hrm_time_tracking_projects` on `hrm_time_tracking_project_id` to scope results to the authenticated user's current organization
- Enforce task visibility rules: users with project:view permission can see all tasks; project members can only see tasks in projects they are assigned to

Apply filters from request body:
- `hrm_time_tracking_employee_id` (optional): filter by the employee who performed the status change
- `previous_status` (optional): filter by the source status of the transition
- `new_status` (optional): filter by the destination status of the transition
- `created_at` date range (optional): filter by when the status change occurred

Apply sorting:
- Default sort by `created_at` descending (most recent first)
- Support ascending sort on `created_at` for chronological timeline view

Apply pagination using IPage cursor-based or offset pagination pattern.

Return summary records containing: id, created_at, previous_status, new_status, and employee information (id, display name). The summary should not include full entity data.

No write operations are permitted — task history is immutable (append-only audit trail).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of task history summary records containing timestamp, previous status, new status, and the employee who performed the change, ordered by creation date with the most recent first.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single task history entry recording a status change in a task's lifecycle.

Task history entries are immutable audit trail records that capture every task status transition within a project. Each entry records the previous status, new status, the employee who performed the change, and the exact timestamp. This endpoint returns a complete history record scoped within the specified task and project, providing full visibility into task lifecycle changes for accountability and auditing purposes.

The response includes all fields of the task history record: the associated task and employee identifiers, the status transition details (previous and new status values), and creation timestamp. Since task history entries are immutable append-only records, the returned data represents a permanent historical fact that cannot be modified or deleted.

Access is restricted to employees who are members of the parent project, or users with organization-level project:view permission.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_tracking_task_histories table with authorization scoping through the project hierarchy.

1. Verify the project exists within the user's organization context: query hrm_time_tracking_projects with id = projectId AND hrm_time_tracking_organization_id = <current_org_id> AND deleted_at IS NULL. Return 404 if not found.
2. Verify the task exists within the project: query hrm_time_tracking_tasks with id = taskId AND hrm_time_tracking_project_id = projectId AND deleted_at IS NULL. Return 404 if not found.
3. Verify the requesting employee has access to the project: check hrm_time_tracking_project_members for the employee's record OR check if the user has organization-level project:view permission. Return 403 if unauthorized.
4. Query hrm_time_tracking_task_histories with id = historyId AND hrm_time_tracking_task_id = taskId AND deleted_at IS NULL. Return 404 if not found.
5. Return the full history record including: id, hrm_time_tracking_task_id, hrm_time_tracking_employee_id, previous_status, new_status, created_at, updated_at. The deleted_at field should be null for valid records.
6. No joins are required — this is a simple single-record lookup.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of timelogs with filtering capabilities.

This endpoint returns timelog entries with support for date range filtering, project and task scoping, and billable status filtering. Results are paginated and sorted for efficient browsing.

## Access Control
- Employees can only view their own timelogs by default
- Users with the **time:viewing** permission can view timelogs across all employees in the organization

## Filtering
Supports combined filtering by date range (`from`/`to`), project ID, task ID, employee ID (for authorized viewers), and billable status. Deleted timelogs (soft-deleted via `deleted_at`) are excluded from results.

## Pagination
Results are paginated with configurable page size. Use the `page` and `limit` parameters in the request body to navigate through results.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_timelogs table excluding soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL).

Apply permission-based employee filtering:
- If the requesting user does NOT have time:viewing permission → filter by hrm_time_tracking_employee_id = current employee's ID
- If the requesting user HAS time:viewing permission → if employeeId filter is provided in request, apply it; otherwise return all employees' timelogs within the organization

Apply optional filters from request body:
- date_from / date_to: filter on `date` column (greater than/less than)
- projectId: filter by hrm_time_tracking_project_id
- taskId: filter by hrm_time_tracking_task_id
- billable: filter by `billable` boolean flag
- employeeId: filter by hrm_time_tracking_employee_id (only for time:viewing users)

Join with hrm_time_tracking_projects to verify organization-scoped access. The employee's organization context is derived from their employee record.

Implement cursor or offset-based pagination using page/limit parameters. Sort by date descending by default, with optional sort field and direction.

Return paginated summary records including: id, employee (id, name), project (id, name, colorCode), task (id, title) if present, date, duration_minutes, description (truncated), billable flag, and timesheet status indicator.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timelog summary records. Each entry includes the timelog's date, duration, project details, optional task, description, billable status, and timesheet association status.
