operations.description:
Retrieve a single timelog entry by its unique identifier.

Employees can view their own timelogs to review logged work hours, check descriptions, and verify billable status. Users with the time:viewing permission can view any employee's timelogs across the organization, enabling supervisors and managers to review logged time without needing access to individual employee accounts.

The response includes the full timelog record with its associated employee, project, optional task reference, and optional timesheet relationship. The timelog's timesheet status indicates whether the entry is draft, submitted, approved (locked), or rejected.

Returns 404 Not Found if the timelog does not exist or has been soft-deleted. Returns 403 Forbidden if the requesting employee lacks permission to view this specific timelog.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_tracking_timelogs table by primary key (id) matching the timelogId path parameter.

Authorization logic:
- Extract the requesting employee's ID from the authenticated session context.
- If the employee does NOT have time:viewing permission, require that hrm_time_tracking_employee_id matches the requesting employee's ID. If it does not match, return 403 Forbidden.
- If the employee HAS time:viewing permission, allow access to any timelog within the same organization.

Joins:
- Join hrm_time_tracking_employees to include employee name and details.
- Join hrm_time_tracking_projects to include project name, color_code, and status.
- If hrm_time_tracking_task_id is not null, join hrm_time_tracking_tasks to include task title, status, and priority.
- If hrm_time_tracking_timesheet_id is not null, join hrm_time_tracking_timesheets to include timesheet status (for determining if the timelog is locked).

For soft-deleted (deleted_at not null) timelogs: return 404 Not Found — soft-deleted records are not accessible through the standard retrieval endpoint.

Return the full IHrmTimeTrackingTimelog response with all fields populated.

operations.description:
Creates a new timelog entry recording work performed by the authenticated employee on a specific date for a given project.

Each timelog captures a discrete interval of work — the date, duration in minutes, project association, optional task for granular tracking, and a description of the work performed. The billable flag indicates whether the time is chargeable (defaults to true; set to false for non-billable activities such as internal meetings or training).

Employees may only log time against projects they are actively assigned to as project members. Archived or completed projects are not eligible for new timelogs. The authenticated employee is inferred from the session — employees cannot create timelogs on behalf of others unless they hold the time:manage permission.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate that the authenticated user has a corresponding employee record in the organization. Verify the employee is active (status = 'active'). Confirm the referenced project exists, is not archived/completed (status = 'active'), and belongs to the same organization as the employee. Validate that the employee is a project member (has a record in hrm_time_tracking_project_members) for the given project. When taskId is provided, verify the task belongs to the specified project, is not deleted, and the employee is assigned to it (or task is unassigned). Validate date — allow future dates unless the organization has restricted them. Set employee_id from the authenticated session's employee record. Set billable to the provided value or default to true. Auto-set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp. Return the complete created timelog record.

responseBody.description: The newly created timelog record with all fields including system-generated identifier, timestamps, and the billable flag.

requestBody.description: Timelog creation payload including work date, duration in minutes, target project, optional task within that project, optional work description, and billable flag (defaults to true).

prerequisites.description: The project referenced by project_id must exist before a timelog can be created against it. The timelog creation validates that the project exists, is active (not archived/completed), and belongs to the same organization as the employee.

The employee must be added as a project member before they can log time against the project. The specification explicitly validates that a record in hrm_time_tracking_project_members exists linking the employee to the given project.

operations.description:
Update an existing timelog (time entry) record.

This operation updates the fields of a specific timelog identified by its UUID. The authenticated employee can only update their own timelogs unless they hold the time:manage permission, which allows updating any employee's timelogs. Timelogs that belong to a submitted or approved timesheet are locked and cannot be modified. Soft-deleted timelogs cannot be updated.

The updatable fields include the work date, duration in minutes, project assignment, optional task assignment, description text, and billable flag. When changing the project assignment, the target project must be in 'active' status and the employee must be a member of the project via a ProjectMember record. When changing the task assignment, the task must belong to the same project as the timelog.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Query the timelog by ID from hrm_time_tracking_timelogs table (soft-delete check: reject if deleted_at IS NOT NULL).

Authorization: If the requesting member does NOT have the time:manage permission, verify that hrm_time_tracking_employee_id matches the requesting employee's ID. Reject with 403 Forbidden if mismatched.

Timesheet lock: If hrm_time_tracking_timesheet_id IS NOT NULL, join to the timesheet and check its status. If status is 'submitted' OR 'approved', reject with 422 Unprocessable Entity — timelogs in submitted or approved timesheets cannot be modified.

Project status validation: If the project field is being changed, verify the new project's status is 'active'. Reject if the new project is 'archived' or 'completed'.

Employee membership: If the project field is being changed, verify the employee has a ProjectMember record for the new project. Reject with 422 if not assigned.

Task validation: If the task field is being changed, verify the task belongs to the same project as the timelog (hrm_time_tracking_task_id -> task's project_id matches hrm_time_tracking_project_id).

Update duration_minutes, description, billable, date, hrm_time_tracking_project_id, and hrm_time_tracking_task_id fields with the provided values. Update the updated_at timestamp to the current time.

Return the fully updated timelog record on success.

responseBody.description: The fully updated timelog record reflecting all applied changes.

parameters.description: The UUID identifier of the timelog to update. (global scope)
parameters.name: timelogId

requestBody.description: Updated timelog data including optional changes to duration, description, billable flag, date, project, and task assignment.

prerequisites.description: The timelog must exist before it can be updated. POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/timelogs creates the initial timelog record that this PUT operation subsequently modifies. Without a prior create, there is no timelog to update and the update operation would fail with a 404 Not Found.

operations.description:
Delete a timelog entry.

Soft-deletes a timelog identified by its unique ID. The timelog is not permanently removed from the database; instead, its `deleted_at` timestamp is set to the current time, preserving the record for historical and audit purposes. The response returns the deleted timelog entity including the timestamp marking when it was deleted.

Deletion is only allowed if the timelog is not part of any submitted or approved timesheet — timelogs in draft timesheets or unassigned to any timesheet can be freely deleted. Employees can only delete their own timelogs unless they hold the `time:manage` permission, which grants the ability to delete any employee's timelogs regardless of timesheet association.

When a timelog is successfully deleted, a real-time `timelog-deleted` event is fired with the timelog's details including identifier, employee, date, duration, project, optional task, and billable status. The event is delivered to the timelog owner, users with `time:view_all` permission, and users with `time:manage` permission.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Validate that the authenticated member has the `time:manage` permission OR the timelog's `hrm_time_tracking_employee_id` matches the authenticated member's employee record. If neither condition is met, reject with 403 Forbidden.

Query the timelog by its `id` (UUID) and verify it exists and is not already soft-deleted (`deleted_at IS NULL`). If not found or already deleted, reject with 404 Not Found.

Check the timelog's associated timesheet status via `hrm_time_tracking_timesheet_id`:
- If the timelog belongs to a timesheet with status `"submitted"` → reject with 422 Unprocessable Entity.
- If the timelog belongs to a timesheet with status `"approved"` → reject with 422 Unprocessable Entity.
- If `hrm_time_tracking_timesheet_id` is null (unassigned) or the timesheet has status `"draft"` or `"rejected"` → proceed with deletion.

Perform a soft delete by setting `deleted_at` to the current timestamp. Return the updated IHrmTimeTrackingTimelog entity (including the now-populated `deleted_at` field) as the response body with status 200 OK.

After successful deletion, fire a real-time `timelog-deleted` event with payload containing: timelog `id`, `hrm_time_tracking_employee_id`, `date`, `duration_minutes`, `hrm_time_tracking_project_id`, optional `hrm_time_tracking_task_id` (if present), and `billable`. Deliver the event to the timelog owner (the employee), users with `time:view_all` permission, and users with `time:manage` permission.

parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the timelog to delete.
parameters.name: timelogId

operations.description:
Search and list weekly timesheets with filtering and pagination.

This endpoint returns a paginated list of timesheets scoped to the authenticated member's organization. Employees see only their own timesheets, while users with time:approve permission can view all employees' submitted timesheets. Each timesheet aggregates an employee's timelogs for a Monday-to-Sunday work week and follows a status lifecycle: draft, submitted, approved, or rejected.

Supports filtering by timesheet status (draft, submitted, approved, rejected) and by week date range (week_start_date). Results are sorted by week_start_date descending by default, showing the most recent timesheets first.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_timesheets table with organization-scoped access control. Join with hrm_time_tracking_employees to verify the employee belongs to the authenticated member's organization. Apply organization context from the authenticated member's session.

Access control:
- Employee role: filter by hrm_time_tracking_employee_id = authenticated employee's ID. Only data in draft, submitted, approved, rejected statuses is visible.
- Manager/Admin (time:approve permission): can see all employees' timesheets within the organization. Filter by employee ID if provided in request.
- Deactivated employees: blocked from accessing this endpoint for their organization.

Filter logic:
- status (optional): exact match on status field. Valid values: draft, submitted, approved, rejected.
- week_start_date range (optional): filter by week_start_date >= startDate AND week_start_date <= endDate.
- hrm_time_tracking_employee_id (optional, manager only): filter by a specific employee.

Pagination: use cursor-based pagination. Sort by week_start_date descending. Apply soft-delete filter: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL.

Response returns IPageIHrmTimeTrackingTimesheet.ISummary with: id, week_start_date, week_end_date, status, total_hours, submitted_at, reviewed_at, rejection_reason, employee summary (id, name).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timesheet summaries, each containing key metadata including the week period, current status, total hours, and submission/review timestamps.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering timesheets by status, date range, and employee. Supports standard pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific timesheet by its unique identifier.

A timesheet is a weekly aggregation of an employee's timelogs for a Monday-to-Sunday work period, tracking the total hours worked and progressing through a status workflow (draft → submitted → approved → rejected). This endpoint returns the full timesheet record including review metadata, total hours, and lifecycle timestamps.

Employees can only access their own timesheets. Users with the "time:view_all" or "time:approve" permission can view any employee's timesheet within the organization. Soft-deleted timesheets are excluded and return a 404 Not Found.

When approved, the timesheet is final and all included timelogs are permanently locked. When rejected, the rejection_reason field provides the reason for return to draft status.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_tracking_timesheets table by id with the given timesheetId parameter. Exclude soft-deleted records by filtering deleted_at IS NULL.

Authorization: Determine the requesting employee's identity from the authenticated member context (hrm_time_tracking_employee_id).
- If the timesheet's hrm_time_tracking_employee_id matches the requesting employee → allow access.
- If the requesting user has 'time:view_all' or 'time:approve' permission within the employee's organization → allow access.
- Otherwise → return 404 Not Found (do not reveal existence of unauthorized timesheets).

Include the related employee and reviewer data if needed by the response DTO. Return 404 if the timesheet is not found or is soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL).

responseBody.description: The full timesheet entity including total hours, status, week date range, review metadata (reviewer, reviewed_at, rejection_reason), and lifecycle timestamps (created_at, updated_at).

parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target timesheet.
parameters.name: timesheetId

operations.description:
Creates a new draft timesheet for the authenticated employee for a specified work week.

The work week runs from Monday to Sunday. The employee provides the Monday date (weekStartDate), and the system automatically calculates the week end date (Sunday). At most one timesheet per employee per work week is allowed — if a timesheet already exists for the specified week, the request is rejected.

Upon creation, the system automatically includes all timelogs owned by the employee whose date falls within the Monday-to-Sunday period. The total hours are calculated by summing the duration of all included timelogs. The timesheet is created in 'draft' status, allowing the employee to add or remove timelogs before submission.

Deactivated employees are blocked from creating timesheets. Historical data from previous weeks remains accessible for viewing and reporting.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Authenticated employee context:
- Extract employee_id from the authenticated user's active employee record in the current organization.
- Verify employee is active (status !== 'deactivated'). If deactivated, reject with 403 Forbidden.

Create logic:
1. Validate weekStartDate is a Monday (day of week = 1 in JavaScript/ISO). If not, reject with 400 Bad Request.
2. Calculate weekEndDate = weekStartDate + 6 days (Sunday).
3. Check uniqueness: query hrm_time_tracking_timesheets for existing record with same employee_id AND week_start_date. If found, reject with 409 Conflict.
4. Query hrm_time_tracking_timelogs for all entries where:
   - hrm_time_tracking_employee_id = employee_id
   - date >= weekStartDate AND date <= weekEndDate
   - deleted_at IS NULL
   - hrm_time_tracking_timesheet_id IS NULL (unassociated timelogs)
5. Calculate total_hours = SUM(duration_minutes) / 60.0 of found timelogs.
6. Create timesheet record with:
   - employee_id, week_start_date, week_end_date
   - status = 'draft'
   - total_hours = computed value
   - submitted_at = null, reviewed_at = null, rejection_reason = null
7. Update all found timelogs: set hrm_time_tracking_timesheet_id to the new timesheet's ID.
8. Return the created timesheet with all fields populated.

Edge cases:
- Employee deactivated → 403 Forbidden
- Duplicate week → 409 Conflict
- No timelogs found for the week → still create the draft timesheet (draft can be empty, but submission requires at least one timelog per section [198])
- Cross-timezone considerations: dates are stored as timestamps; use UTC date boundaries for query consistency

responseBody.description: The created draft timesheet including its auto-calculated total hours, the associated week range, initial draft status, and the list of automatically included timelogs.

requestBody.description: The week start date (Monday) identifying the work week for which a draft timesheet should be created. The work week runs Monday to Sunday.

operations.description:
Submit a draft timesheet for managerial approval. This operation transitions the timesheet from draft to submitted status, initiating the approval workflow. Upon successful submission, all timelogs within the timesheet become locked and cannot be edited or deleted until the timesheet is rejected and returned to draft status.

The operation validates that the timesheet is currently in draft status, contains at least one timelog, and that no other timesheet for the same work week is already in submitted or approved status. The submission timestamp is recorded at the time of successful transition. After submission, the timesheet is visible to reviewers with time:approve permission for approval or rejection processing.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Validate the timesheet exists and belongs to the authenticated employee's organization. Verify the timesheet is owned by the requesting employee (self-only submission). Check status is 'draft' — reject with 422 if not draft. Check the timesheet has at least one associated timelog — reject with 422 if empty. Verify no other timesheet for the same work week (same week_start_date) is already in 'submitted' or 'approved' status — reject with 409 Conflict if duplicate exists. On all checks passing: update status to 'submitted', set submitted_at to current timestamp, increment updated_at. Lock all associated timelogs from editing/deletion. Return the updated timesheet with full details including employee reference, timelog summaries, and submission metadata.

responseBody.description: The updated timesheet with status changed to submitted, including submission timestamp, employee details, and associated timelogs.

parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the timesheet to submit for approval. Must belong to the authenticated employee's organization.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Submission confirmation for the draft timesheet. The act of submitting requires no additional data beyond authentication context; the presence of the request body with valid structure confirms the submission intent.

prerequisites.description: At least one timelog must exist for the employee within the work week before the timesheet can be submitted. The submission operation validates that the timesheet contains at least one timelog and rejects with 422 if empty.

A draft timesheet must exist before it can be submitted for approval. The submission operation references the timesheet by {timesheetId} and validates it is in 'draft' status — reject with 422 if not draft.

operations.description:
Delete a timesheet.

Deletes an existing timesheet by its unique identifier. Only timesheets in draft or rejected status can be deleted — submitted timesheets awaiting review and approved timesheets (which are final and immutable) cannot be deleted. When a timesheet is deleted, all timelogs associated with it are automatically disassociated (their timesheet reference is cleared), but the timelogs themselves are preserved.

This operation performs a soft delete: the timesheet record is marked as deleted via a timestamp for historical auditing purposes but is not physically removed from the database. The soft-deleted record is excluded from standard list queries but retained for audit trail integrity.

Authorization: The authenticated employee must be the owner of the timesheet, or the user must hold the time:manage permission to delete any employee's timesheet.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Validate the timesheet exists and is not already soft-deleted (deleted_at is null). Verify the requesting user has authorization: either the timesheet belongs to the requesting employee, or the user has the time:manage permission. Check the timesheet status: if status is 'submitted' or 'approved', reject the operation with a business error indicating that submitted/approved timesheets cannot be deleted. Only timesheets with status 'draft' or 'rejected' are eligible for deletion. Perform a soft delete by setting the deleted_at column to the current timestamp using the database's UTC now function. Disassociate all timelogs referencing this timesheet by setting their hrm_time_tracking_timesheet_id foreign key to null (do not delete the timelogs). Update the updated_at timestamp on the timesheet. Do not cascade delete any related records. Return HTTP 204 No Content with no response body on success. If the timesheet is not found or already deleted, return 404 Not Found. If the timesheet is in an invalid status, return 422 Unprocessable Entity with a description of the constraint.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet to delete (UUID).
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: The timesheet must be created before it can be deleted. POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/timesheets creates a new draft timesheet that this delete operation targets.

operations.description:
Search and list timer records with powerful filtering, pagination, and sorting capabilities.

This endpoint allows organization members to browse timer sessions recorded within their organization. A timer represents a live time tracking session that an employee uses to record work duration in real-time — each timer captures the project being worked on, an optional task, an optional description, and tracks the elapsed duration from its start timestamp.

Users with the `time:view_all` permission can view timer records across all employees in the organization, making it useful for managers and administrators who need to monitor time tracking activity and see who is currently running timers. Users without this permission can only view their own timer records — the system automatically restricts the result set.

Results can be filtered by timer status (running, stopped, or discarded), associated project, optional task assignment, and date ranges for when the timer started or stopped. This enables workflows such as reviewing all running timers across the organization, inspecting completed timer sessions for a specific project, or auditing timer activity within a date range. The response is cursor-paginated with configurable sorting to support efficient browsing of large timer histories.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_timers table with pagination and filtering.

**Data Access & Organization Isolation:**
- Join through hrm_time_tracking_employees to the requesting user's current organization context
- The requesting user's organization is resolved from their Employee record (hrm_time_tracking_employee_id on the member session)
- Only return timers belonging to employees whose organization_id matches the requesting user's organization
- NEVER allow cross-organization data leaks — this is strictly enforced

**Permission-Based Access:**
- Check if the requesting user has `time:view_all` permission via their role
- If user HAS `time:view_all`: return timers for ALL employees in the organization (filterable by employeeId)
- If user does NOT have `time:view_all`: only return timers owned by the requesting user themselves (ignore any employeeId filter)

**Filtering Criteria (in request body):**
- `employeeId`: Filter by timer owner (ignored if user lacks time:view_all)
- `status`: Filter by timer status — "running", "stopped", "discarded"
- `projectId`: Filter by associated project
- `taskId`: Filter by optional task (null task filter returns timers without task)
- `startedAt.from` / `startedAt.to`: Date range filter on started_at timestamp
- `stoppedAt.from` / `stoppedAt.to`: Date range filter on stopped_at timestamp

**Pagination & Sorting:**
- Use cursor-based pagination with sort and limit fields in request body
- Default sort: started_at descending (newest first)
- Supported sort fields: started_at, stopped_at, status
- Include next cursor in response for pagination continuation
- Return empty array (not error) when no results match

**Edge Cases:**
- Employee with no timers → empty result set
- Invalid employee ID (within org but doesn't exist) → empty result set
- Stopped timers have stopped_at populated and status "stopped"
- Discarded timers have stopped_at populated and status "discarded"
- Running timers have stopped_at = null and status "running"
- An employee can have at most one running timer
- Filtering by "running" status should return at most one per employee
- Archived/completed project filters: existing timer records for archived projects are still visible (the filter restriction applies only to creating new timers, not viewing historical ones)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timer summary records. Each summary includes the timer's unique identifier, status, start timestamp, stop timestamp (null if running), employee reference, project reference, optional task reference, description, and timestamps. The response includes pagination metadata for cursor-based navigation.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering timer records. Supports filtering by employee ID (for users with time:view_all), timer status (running, stopped, discarded), associated project, optional task, and date range for started_at or stopped_at timestamps. Includes pagination parameters (sort, limit, cursor) for browsing large result sets.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific timer session by its unique identifier.

Each timer belongs to an employee and tracks a real-time work session with a project (and optionally a task). The response includes the timer's current status (running, stopped, or discarded), the start timestamp, the optional stopped timestamp, and the associated project and task references. If the timer is currently running, the stopped_at field is null.

This endpoint enforces organization-level data isolation: the requesting employee must belong to the same organization as the timer's owning employee. A 404 response is returned if the timer does not exist or is not accessible within the current organization context.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query hrm_time_tracking_timers by id = {timerId}. Join with hrm_time_tracking_employees to enforce multi-tenant isolation: verify the timer's employee belongs to the same organization as the requesting employee (via hrm_time_tracking_organization_id). If no matching record is found or the organization does not match, return 404 Not Found. The response should return the full timer entity data including id, hrm_time_tracking_employee_id, hrm_time_tracking_project_id, hrm_time_tracking_task_id, description, started_at, stopped_at, status, created_at, and updated_at. No pagination or filtering is needed — this is a single record retrieval.

responseBody.description: The complete timer entity with current status, timestamps, and associated project/task references.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the timer session to retrieve.
parameters.name: timerId

prerequisites.description: The timer must be created before it can be retrieved by ID. POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/timers starts a new timer session, producing the timer entity that this GET operation reads.

operations.description:
Starts a new timer session for the authenticated employee to track work time in real-time.

The employee must select a project they are currently assigned to. Optionally, a specific task within that project and a description of the work can be provided. The system automatically records the start timestamp and sets the timer status to "running".

An employee can have at most one active timer at any time — if a timer is already running, the request is rejected and the employee must stop or discard the existing timer first. Deactivated employees cannot start timers. Timers cannot be started on archived or completed projects.

Once started, the timer runs indefinitely until the employee manually stops it (which creates a timelog with the calculated duration) or discards it (which abandons the session without recording time).
operations.name: start
operations.specification:
Start a timer for the authenticated employee.

Validate:
1. The authenticated employee exists and has status 'active' — reject with error if deactivated.
2. The employee has no existing timer with status 'running' — query hrm_time_tracking_timers where employee_id = {employee.id} AND status = 'running'. If found, reject with error (multiple active timers blocked).
3. The referenced project exists, belongs to the employee's organization, and the employee is a project member — query hrm_time_tracking_projects and hrm_time_tracking_project_members. Project status must NOT be 'archived' or 'completed' — reject if so.
4. If taskId is provided, verify the task exists and belongs to the specified project — query hrm_time_tracking_tasks.

On success:
- Create a new hrm_time_tracking_timers record with:
  - id: auto-generated UUID
  - hrm_time_tracking_employee_id: from authenticated employee
  - hrm_time_tracking_project_id: from request
  - hrm_time_tracking_task_id: from request (optional, null if not provided)
  - description: from request (optional, null if not provided)
  - started_at: current timestamp
  - stopped_at: null
  - status: 'running'
  - created_at: current timestamp
  - updated_at: current timestamp
- Fire timer-started event to the timer owner and users with time:view_all permission.
- Return the created timer entity.

responseBody.description: The created timer entity with system-assigned fields including the unique identifier, the start timestamp, the running status, and all user-provided values.

requestBody.description: Parameters for starting a timer: the project to track time against (required), an optional task within that project, and an optional description of the work being performed.

prerequisites.description: The project must exist and be in 'active' status before a timer can track time against it. The timer's required projectId references this project.

The authenticated employee must be an active member of the project with a project membership record. The timer specification validates that the employee is a project member before allowing the timer to start.
If the timer references a specific task (optional taskId), that task must exist and belong to the same project. Required only when taskId is provided in the timer start request.

operations.description:
Update a running timer's details including the associated project, task, and description.

This operation allows an employee to modify the project, task assignment, and description of their currently active (running) timer. The timer must belong to the requesting employee and be in the 'running' status to accept updates.

**Modifiable fields**: The project (required), task (optional, must belong to the selected project), and description (optional) can all be changed while the timer is running. When the timer is later stopped, the timelog inherits the final values of these fields.

**Project validation**: The selected project must be in 'active' status. Archived or completed projects are not accepting new time entries and cannot be assigned to a running timer.

**Task validation**: If a task is specified, it must belong to the selected project.

**Authorization**: Only the employee who owns the timer (the employee who started it) can update their own timer.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_tracking_timers table by timerId. Verify the timer exists and the requesting employee is the owner (hrm_time_tracking_employee_id matches the authenticated employee).

**Status check**: Verify timer.status === 'running'. Reject with 422 if status is 'stopped' or 'discarded' — stopped/discarded timers are final and cannot be modified.

**Project validation**: Verify the new project exists, belongs to the same organization as the timer's employee, and has status === 'active'. Reject with 422 if status is 'archived' or 'completed'.

**Task validation**: If taskId is provided, verify the task exists, belongs to the selected project (hrm_time_tracking_project_id matches), and is not soft-deleted. Reject with 422 if the task does not match the project.

**Update**: Update only the provided fields (hrm_time_tracking_project_id, hrm_time_tracking_task_id, description) and set updated_at to current timestamp. Return the full updated timer record.

**Edge cases**: If the timer is stopped/discarded, reject with appropriate error message. If the employee is deactivated (status !== 'active'), reject per employee status rules.

responseBody.description: The updated timer entity with all fields reflecting the changes, including the updated timestamp.

parameters.description: The UUID of the timer session to update. The timer must belong to the authenticated employee and be in 'running' status.
parameters.name: timerId

requestBody.description: Fields to update on a running timer: the project, optional task within that project, and optional description. The timer must be in 'running' status.

prerequisites.description: The project must exist before it can be assigned to a running timer. The operation validates that the referenced project is in 'active' status and belongs to the same organization as the authenticated employee.

If a taskId is provided in the update request, the task must exist and belong to the selected project. The operation validates that the task's hrm_time_tracking_project_id matches the projectId being assigned.

The timer must have been started (created) before it can be updated. The operation queries the timer by timerId and verifies it exists and belongs to the authenticated employee before applying any updates.

operations.description:
Discard a running timer without creating a timelog.

When an employee discards a timer, the timer session is terminated without generating a time entry. This operation is the counterpart to stopping a timer — while stopping creates a timelog with the elapsed duration, discarding abandons the session entirely. The discarded timer record is preserved with status set to 'discarded' and stopped_at populated for audit trail purposes.

Only the timer owner (the employee who started the timer) can discard their own running timer. Users with the time:manage permission may discard any employee's running timer. Timers that are already in 'stopped' or 'discarded' status cannot be discarded — the timer must be currently running.

After discarding, the employee is free to start a new timer. No timelog is created, and the elapsed time is not recorded. The response returns the updated timer object reflecting the new status and stopped_at timestamp.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_tracking_timers table by id (timerId). If not found, return 404 Not Found.

Validate timer state: the timer must be in 'running' status (status = 'running', stopped_at is null). If the timer is already 'stopped' or 'discarded', return 409 Conflict with a message indicating only running timers can be discarded.

Authorization check: the authenticated employee must own the timer (hrm_time_tracking_employee_id matches the current employee's employee id), OR the authenticated user must hold the time:manage permission. If neither condition is met, return 403 Forbidden.

Update the timer record: set stopped_at to the current UTC timestamp, status to 'discarded', and updated_at to the current UTC timestamp. Do NOT create a timelog — this is the critical difference from the stop operation.

Emit a timer-discarded real-time event. Deliver the event to the timer owner (the employee who owns the timer). For users with time:view_all permission, remove the timer from the visible active-timer list.

Return the updated timer record (IHrmTimeTrackingTimer) with the new status and stopped_at values.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the running timer to discard.
parameters.name: timerId

prerequisites.description: Timer must be created (started) before it can be discarded. The POST operation starts a timer session for the authenticated employee, which generates the timerId used in the discard operation.

operations.description:
Search and list employee invitations within the organization.

This endpoint allows organization members with the `employee:manage` permission to browse, filter, and search through all invitation records for their organization. Invitations represent pending or historical onboarding requests sent to external email addresses, tracking the full lifecycle from pending to accepted, expired, or cancelled.

Supports filtering by invitation status (pending, accepted, expired, cancelled), target email address, inviter member, assigned role, and date ranges (creation date, expiration date, acceptance date). Results are paginated with configurable page size and cursor or offset-based navigation. Results are sorted by creation date in descending order by default.

Access is restricted to organization members holding the `employee:manage` permission. The organization scope is automatically determined from the authenticated member's current organization context — cross-organization invitation browsing is not supported.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_invitations table filtered by the authenticated member's current organization (hrm_time_tracking_organization_id).

Authorization: Only members with `employee:manage` permission within the organization can access this endpoint. Return 403 Forbidden for unauthorized users.

Filter criteria from request body:
- status: Filter by invitation status (pending, accepted, expired, cancelled). Support single or multiple status values.
- email: Partial or exact email search (case-insensitive).
- inviterId: Filter by the member who sent the invitation.
- roleId: Filter by the assigned role.
- dateRange.createdAt: Filter by creation date range.
- dateRange.expiredAt: Filter by expiration date range.
- dateRange.acceptedAt: Filter by acceptance date range.

Pagination: Support standard pagination with page/limit parameters. Return total count for UI display.

Sorting: Default sort by created_at descending. Support sort by email, status, created_at.

Relations to include in summary:
- inviter: member name and email from hrm_time_tracking_members
- role: role name from hrm_time_tracking_roles
- acceptor: member name and email (only if status is accepted)

Soft delete: Exclude soft-deleted invitations (deleted_at IS NULL) by default unless explicitly requested.

Data isolation: Results MUST be scoped to the authenticated member's current organization. Never return invitations from other organizations.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of invitation summary records optimized for administrative invitation management displays, including inviter details, role information, and status indicators.

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for browsing organization invitations, including status filters, email search, date ranges, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieves detailed information about a specific invitation record by its unique identifier.

Invitations are onboarding requests sent to external email addresses by organization members with employee management permissions. Each invitation follows a lifecycle: pending (awaiting recipient sign-up), accepted (recipient signed up and joined the organization), expired (validity period elapsed), or cancelled (manually revoked by an administrator). This endpoint returns the complete invitation state including the invited email address, the assigned role, the member who sent the invitation, and where applicable, the member who accepted it.

Access to this endpoint requires the `employee:manage` permission within the organization. The invitation is strictly scoped to the requesting member's current organization — invitations from other organizations are never visible, enforcing cross-organization data isolation.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting member from the JWT session.
2. Resolve the member's current active organization from the session context.
3. Verify the member has the `employee:manage` permission within that organization. If not, return 403 Forbidden.
4. Query `hrm_time_tracking_invitations` by `id` matching the `invitationId` parameter.
5. Ensure the invitation belongs to the member's current organization (`hrm_time_tracking_organization_id` matches the resolved organization). This enforces cross-organization isolation (Section 347).
6. Exclude soft-deleted records: add `deleted_at IS NULL` filter.
7. Include related data via joins: organization name, inviter member name and email, acceptor member name and email (nullable), and role name.
8. If the invitation is not found, belongs to a different organization, or is soft-deleted, return 404 Not Found.
9. Return the full `IHrmTimeTrackingInvitation` DTO with all fields.

responseBody.description: Full invitation record including the organization ID, invited email address, current lifecycle status, the member who sent the invitation, the member who accepted it (if applicable), the assigned role, and timestamps for creation, expiry, and acceptance.

parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the invitation record to retrieve. This is the primary key of the invitation in the system.
parameters.name: invitationId

operations.description:
Invite an external person to join the organization by email.

The operation accepts an email address and a role, then handles two distinct cases automatically. If the invited email already belongs to a registered user, the system immediately creates an active employee record for that user in the organization with the specified role — granting them instant access without any invitation workflow. If the email has no registered account, a pending invitation is created that the recipient can accept by signing up with that email address.

Requires the `employee:manage` permission within the current organization. The organization context is determined by the authenticated member's current organization selection. If an active employee record already exists for the invited email in the same organization, or if a pending invitation for the same email already exists, the request is rejected with an appropriate conflict error.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Verify the authenticated member has `employee:manage` permission within their current organization. Look up the invited email in the hrm_time_tracking_members table. If the email belongs to an existing member: (a) check that no active employee record already exists for that member in this organization (enforced by @@unique constraint but needs a readable error); (b) create an hrm_time_tracking_employee record with status='active', the specified roleId, and employment_type defaulted; (c) record an activity log entry with type 'employee.invited'. If the email has no registered account: (a) verify no pending invitation exists for the same email+organization combination (enforced by application logic, not schema); (b) create hrm_time_tracking_invitation record with status='pending', email, roleId, and inviterId. In both cases, return the invitation (for auto-add, create an accepted invitation record as a log of the action alongside the employee). Validate roleId belongs to the current organization (cross-org role assignment rejected).

responseBody.description: The created invitation record capturing the invite details, current status, and timestamps. When the invited email belongs to an existing user, an accepted invitation record is returned alongside the auto-created employee.

requestBody.description: The email address to invite and the role to assign upon acceptance. For existing users, the role takes effect immediately when the employee record is created. For new users, the role is stored in the invitation and assigned when the recipient signs up.

prerequisites.description: The role referenced by role_id must exist in the organization before an invitation can reference it. The operation validates that the role belongs to the current organization and rejects non-existent or cross-organization role assignments. Create the custom role first via this endpoint so it can be assigned to the invited person.

operations.description:
Update an existing pending invitation.

This endpoint allows organization members with the `employee:manage` permission to modify a pending invitation by its unique identifier. Only invitations in `pending` status can be updated — invitations that have already been accepted, expired, or cancelled cannot be modified.

**Role Update**: The role assigned upon acceptance can be changed by updating the role identifier. The new role must belong to the same organization as the invitation.

**Cancellation**: Setting the status to `cancelled` revokes the invitation. Once cancelled, the invited person cannot accept it by signing up later. The system also records a soft-delete timestamp for audit purposes.

**Authorization**: The requesting user must have the `employee:manage` permission within the invitation's target organization. Invitations are scoped to a single organization and are not visible across organizations.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Validate the authenticated user has `employee:manage` permission within the organization that owns the invitation. Find the invitation by `invitationId` (UUID). If not found, throw 404 Not Found. Verify the invitation is in `pending` status — only pending invitations can be updated; if already accepted, expired, or cancelled, throw 422 Unprocessable Entity with appropriate message. If updating `hrm_time_tracking_role_id`, validate the new role exists, belongs to the same organization, and is not a deleted role. If updating `status` to `cancelled`, set `deleted_at` timestamp; do not allow changing status to any other value via this endpoint (acceptance and expiry are system-managed). Return the updated invitation record. Use a database transaction to ensure atomicity of the update.

responseBody.description: The updated invitation record reflecting the applied changes.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the invitation to update.
parameters.name: invitationId

requestBody.description: Fields to update on the invitation. Allows modifying the target role or cancelling the invitation by setting status to `cancelled`.

prerequisites.description: The invitation record must exist before it can be updated. POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/invitations creates the invitation in 'pending' status, which is the only status that allows updates via this endpoint.

operations.description:
Cancel a pending employee invitation by its unique identifier.

Only invitations in **pending** status can be cancelled. Once cancelled, the invitation becomes permanently invalid — the invited person cannot accept it by signing up later. The cancelled invitation is soft-deleted and preserved for audit trail purposes. Cancellation of one invitation does not affect other pending invitations for the same email address in different organizations.

This operation requires the `employee:manage` permission within the target organization. Any member with sufficient permission can perform the cancellation.

On success, the response returns the cancelled invitation with its status updated to `cancelled`, the `deleted_at` timestamp recorded, and the `updated_at` timestamp reflecting the change.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting member and identify their current organization context.
2. Authorize: verify the requesting member has `employee:manage` permission within the organization. Return 403 if unauthorized.
3. Load the invitation by `invitationId` from `hrm_time_tracking_invitations` where `deleted_at IS NULL`. Throw 404 if not found.
4. Validate the invitation belongs to the requesting member's current organization for tenant isolation.
5. Validate the invitation is in `pending` status — only pending invitations can be cancelled. Throw 422 with details if status is `accepted`, `expired`, or already `cancelled`.
6. Perform the cancellation: update `status` to "cancelled", set `deleted_at` to current timestamp, update `updated_at` to current timestamp. Do NOT actually delete the row — this is a soft-delete operation.
7. Record an activity log entry (action type: invitation cancellation) for audit trail.
8. Return the updated invitation record reflecting the status change and timestamps.

parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the invitation to cancel. The invitation must currently be in `pending` status.
parameters.name: invitationId

prerequisites.description: The invitation must be created (sent) before it can be cancelled. POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/invitations sends an invitation to an external email, creating a pending invitation record that can later be cancelled via this delete operation.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of activity log entries for the current organization.

Activity logs provide an immutable audit trail of significant organizational actions, including employee lifecycle events (invited, deactivated, reactivated), contract changes (created, edited), project operations (created, archived, completed, deleted), task status transitions, timesheet workflow events (submitted, approved, rejected), and role assignment changes.

Each entry captures the action timestamp, the member who performed the action, the action type classification, the target entity (type, ID, and name), and optional contextual details about what changed. Entries are automatically generated by the system and cannot be manually created, edited, or deleted.

Supports filtering by action type, actor member, and date range for investigation and compliance purposes. Results are ordered chronologically by default, with the most recent entries first. Organization scope is determined by the authenticated member's current organization context.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query hrm_time_tracking_activity_logs table filtered by the authentication middleware's resolved organization ID. Join with hrm_time_tracking_activity_log_types for action type classification and with hrm_time_tracking_members for actor information. Apply optional request body filters: filter by activity log type code(s) via the activityLogType relation, filter by actor member ID, filter by date range on created_at (fromDate/toDate). Support cursor-based pagination with sorting by created_at descending by default. Return paginated summary records containing id, createdAt, action type code/name, actor display name and email, target entity type/id/name, and details. Apply authorization: only members with org:manage permission can access activity logs for their organization.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of activity log summary records optimized for audit trail browsing and investigation displays.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering activity log entries, including optional filters for action type, actor member, date range, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single activity log entry by its unique identifier.

Activity logs are immutable audit trail entries that capture significant actions performed within an organization, such as employee lifecycle events (invited, deactivated, reactivated), contract changes, project operations (created, archived, completed, deleted), task status transitions, timesheet workflow events (submitted, approved, rejected), and role assignments.

Each entry records the actor (member) who performed the action, the action type classification, a reference to the affected business entity (type, UUID, and display name), contextual details about what changed, and the exact timestamp. Once created, activity log entries are never modified or deleted, ensuring a tamper-proof audit trail.

Only members with the org:manage permission within the organization can view activity log entries. If the requested activity log does not exist or belongs to a different organization, the system returns a 404 Not Found response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_tracking_activity_logs table by primary key (id) UUID. Join with hrm_time_tracking_members to resolve the actor's display name and email, join with hrm_time_tracking_activity_log_types to resolve the action type code and name, and join with the parent hrm_time_tracking_organizations for org-level filtering.

Implement organization-scoped access control: the requesting member must have org:manage permission within the organization that owns this activity log. If no record is found or the record belongs to a different organization, return 404 Not Found — do not distinguish between 'not found' and 'access denied' to avoid information leakage.

Return the full activity log record including: id, organization reference (id, name), actor member reference (id, display name, email), action type reference (code, name, category), target entity details (type, id, name), details text, and created_at timestamp. Since activity logs are immutable, no additional locking or versioning is required.

responseBody.description: The full activity log entry including actor identity, action type classification, target entity reference, contextual details, and creation timestamp.

parameters.description: The UUID of the activity log entry to retrieve.
parameters.name: activityLogId

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of activity log action type classifications.

Activity log action types are system-defined categories that classify the kinds of actions recorded in the organization's activity log. Each action type represents a specific event such as employee invitations, contract changes, project lifecycle events, task status transitions, timesheet workflow events, or role assignment changes. These types are seeded during organization initialization and are read-only — users cannot create, modify, or delete action type definitions.

Results can be filtered by category group (e.g., employee, contract, project, task, timesheet, role) to narrow down relevant action types, and sorted for consistent display in the activity log filtering UI.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query the hrm_time_tracking_activity_log_types table with pagination and filtering. Exclude soft-deleted records (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL). Apply search filters: category (exact match), code (partial text search), name (partial text search). Order by category then code for consistent display. Return IPageIHrmTimeTrackingActivityLogType.ISummary with id, code, category, name, description fields. Support cursor-based pagination via sort and limit parameters. Since this is system-seeded reference data, no authorization beyond valid organization membership is required for reading.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of activity log action type summary records. Each item includes the unique code (e.g., employee.invited, project.created), category grouping, display name, and optional description for use in activity log filtering interfaces.

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for listing activity log action types. Supports filtering by category group and searching by action type code or name. Includes pagination parameters for cursor-based result set navigation.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific action type classification by its unique dot-notation code.

Activity log types are system-defined reference records that classify all auditable actions within an organization. Each type uses a structured {category}.{action} identifier (e.g., 'employee.invited', 'project.archived', 'timesheet.approved') and includes a human-readable display name and optional description explaining when the action type is triggered.

This endpoint returns the full record including the category grouping, display name, and descriptive documentation. Since action types are system-seeded reference data that users cannot create or modify, this is a read-only lookup operation.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query hrm_time_tracking_activity_log_types table filtering by the unique code field where deleted_at IS NULL (active records only). Return the single matching record or throw a 404 Not Found error if no active type matches the provided code. Use the @@unique([code]) index for efficient lookup.

responseBody.description: The full activity log type record including the unique code, category grouping, display name, and description explaining when this action type is triggered.

parameters.description: Unique action type code in dot notation (e.g., 'employee.invited', 'project.created', 'timesheet.approved'). This is the stable identifier used to classify activity log entries across the audit system.
parameters.name: activityLogTypeCode

operations.description:
Switch the authenticated member's active organization context to the specified organization.

This operation allows a member who belongs to multiple organizations to change their current working context without logging out or re-authenticating. Upon successful switch, all subsequent API operations performed by the member will be scoped to the newly selected organization, with data access and permissions determined by the member's role within that organization. The member's authentication session and credentials remain unchanged across context switches.

The member must have an active employee record in the target organization. If the member does not belong to the specified organization, the operation is rejected.
operations.name: switchOrganization
operations.specification: Verify the authenticated member exists and has a valid session. Look up the organization by the provided UUID (hrm_time_tracking_organizations.id). Verify the organization exists and has status 'active'. Check that the authenticated member has an active employee record (hrm_time_tracking_employees) linked to this organization. If any check fails, return appropriate 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden error. Update the current session or context state to associate the member with the target organization. Return the organization record as confirmation. Edge case: if the member is already operating in this organization, still succeed gracefully (idempotent behavior).

responseBody.description: The organization that has been activated as the member's current working context. All subsequent operations within this session will be scoped to this organization, applying the permissions associated with the member's role in it.

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the target organization to switch the current session context to. The member must have an active employee record in this organization.
parameters.name: organizationId

operations.description:
Switch the authenticated user's active organization context to the specified organization.

This endpoint allows a member who belongs to multiple organizations to change their current working context without logging out. The target organization is identified by its UUID in the path. Upon a successful switch, all subsequent API operations are scoped to the new organization's data boundary, and the system applies the user's role and permissions within that specific organization.

The system validates that the user has an active employee record in the target organization before allowing the switch. Users whose employee record has been deactivated in the target organization are denied access and informed accordingly. The current organization context is preserved when a switch is denied.

Returns the target organization's full details so the client application can update its UI, apply the correct timezone and currency settings, and reflect the new organizational context.
operations.name: change
operations.specification:
Validate and execute organization context switch:

1. Look up the target organization by organizationId (UUID). If not found, return 404 Not Found.
2. Verify the authenticated member has an employee record in the target organization with status = 'active' (not 'deactivated'). Query hrm_time_tracking_employees where hrm_time_tracking_member_id = session member and hrm_time_tracking_organization_id = organizationId.
3. If no employee record exists, return 403 Forbidden indicating no membership in the target organization.
4. If the employee record has status = 'deactivated', reject with 403 Forbidden referencing 'deactivated employee access denied'. The current organization context must be preserved.
5. If the target organization has status = 'deleted', reject the switch.
6. Update the user's session/organization context to the target organization (in-memory/session state, not persisted to DB).
7. Return the organization record (id, name, description, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month, status, created_at, updated_at).

responseBody.description: The full organization record that the user's active context has been switched to, including its name, description, currency, timezone, fiscal start month, status, and timestamps.

parameters.description: UUID of the target organization to switch the active context to. The authenticated user must have an active employee record in this organization.
parameters.name: organizationId

prerequisites.description: The target organization must exist in the system before a user can switch their active context to it. POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/organizations creates the organization entity and establishes the owner's employee record with the Owner role, satisfying both the organization existence check (step 1) and the active employee membership check (step 2) required by the switch operation.

operations.description:
Transfers ownership of an organization from the current owner to another active employee within the same organization.

This operation changes the organization's owner to the specified employee. The target employee must have an active employee record in the organization and will be assigned the Owner role upon successful transfer. The current owner's role is modified accordingly — they retain access as an Employee (or another role) in the organization unless they are deactivated.

This operation is idempotent: if the target employee is already the owner, the request succeeds without changes.

Authorization: Only the current organization owner can perform this operation. Requires the org:manage permission implicitly through ownership.
operations.name: transferOwnership
operations.specification:
Verify the requesting user is the current organization owner (checked via hrm_time_tracking_organizations.hrm_time_tracking_member_id matching the authenticated member).

Look up the target employee by their UUID (hrm_time_tracking_employees.id). Verify the target employee belongs to the same organization (hrm_time_tracking_employees.hrm_time_tracking_organization_id matches the path parameter). Verify the target employee has status='active' and deleted_at IS NULL.

Use a Prisma transaction to:
1. Update the target employee's role to the 'Owner' built-in role for this organization (find hrm_time_tracking_roles where name='Owner' AND hrm_time_tracking_organization_id = organizationId AND type='built_in')
2. Update the current owner's employee role to 'Manager' (or a configurable fallback role)
3. Update hrm_time_tracking_organizations.hrm_time_tracking_member_id to reference the target employee's member ID
4. Create an activity log entry recording the ownership transfer

If the target employee is the current owner (self-transfer), return success without changes.

Error cases:
- 403: Requesting user is not the current owner
- 404: Organization not found, or target employee not found in this organization
- 409: Target employee is deactivated
- 422: Target employee does not have an active employee record

responseBody.description: The updated organization entity reflecting the new owner information after a successful ownership transfer.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the organization whose ownership will be transferred.
parameters.name: organizationId

requestBody.description: Specifies the target employee who will receive ownership of the organization. The employee must have an active record within the same organization.

prerequisites.description: The organization must be created before ownership can be transferred. The {organizationId} in the path parameter identifies the specific organization whose ownership is being reassigned.

The target employee must exist as an active employee record within the organization. Employee records are created via this operation (auto-creates an active employee when the invited email belongs to an existing registered member). The employee_id in the request body references this record.

operations.description:
Retrieves the current status of all prerequisites required to delete an organization.

An organization can only be deleted when all pending timesheets within the organization have been resolved (approved or rejected) and there are no active employee contracts (contracts with no end date). This endpoint evaluates both conditions and returns detailed status information so the organization owner can determine what actions remain before deletion can proceed.

The response includes individual boolean flags for each requirement along with detail counts to help the owner understand the scope of pending items. Only the organization owner has access to this information.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve the organization by organizationId. Verify the authenticated caller is the organization owner by comparing hrm_time_tracking_member_id against the authenticated member's ID. If the organization does not exist, return 404. If the caller is not the owner, return 403.

Requirement 1 — Pending timesheets resolved:
Query hrm_time_tracking_timesheets joined to hrm_time_tracking_employees (filtered by hrm_time_tracking_organization_id = organizationId) where status is 'draft' or 'submitted' (unresolved states) and deleted_at IS NULL. Count results. The condition is met (true) when count is 0.

Requirement 2 — No active contracts:
Query hrm_time_tracking_employee_contracts joined to hrm_time_tracking_employees (filtered by hrm_time_tracking_organization_id = organizationId) where end_date IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL. Count results. The condition is met (true) when count is 0.

Return both boolean flags, detail counts for each requirement, and a combined allRequirementsMet boolean (true only when both flags are true).

responseBody.description: Current status of all organization deletion prerequisites. Contains boolean flags for each individual requirement, detail counts showing the number of items blocking each requirement, and a combined boolean indicating whether all requirements are satisfied.

parameters.description: UUID of the organization whose deletion prerequisites are being checked. Only the organization owner can view this information.
parameters.name: organizationId

prerequisites.description: The organization must exist before its deletion requirements can be checked. POST /hrmTimeTracking/member/organizations creates the organization that is referenced via the organizationId path parameter.

operations.description:
Retrieves the complete list of all 9 fixed system permission codes available for role-based access control within the time tracking system.

Each permission object contains the permission code string (e.g., 'time:manage') and a human-readable label describing what the permission grants access to. These permissions are assigned to roles via the role-permission junction and govern what operations users can perform within an organization.

The 9 available permissions are: org:manage (organization management), employee:manage (employee administration), employee:view (employee read access), project:manage (project management), project:view (project read access), time:manage (time entry management), time:approve (timesheet approval), time:view_all (view all time entries), and report:view (report viewing).

This endpoint requires no authentication parameters and returns the same permission set regardless of the requesting user or organization context.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query is static — return the 9 fixed permission codes from system configuration or a lookup table. No database query needed; these are hardcoded values: org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, report:view. For each permission code, include its code string and a human-readable description/label for UI display. No pagination, no filtering, no search. No authentication scoping needed — these permissions are the same across all organizations.

responseBody.description: Array of all available system permission codes with their human-readable labels and descriptions for display in role configuration interfaces.

operations.description:
Retrieve the current user's dashboard providing a comprehensive work status overview.

The dashboard combines personal work tracking data with organization-wide metrics for authorized users. The personal section shows hours logged today and this week, active timer status with running duration, the five most recent timelog entries, the current week's timesheet status, and tasks assigned to the employee that are still open or in-progress. When the authenticated employee's role includes the report:view permission, the response additionally includes organization-level metrics: total active employee count, total hours logged across all employees this week, number of pending timesheets awaiting approval, projects approaching or exceeding 80% budget utilization, and the top 5 employees by hours logged this week.

This endpoint requires an active authenticated session with a selected organization context. All date calculations respect the organization's configured timezone. Data access is scoped to the current organization only — no cross-organization data is exposed.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Authenticate the member and identify the current organization context. Find the employee record for this member in the organization (join hrm_time_tracking_employees by member_id and organization_id). If not found, return 404.

Personal Dashboard:
1. Hours logged today: SUM(duration_minutes) FROM hrm_time_tracking_timelogs WHERE employee_id = {employeeId} AND date = TODAY (org timezone) AND deleted_at IS NULL. Convert to hours (divide by 60).
2. Hours logged this week: Same query but date BETWEEN week_start AND week_end (Monday to Sunday in org timezone).
3. Active timer: SELECT FROM hrm_time_tracking_timers WHERE employee_id = {employeeId} AND status = 'running'. Include project name, task name, started_at for elapsed duration calculation.
4. Recent timelogs: Last 5 timelogs for the employee (ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 5), include project name, task name, date, duration_minutes, description, billable.
5. Pending timesheet: SELECT FROM hrm_time_tracking_timesheets WHERE employee_id = {employeeId} AND week_start_date = CURRENT_WEEK_MONDAY (org timezone). Return status (or null if none), total_hours.
6. Assigned tasks: SELECT FROM hrm_time_tracking_tasks WHERE hrm_time_tracking_employee_id = {employeeId} AND status IN ('open', 'in-progress') AND deleted_at IS NULL. Include title, status, priority, due_date, project name.

Organization Dashboard (only if employee's role has 'report:view' permission):
1. Total active employees: COUNT FROM hrm_time_tracking_employees WHERE organization_id = {orgId} AND status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL.
2. Total hours logged this week: SUM(duration_minutes) FROM hrm_time_tracking_timelogs JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees ON employee_id = employees.id WHERE organization_id = {orgId} AND date BETWEEN week_start AND week_end AND deleted_at IS NULL. Convert to hours.
3. Pending timesheets: COUNT FROM hrm_time_tracking_timesheets WHERE status = 'submitted' AND employee is in current organization (JOIN through employees).
4. Budget alerts: Projects WHERE organization_id = {orgId} AND status = 'active' AND budget_hours IS NOT NULL AND (SUM of timelog durations / (budget_hours * 60)) > 0.8. Include name, budget_hours, actual hours, utilization percentage.
5. Top 5 employees by hours: GROUP BY employee_id, SUM(duration_minutes) WHERE date BETWEEN week_start AND week_end, JOIN employees for display_name, ORDER BY SUM DESC LIMIT 5.

Use the organization's configured timezone for date boundaries (today, week start/end). All duration values returned in hours (decimal).

responseBody.description: Combined dashboard data including the employee's personal work overview (hours logged, timer status, recent timelogs, pending timesheet status, assigned tasks) and, for authorized users with report:view permission, organization-wide metrics (active employee count, total hours, pending approvals, budget alerts, top performers).

operations.description:
Retrieves the organization dashboard providing a high-level overview of team productivity and operational status.

The dashboard aggregates real-time data across all active employees, projects, timelogs, and timesheets within the currently active organization. It is intended for users with the `report:view` permission — typically organization owners and managers.

The response includes: total active employee count, total hours logged across all employees for the current week, the number of pending timesheets awaiting approval, projects whose budget utilization exceeds 80%, and the top 5 employees by hours logged this week.

All data is strictly scoped to the organization context selected by the authenticated user. Cross-organization data is never included.

Requires `report:view` permission.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query across multiple tables within the current organization context:

1. Active employees count: COUNT of hrm_time_tracking_employees WHERE organization_id = current AND status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL.

2. Total hours this week: SUM of duration_minutes / 60 from hrm_time_tracking_timelogs JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees WHERE employee.organization_id = current AND timelog.deleted_at IS NULL AND timelog.date is within the current Monday-to-Sunday week (use the organization's timezone setting to determine week boundaries).

3. Pending timesheets count: COUNT of hrm_time_tracking_timesheets WHERE employee.organization_id = current AND status = 'submitted' AND deleted_at IS NULL.

4. Projects with budget utilization > 80%: SELECT from hrm_time_tracking_projects WHERE organization_id = current AND status = 'active' AND budget_hours IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL. For each project, calculate SUM of timelog duration_minutes / 60 and compare against budget_hours. Return projects where SUM/budget_hours > 0.8 along with utilization percentage.

5. Top 5 employees by hours this week: GROUP BY employee_id on timelogs within current week, SUM(duration_minutes), ORDER BY SUM DESC, LIMIT 5. JOIN with employees table to include employee name/id.

All queries MUST enforce organization data isolation — only data belonging to the authenticated user's current organization context. Apply soft-delete filtering (deleted_at IS NULL) on all tables that support it.

responseBody.description: Organization dashboard summary containing aggregated metrics and alerts for quick managerial overview.

operations.description:
Retrieve the list of projects assigned to the current authenticated employee.

This endpoint returns all projects within the currently selected organization that the employee has an active membership in. Each project entry includes the project's name, color code, status, description, start and end dates, along with the employee's role on that project ("member" or "project-lead").

Projects are scoped to the employee's current organization context. Only projects where the employee has an active (non-soft-deleted) membership record are returned. If the employee has no project memberships, an empty paginated list is returned.

Filtering by project status and free-text search on the project name are supported through the request body. Results are paginated for efficient browsing.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_tracking_project_members with employee context from the authenticated session, joining hrm_time_tracking_projects for project details:

1. Resolve the current employee record from the authenticated member's session and current organization context (hrm_time_tracking_member_id + hrm_time_tracking_organization_id)
2. Query project_members where hrm_time_tracking_employee_id = current employee's id AND deleted_at IS NULL
3. Join hrm_time_tracking_projects where id = hrm_time_tracking_project_id AND deleted_at IS NULL
4. Apply optional filters from request body:
   - status: filter projects by their lifecycle status (active, archived, completed)
   - search: text search on project name (case-insensitive LIKE/ILIKE)
5. Include the project_member.role field in each result (employee's role on the project)
6. Apply pagination (page, limit) and return sorted by project name or created_at
7. Return empty page if no memberships found

Edge cases: deactivated employees cannot access this endpoint (blocked at auth middleware layer); soft-deleted memberships are excluded; soft-deleted projects are excluded.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of project summary records assigned to the current employee. Each summary includes the project name, color code, status, description, start/end dates, and the employee's role on the project.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination criteria for filtering the employee's assigned projects. Supports optional status filter, free-text name search, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Change the lifecycle status of a project.

This operation allows users with `project:manage` permission to transition a project from its current status to a new status.
