Used for task prioritization and schedule tracking. Past due dates are allowed, indicating overdue tasks. Send `null` to remove the existing deadline.
dueDate.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_tracking_tasks.due_date (column name: due_date). ISO 8601 date-time. Nullable — use null to clear the deadline.

hrmTimeTrackingEmployeeId.description:
The unique identifier of the employee assigned to complete this task.

Must be a UUID referencing an active employee with a valid project membership in the parent project. The assigned employee must be a member of the project (have a non-deleted entry in the project members table). Send `null` to unassign the current employee.
hrmTimeTrackingEmployeeId.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_tracking_tasks.hrm_time_tracking_employee_id. UUID or null. Validated as active project member — must have a non-deleted entry in hrm_time_tracking_project_members for this project.

IHrmTimeTrackingTask.IUpdate.description:
The task attributes to be updated. All fields are optional — only provided fields are applied; omitted fields retain their current values. The task's project association cannot be changed through this endpoint.

Use `null` to clear a nullable field: set `description` to `null` to remove the description, set `hrmTimeTrackingEmployeeId` to `null` to unassign the employee, set `estimatedHours` to `null` to clear the estimate, or set `dueDate` to `null` to remove the deadline.

Status transitions follow a linear lifecycle: open → in-progress → completed → closed. Statuses cannot be skipped or regressed. When the status field is changed, an immutable TaskHistory entry is automatically created to record the transition.

Employee assignment is subject to validation: the assigned employee must have an active (non-deleted) project membership record in the parent project at the time of update.
IHrmTimeTrackingTask.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Update DTO for hrm_time_tracking_tasks. All fields optional — partial updates only. Nullable fields (description, estimatedHours, dueDate, hrmTimeTrackingEmployeeId) use oneOf with null for explicit clearing. Validation: title (non-empty string if provided), status (one of: open, in-progress, completed, closed — linear forward-only transition), priority (one of: low, medium, high, urgent), estimatedHours (non-negative float), dueDate (ISO date-time), hrmTimeTrackingEmployeeId (UUID, validated as active project member — must exist in hrm_time_tracking_project_members where project matches and deleted_at is null). Excluded: id (immutable PK), projectId (path param), parentTaskId (immutable), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (system-managed timestamps).

IHrmTimeTrackingActivityLog.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request for retrieving a paginated list of activity log entries within the current organization.

Activity logs provide an immutable audit trail of significant organizational actions, including employee lifecycle events, contract changes, project operations, task status transitions, timesheet workflow events, and role assignment changes. This request allows filtering by keyword, action type, actor member, and date range.

All filters are optional; omitting all filters returns all activity log entries for the organization ordered chronologically (most recent first). The organization scope is determined by the authenticated member's current organization context — no organization ID parameter is needed.

Apply optional request body filters: search applies LIKE on target_entity_name and details columns; activity_log_type_code filters via JOIN to hrm_time_tracking_activity_log_types on code; member_id filters by hrm_time_tracking_member_id (actor FK); from_date/to_date apply range filter on created_at with exclusive upper bound (to_date is exclusive). Support cursor-based pagination with page/limit parameters, sorted by created_at descending by default. Limit is capped at 100 records maximum.

stoppedAtFrom.description:
Start of the date range filter for when the timer was stopped.

Filters for timer sessions whose stopped_at timestamp is greater than or equal to this value. Combine with stoppedAtTo to define a complete time range (inclusive on both ends). Running timers (null stopped_at) are excluded from results when this filter is applied. Format: ISO 8601 date-time.
stoppedAtFrom.x-autobe-specification: Lower bound range filter on hrm_time_tracking_timers.stopped_at. ISO 8601 format. Applied as: stopped_at >= stoppedAtFrom. Combine with stoppedAtTo for inclusive range. Running timers (null stopped_at) are excluded when this filter is active.

stoppedAtTo.description:
End of the date range filter for when the timer was stopped.

Filters for timer sessions whose stopped_at timestamp is less than or equal to this value. Combine with stoppedAtFrom to define a complete time range (inclusive on both ends). Format: ISO 8601 date-time.
stoppedAtTo.x-autobe-specification: Upper bound range filter on hrm_time_tracking_timers.stopped_at. ISO 8601 format. Applied as: stopped_at <= stoppedAtTo. Combine with stoppedAtFrom for inclusive range.

sort.description:
Field to sort the timer records by for cursor-based pagination.

Supports sorting by started_at, stopped_at, or status. The sort direction (ascending/descending) is encoded within the cursor value. Default sorting is by started_at in descending order (newest timer sessions first).
sort.x-autobe-specification: Cursor-based pagination sort field. Allowed values: started_at, stopped_at, status. Sort direction encoded within cursor. Default: started_at descending (newest first).

limit.description:
Maximum number of timer records to return per page.

Controls the page size for cursor-based pagination. Must be between 1 and 100. The actual number of records returned may be less than this value on the final page.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Cursor-based pagination page size. Controls maximum records per page. Minimum: 1, Maximum: 100. Default applied by the service layer if not provided.

cursor.description:
Pagination cursor for retrieving the next page of timer records.

Provide the cursor value returned in the previous page response to fetch the next set of results. Omit or pass null to retrieve the first page.
cursor.x-autobe-specification: Cursor-based pagination continuation token. Opaque string returned from the previous page response. Null/omitted for the first page request.

page.description:
Target page number to retrieve (1-indexed).

Specifies which page of results to return. Page numbering starts from 1. If omitted, null, or undefined, defaults to page 1 (first page). Requesting a page beyond the available range returns an empty data array with valid pagination metadata reflecting the actual totals.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-indexed page number for page-based pagination (fallback). Defaults to 1 if not provided. When both cursor and page are provided, cursor takes precedence.

IHrmTimeTrackingTimer.IRequest.description:
Search criteria for filtering and paginating timer records within the organization.

Provides comprehensive filtering by timer status (running, stopped, discarded), associated project, optional task assignment, and date ranges for start and stop timestamps. Supports cursor-based pagination with configurable sorting for efficient browsing of large timer histories.

The employeeId filter is permission-sensitive — users with the time:view_all permission can filter by any employee in the organization, while users without this permission can only browse their own timer records.
IHrmTimeTrackingTimer.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Computed search request type for querying hrm_time_tracking_timers. Filter fields map to SQL WHERE clauses: employeeId→hrm_time_tracking_employee_id, status→status, projectId→hrm_time_tracking_project_id, taskId→hrm_time_tracking_task_id, startedAtFrom/startedAtTo→started_at (range), stoppedAtFrom/stoppedAtTo→stopped_at (range). The employeeId filter is conditionally applied at the service layer based on time:view_all permission. date-time fields use ISO 8601 format. Pagination fields (sort, limit, cursor, page) control cursor-based result set navigation.

IHrmTimeTrackingActivityLogType.description:
Complete record of an activity log type classification used by audit trail entries.

Each activity log type defines a distinct auditable action category (e.g., 'employee.invited', 'project.created', 'timesheet.approved') using a structured {category}.{action} dot-notation identifier. These types are system-defined reference records seeded during organization initialization — users cannot create, modify, or delete them directly.

The record includes the unique code, optional category grouping, human-readable display name, and detailed description explaining when the action type is triggered and recorded.

No JOINs needed. No belongs-to relations exist. The reverse has-many activityLogs relation is excluded because log entries are independent entities that reference this type via FK — not a child composition to embed. Used for read-only lookups via the unique `code` index.

id.description: Unique identifier for the activity log entry.

targetEntityType.description:
Type of the business entity that was acted upon.

Identifies the kind of entity targeted by the action (e.g., Employee, Contract, Project, Task, Timesheet, Role). Used in conjunction with targetEntityId to uniquely reference the affected entity.

UUID of the business entity that was acted upon.

details.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_tracking_activity_logs.details. Nullable in DB, represented as oneOf string|null.

IHrmTimeTrackingActivityLog.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an activity log entry optimized for list displays in audit trail and investigation views.

Each entry captures a single auditable action within the organization, including the actor who performed it, the action type classification, the target entity reference, and optional contextual details.

This summary includes the actor's identity (display name and email via {@link actor}) and the action type's code and name (via {@link activityLogType}), making it suitable for browsing and filtering without requiring additional lookups.
IHrmTimeTrackingActivityLog.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct fields: id (UUID), targetEntityType (target_entity_type), targetEntityId (target_entity_id), targetEntityName (target_entity_name), details (nullable String). Relations: actor via member_id JOIN to hrm_time_tracking_members (ISummary: id, displayName, email, avatar), activityLogType via activity_log_type_id JOIN to hrm_time_tracking_activity_log_types (ISummary: id, code, name). Timestamps: created_at mapped as createdAt. Excluded: hrm_time_tracking_organization_id (JWT session context provides scoping), organization relation (implied by session), FK columns exposed as relation objects.

rejection_reason.description:
The reason explaining why the timesheet was rejected.

Must be a non-empty string providing actionable feedback to the employee about what needs to be corrected before resubmission. The rejection reason is stored on the timesheet record and is visible to both the employee and reviewer in the timesheet history.
rejection_reason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the DB column hrm_time_tracking_timesheets.rejection_reason (nullable String). Controller-level validation enforces non-empty string for the reject action per Section 530 business rules — not enforced at the JSON Schema level to avoid validation loopholes with oneOf/null branching.

IHrmTimeTrackingTimesheet.IReject.description:
Rejection payload containing the mandatory reason explaining why a submitted timesheet was rejected.

The {@link rejection_reason} provides context for the employee about why their timesheet was returned to draft status, enabling them to make the necessary corrections before resubmitting.

The timesheet to reject is identified via the `timesheetId` path parameter. The rejecting reviewer is automatically determined from the authenticated member's JWT — not provided in the request body.
IHrmTimeTrackingTimesheet.IReject.x-autobe-specification: Maps rejection_reason directly to the DB column rejection_reason on hrm_time_tracking_timesheets. The path parameter timesheetId identifies which timesheet to reject, the reviewer identity (hrm_time_tracking_reviewer_id) is resolved from the JWT of the authenticated member, and the reviewed_at timestamp is set by the controller on rejection — none of these appear in the request body.

IHrmTimeTrackingProject.description:
Complete project entity within the time tracking system.

A project is a work initiative within an organization that serves as a container for time tracking, task management, and reporting activities. Each project belongs to exactly one organization and follows a lifecycle through active, archived, and completed statuses.

The {@link organization} provides the multi-tenant context. The {@link projectMembers} array lists employees assigned to this project with their roles. The {@link tasks} array contains discrete work items. The {@link timelogs} array records all time entries logged against this project. The {@link timers} array tracks any active or completed timer sessions associated with this project.
IHrmTimeTrackingProject.x-autobe-specification: Direct fields: id, name, description, color_code, status, budget_hours, started_at, ended_at, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. BELONGS-TO: organization via JOIN on hrm_time_tracking_organization_id → IHrmTimeTrackingOrganization.ISummary. HAS-MANY: projectMembers (junction to employees), tasks, timelogs, timers — each as full entity arrays via separate queries or JOINs.

IHrmTimeTrackingTimesheet.description:
A weekly timesheet aggregating an employee's timelogs for a Monday-to-Sunday work period, tracking lifecycle through draft, submitted, approved, and rejected states.

Each timesheet belongs to exactly one {@link employee} and may be reviewed by an authorized {@link reviewer}. The {@link status} field tracks the approval workflow: `draft` (composing), `submitted` (pending review), `approved` (finalized, timelogs locked), or `rejected` (returned to draft with a {@link rejectionReason}).

The {@link totalHours} is automatically computed from the duration of all included {@link timelogs}. When approved, all associated timelogs become permanently locked. When rejected, the timesheet returns to `draft` status with a rejection reason, allowing the employee to modify and resubmit.
IHrmTimeTrackingTimesheet.x-autobe-specification: Direct: id, week_start_date, week_end_date, status, total_hours, submitted_at, reviewed_at, rejection_reason, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Relations: employee via JOIN (hrm_time_tracking_employees), reviewer via JOIN (hrm_time_tracking_members, nullable). Compositions: timelogs via JOIN (hrm_time_tracking_timelogs WHERE timesheet_id matches).

id.description:
The unique identifier of the activity log entry.

id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_tracking_activity_logs.id. UUID format.

organization.description:
The organization that owns this activity log entry.

member.description:
The member who performed the action that triggered this activity log entry.

The summary includes the member's unique identifier, email address, display name, optional avatar URL, optional phone number, and account lifecycle timestamps.
member.x-autobe-specification: Join from hrm_time_tracking_activity_logs.hrm_time_tracking_member_id to hrm_time_tracking_members.id. Returns IHrmTimeTrackingMember.ISummary (id, email, display_name, avatar, phone_number, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at).

IHrmTimeTrackingActivityLog.description:
A single immutable activity log entry recording a significant organizational action.

Each entry captures an auditable event within an organization, including the timestamp of occurrence, the actor (member) who performed the action, the action type classification, and a reference to the affected business entity with its type, UUID, and display name. Activity log entries are created automatically by the system whenever a significant action occurs — employee lifecycle events, contract changes, project operations, task status transitions, timesheet workflow events, and role assignments. Once created, entries are never modified or deleted, forming a permanent audit trail for organizational governance.

Available via the {@link at} endpoint. Accessible only to members with the org:manage permission within the owning organization. If the requested activity log does not exist or belongs to a different organization, the system returns 404 Not Found to avoid information leakage.
IHrmTimeTrackingActivityLog.x-autobe-specification: Query hrm_time_tracking_activity_logs by id UUID. JOIN hrm_time_tracking_organizations for organization (id, name, description, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month, status) with owner sub-join. JOIN hrm_time_tracking_members for actor member (id, email, display_name, avatar, phone_number, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at). JOIN hrm_time_tracking_activity_log_types for action type (id, code, category, name, description). Direct fields: target_entity_type → targetEntityType, target_entity_id → targetEntityId, target_entity_name → targetEntityName, details → details, created_at → createdAt.

activeEmployeeCount.description:
Total number of employees currently in active status within the organization.

This metric counts all employee records where the employment status is set to 'active' and the record has not been soft-deleted. It provides a quick headcount of the current workforce available for assignment and time tracking.
activeEmployeeCount.x-autobe-specification: COUNT of hrm_time_tracking_employees WHERE organization_id = current AND status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL. Returns total number of currently active employees in the organization.

weeklyHours.description:
Total hours logged by all employees during the current work week.

The current week is defined as Monday through Sunday, calculated using the organization's configured timezone setting. This aggregate sums all timelog durations across every employee, providing a team-wide view of weekly productivity.
weeklyHours.x-autobe-specification: SUM(duration_minutes)/60.0 from hrm_time_tracking_timelogs JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees WHERE employee.organization_id = current AND timelog.date within current Monday-Sunday week (use organization's timezone for week boundaries) AND timelog.deleted_at IS NULL. Returns total hours as a float.

pendingTimesheetCount.description:
Number of submitted timesheets currently awaiting manager approval.

Timesheets enter the 'submitted' state when employees finalize their weekly entries. This metric helps managers identify outstanding approval work that needs their attention.
pendingTimesheetCount.x-autobe-specification: COUNT of hrm_time_tracking_timesheets JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees WHERE employee.organization_id = current AND timesheet.status = 'submitted' AND timesheet.deleted_at IS NULL. Returns count of timesheets awaiting approval.

budgetAlerts.description:
Projects where actual logged hours have exceeded 80% of the budgeted hours.

This alert helps managers proactively monitor budget consumption. Only active projects with a defined budget are evaluated. The utilization percentage is calculated as (total logged hours ÷ budgeted hours) × 100. Projects exceeding the 80% threshold are returned with their budget details and current utilization rate, enabling timely intervention before budgets are fully consumed.
budgetAlerts.x-autobe-specification: Query hrm_time_tracking_projects WHERE organization_id = current AND status = 'active' AND budget_hours IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL. For each project, calculate total logged hours from timelogs (SUM duration_minutes/60 where deleted_at IS NULL). Compute utilization_pct = total_logged / budget_hours * 100. Return projects where utilization_pct > 80 as an array of { projectId, projectName, budgetHours, totalLoggedHours, utilizationPercent } objects.

topEmployees.description:
Top 5 employees ranked by total hours logged during the current work week.

Employees are ranked in descending order based on the sum of their timelog durations. This metric highlights the most active contributors and provides visibility into workload distribution across the team.
topEmployees.x-autobe-specification: GROUP BY employee_id on hrm_time_tracking_timelogs within current Monday-Sunday week (same week boundaries as weeklyHours), SUM(duration_minutes), ORDER BY SUM DESC, LIMIT 5. JOIN with hrm_time_tracking_employees for employee name. Returns array of { employeeId, employeeName, totalHours } objects ordered by hours descending.

IHrmTimeTrackingOrganizationDashboard.description:
Organization dashboard providing a high-level overview of team productivity and operational status.

Aggregates real-time data across all active employees, projects, timelogs, and timesheets within the organization. Includes total active employee headcount, total hours logged this week, count of pending timesheets awaiting approval, projects exceeding 80% budget utilization, and the top 5 employees by hours logged this week.

All metrics are computed in real-time from the underlying data and scoped strictly to the authenticated user's organization context. Requires the `report:view` permission.
IHrmTimeTrackingOrganizationDashboard.x-autobe-specification:
Computed/aggregated response type with no single-table mapping. Data is queried across multiple tables (hrm_time_tracking_employees, hrm_time_tracking_timelogs, hrm_time_tracking_timesheets, hrm_time_tracking_projects) scoped to the authenticated user's current organization context. All queries must enforce organization data isolation via organization_id and apply soft-delete filtering (deleted_at IS NULL) on all tables that support it. Requires report:view permission.

(1) activeEmployeeCount: COUNT of hrm_time_tracking_employees WHERE organization_id = current AND status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL.

(2) weeklyHours: SUM(duration_minutes)/60.0 from hrm_time_tracking_timelogs JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees WHERE employee.organization_id = current AND timelog.date within current Monday-Sunday week (use organization's timezone for week boundaries) AND timelog.deleted_at IS NULL.

(3) pendingTimesheetCount: COUNT of hrm_time_tracking_timesheets JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees WHERE employee.organization_id = current AND timesheet.status = 'submitted' AND timesheet.deleted_at IS NULL.

(4) budgetAlerts: Query hrm_time_tracking_projects WHERE organization_id = current AND status = 'active' AND budget_hours IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL. For each project, calculate total logged hours from timelogs (SUM duration_minutes/60). Compute utilization_pct = total_logged / budget_hours * 100. Return projects where utilization_pct > 80 with their utilization percentage. Returns array of { projectId, projectName, budgetHours, totalLoggedHours, utilizationPercent } objects.

(5) topEmployees: GROUP BY employee_id on timelogs within current week (same week boundaries as step 2), SUM(duration_minutes), ORDER BY SUM DESC, LIMIT 5. JOIN with employees table for name/id. Returns array of { employeeId, employeeName, totalHours } objects.

today_hours.description:
The total number of hours logged by the employee today.

Calculated by summing the duration of all timelog entries created by the employee for the current calendar date, respecting the organization's configured timezone for determining the date boundary. Expressed in decimal hours (e.g., 7.5 for 7 hours and 30 minutes).
today_hours.x-autobe-specification: Computed: SUM(duration_minutes) FROM hrm_time_tracking_timelogs WHERE employee_id={employeeId} AND date=TODAY(in org timezone) AND deleted_at IS NULL. Convert minutes to decimal hours (divide by 60).

week_hours.description:
The total number of hours logged by the employee this work week.

The work week runs Monday through Sunday, with boundaries determined by the organization's configured timezone. Calculated by summing the duration of all timelog entries created by the employee within this period. Expressed in decimal hours.
week_hours.x-autobe-specification: Computed: SUM(duration_minutes) FROM hrm_time_tracking_timelogs WHERE employee_id={employeeId} AND date BETWEEN week_start(Monday) AND week_end(Sunday in org timezone) AND deleted_at IS NULL. Convert to decimal hours (divide by 60).

active_timer.description:
The employee's currently active timer session, if one exists.

An employee may have at most one running timer at any time. When present, the timer object includes the associated project name, optional task name, and the started_at timestamp from which elapsed duration can be calculated. Null when no timer is currently running.
active_timer.x-autobe-specification: Computed: SELECT FROM hrm_time_tracking_timers WHERE employee_id={employeeId} AND status='running'. Return as IHrmTimeTrackingTimer.ISummary with project and task relations joined. If no running timer exists, return null.

recent_timelogs.description:
The five most recent timelog entries created by the employee.

Provides a quick overview of recently logged work. Each entry includes the associated project, optional task, date, duration, description, and billable status. Ordered by creation time with the newest entry first.
recent_timelogs.x-autobe-specification: Computed: SELECT TOP 5 FROM hrm_time_tracking_timelogs WHERE employee_id={employeeId} AND deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY created_at DESC. Join project, employee, optional task, optional timesheet relations. Return as IHrmTimeTrackingTimelog.ISummary[].

pending_timesheet.description:
The current work week's timesheet, if one exists.

Returns the timesheet for the current Monday-to-Sunday work week, including its status (draft, submitted, approved, or rejected) and total hours. Null when the employee has not yet created a timesheet for the current week.
pending_timesheet.x-autobe-specification: Computed: SELECT FROM hrm_time_tracking_timesheets WHERE employee_id={employeeId} AND week_start_date=CURRENT_WEEK_MONDAY(in org timezone). Return as IHrmTimeTrackingTimesheet.ISummary with employee and optional reviewer relations joined. Null if no timesheet exists for the current week.

assigned_tasks.description:
Tasks assigned to the employee that are currently open or in progress.

Provides a focused view of active work items the employee needs to address. Excludes completed, closed, and soft-deleted tasks. Each task includes its title, status, priority level, due date, estimated hours, and associated project.
assigned_tasks.x-autobe-specification: Computed: SELECT FROM hrm_time_tracking_tasks WHERE hrm_time_tracking_employee_id={employeeId} AND status IN ('open','in-progress') AND deleted_at IS NULL. Join project and optional assignedEmployee/parentTask relations. Return as IHrmTimeTrackingTask.ISummary[].

organization.description:
Organization-wide dashboard metrics, conditionally included when the employee has the report:view permission.

Provides enterprise-level insights including the total number of active employees, total hours logged across the organization this week, pending timesheets awaiting approval, projects nearing or exceeding 80% budget utilization, and the top 5 employees by hours logged this week.

This section is omitted from the response when the authenticated employee's role does not include the report:view permission.
organization.x-autobe-specification: Computed nested object (IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.IOrganization) conditionally included when the employee's role has 'report:view' permission. Contains: total_active_employees (COUNT employees WHERE org_id={orgId} AND status='active'), total_week_hours (SUM timelogs via employee JOIN), pending_timesheet_count (COUNT submitted timesheets), budget_alerts (IBudgetAlert[] — projects >80% budget utilization), top_employees (ITopEmployee[] — top 5 by hours).

IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.description:
Comprehensive dashboard response providing the authenticated employee's personal work status overview with optional organization-wide metrics.

The personal section is always included and provides hours logged today and this week (both in decimal hours), the currently running timer with elapsed duration (if any), the five most recent timelog entries, the current week's timesheet status and total hours (if one exists), and tasks assigned to the employee that are still open or in-progress.

When the employee's role includes the report:view permission, an additional organization section is included with enterprise-wide metrics: total number of active employees, total hours logged across all employees this week, the number of pending timesheets awaiting approval, projects approaching or exceeding 80% budget utilization, and the top 5 employees by hours logged this week.

All date calculations respect the organization's configured timezone. Data access is strictly scoped to the current organization — no cross-organization data is exposed. If the authenticated employee is not found in the current organization context, a 404 error is returned.
IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.x-autobe-specification:
Computed dashboard response aggregating data from multiple tables. All date calculations use the organization's configured timezone. All duration values are in decimal hours (minutes/60).

**Personal Dashboard** (always included):
1. today_hours: SUM(duration_minutes) FROM hrm_time_tracking_timelogs WHERE employee_id={employeeId} AND date=TODAY(org tz) AND deleted_at IS NULL → /60
2. week_hours: SUM(duration_minutes) FROM hrm_time_tracking_timelogs WHERE employee_id={employeeId} AND date BETWEEN week_start AND week_end(org tz) AND deleted_at IS NULL → /60
3. active_timer: SELECT FROM hrm_time_tracking_timers WHERE employee_id={employeeId} AND status='running'. Return as IHrmTimeTrackingTimer.ISummary or null.
4. recent_timelogs: Last 5 timelogs (ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 5) FROM hrm_time_tracking_timelogs WHERE employee_id={employeeId} AND deleted_at IS NULL. Return as IHrmTimeTrackingTimelog.ISummary[].
5. pending_timesheet: SELECT FROM hrm_time_tracking_timesheets WHERE employee_id={employeeId} AND week_start_date=CURRENT_WEEK_MONDAY(org tz). Return as IHrmTimeTrackingTimesheet.ISummary or null.
6. assigned_tasks: SELECT FROM hrm_time_tracking_tasks WHERE hrm_time_tracking_employee_id={employeeId} AND status IN ('open','in-progress') AND deleted_at IS NULL. Return as IHrmTimeTrackingTask.ISummary[].

**Organization Dashboard** (conditional, only if employee role has 'report:view' permission):
- IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.IOrganization nested object containing:
  - total_active_employees: COUNT FROM hrm_time_tracking_employees WHERE organization_id={orgId} AND status='active' AND deleted_at IS NULL
  - total_week_hours: SUM(duration_minutes) FROM hrm_time_tracking_timelogs JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees ON employee_id=employees.id WHERE organization_id={orgId} AND date BETWEEN week_start AND week_end AND deleted_at IS NULL → /60
  - pending_timesheet_count: COUNT FROM hrm_time_tracking_timesheets JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees WHERE status='submitted' AND employees.organization_id={orgId}
  - budget_alerts (IBudgetAlert[]): Projects WHERE organization_id={orgId} AND status='active' AND budget_hours IS NOT NULL AND (SUM timelog_duration/(budget_hours*60))>0.8
  - top_employees (ITopEmployee[]): GROUP BY employee_id SUM(duration), JOIN employees, ORDER BY SUM DESC LIMIT 5

Sub-types: IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.IOrganization, IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.IBudgetAlert, IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.ITopEmployee are defined separately.

projectId.description:
The unique identifier of the project that is approaching or exceeding its allocated time budget.

This identifier references the project record from which all budget alert data is derived. It can be used to navigate to the full project details or to cross-reference with other project-related endpoints.
projectId.x-autobe-specification: Data sourced from hrm_time_tracking_projects.id. UUID primary key of the project record that qualifies for budget alert status (active status, has budget_hours defined, utilization > 80%, not deleted).

projectName.description:
The display name of the project, shown in the budget alert list for easy identification.

This human-readable name helps managers quickly identify which project requires attention without needing to cross-reference project IDs.
projectName.x-autobe-specification: Data sourced from hrm_time_tracking_projects.name. The display name of the project from the qualifying project record.

budgetHours.description:
The total estimated hours budgeted for this project.

This is the planned time allocation against which actual logged hours are compared. Projects without a defined budget are excluded from budget utilization evaluations. The value is stored as a decimal number representing hours.
budgetHours.x-autobe-specification: Data sourced from hrm_time_tracking_projects.budget_hours. Only populated when budget_hours IS NOT NULL for active, non-deleted projects.

totalLoggedHours.description:
The total hours logged against this project across all employee timelogs.

Calculated by summing all timelog durations (recorded in minutes) linked to this project, then converting to hours. This value is compared against the budgeted hours to determine the budget utilization percentage. Only timelogs that have not been soft-deleted are included in the calculation.
totalLoggedHours.x-autobe-specification: Computed as SUM(hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60.0 for timelogs WHERE timelog.hrm_time_tracking_project_id = project.id AND timelog.deleted_at IS NULL. Rounded to 2 decimal places.

utilizationPercent.description:
The percentage of budgeted hours that have been consumed by actual logged time.

Calculated as (totalLoggedHours / budgetHours) * 100. Only projects exceeding 80% utilization are included in this budget alert list. Values approaching or exceeding 100% indicate the project has fully consumed or exceeded its allocated time budget, signaling the need for immediate management attention.
utilizationPercent.x-autobe-specification: Computed as (totalLoggedHours / budgetHours) * 100. This value is always > 80 due to the query filter as only projects exceeding 80% utilization are returned. Rounded to 2 decimal places.

IHrmTimeTrackingOrganizationDashboard.IB.description:
A budget alert for a project whose actual logged hours have exceeded 80% of the budgeted hours.

This alert helps managers proactively monitor budget consumption before projects exceed their allocated time budgets. Only active projects with a defined budget are evaluated. The utilization percentage is calculated as (total logged hours / budgeted hours) * 100.

Projects returned here require attention as they are approaching or have exceeded their budgeted hours.
IHrmTimeTrackingOrganizationDashboard.IB.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregation type with no single-table mapping. Data sourced from hrm_time_tracking_projects and aggregated hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.

Query: SELECT from hrm_time_tracking_projects WHERE organization_id = current AND status = 'active' AND budget_hours IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL. For each qualifying project, calculate total logged hours by aggregating associated hrm_time_tracking_timelogs (SUM(duration_minutes) / 60.0 WHERE deleted_at IS NULL). Compute utilization_percent = (total_logged_hours / budget_hours) * 100. Filter to only projects where utilization_percent > 80.

(1) projectId: String from projects.id.
(2) projectName: String from projects.name.
(3) budgetHours: Number from projects.budget_hours.
(4) totalLoggedHours: Number computed as SUM(timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60.0 WHERE timelog.hrm_time_tracking_project_id = project.id AND timelog.deleted_at IS NULL.
(5) utilizationPercent: Number computed as (totalLoggedHours / budgetHours) * 100.

employeeId.description:
Unique identifier of the employee from the organization's employee roster.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the employee record within the organization, used to identify the employee in subsequent API calls or detail views.
employeeId.x-autobe-specification: Resolved by including hrm_time_tracking_employees.id in the SELECT clause during GROUP BY aggregation on hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.hrm_time_tracking_employee_id, joined via hrm_time_tracking_employees.id = hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.hrm_time_tracking_employee_id. Maps to hrm_time_tracking_employees.id (UUID).

employeeName.description:
Display name of the employee for identification in the leaderboard.

The employee's display name is sourced from their linked member account's global profile, ensuring consistent naming across all organizations the user belongs to. This value comes from the member record, not the employee record.
employeeName.x-autobe-specification: Resolved by joining hrm_time_tracking_employees.member relation (hrm_time_tracking_member_id -> hrm_time_tracking_members.id) to retrieve hrm_time_tracking_members.display_name. The employees table does NOT have a name column; the display name is sourced from the linked member account's global profile shared across all organizations.

totalHours.description:
Total hours logged by the employee during the current Monday-to-Sunday work week, calculated using the organization's configured timezone.

The value is derived by summing all timelog durations (in minutes) for the employee within the current week boundaries and converting to hours. Only active, non-deleted timelogs are included in the calculation. Hours are displayed as a decimal number.
totalHours.x-autobe-specification: Computed as SUM(hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60.0, grouped by hrm_time_tracking_employee_id, filtered to the current Monday-to-Sunday week using the organization's configured timezone. Only non-deleted timelogs (hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL) from non-deleted employees (hrm_time_tracking_employees.deleted_at IS NULL) within the current organization context are included. Results are ordered by SUM(duration_minutes) DESC and limited to 5.

IHrmTimeTrackingOrganizationDashboard.IT.description:
An employee ranked in the top 5 performers by total hours logged during the current work week.

Each entry identifies an employee by their unique identifier and display name, along with the aggregate hours they have logged on timelogs between Monday and Sunday of the current week. Hours are calculated using the organization's configured timezone and employees are ranked in descending order by total hours logged. Only active (non-deleted) employees with non-deleted timelogs are considered. If no employees have logged time during the week, the result is an empty array.
IHrmTimeTrackingOrganizationDashboard.IT.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregation type. Data source: GROUP BY hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.hrm_time_tracking_employee_id within current Monday-Sunday week boundaries (using organization's configured timezone). SUM(duration_minutes)/60.0 as totalHours. JOIN with hrm_time_tracking_employees for employee ID. JOIN with hrm_time_tracking_members via hrm_time_tracking_employees.member relation (hrm_time_tracking_member_id -> hrm_time_tracking_members.id) for employee display name. ORDER BY SUM(duration_minutes) DESC, LIMIT 5.

- employeeId: hrm_time_tracking_employees.id (UUID)
- employeeName: hrm_time_tracking_members.display_name (resolved via hrm_time_tracking_employees.member relation on hrm_time_tracking_member_id)
- totalHours: SUM(hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60.0

Must enforce organization data isolation via hrm_time_tracking_employees.hrm_time_tracking_organization_id = current organization context. Apply soft-delete filtering (hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL, hrm_time_tracking_employees.deleted_at IS NULL). If no timelogs exist for the current week within the organization, return empty array.

id.description:
Primary key — unique identifier for each guest session record.

This UUID is assigned by the system upon session creation and serves as the canonical identifier for referencing this session across the platform.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_tracking_guest_sessions.id. Primary key, UUID format.

ip.description:
The IP address of the guest's client at the time the session was created.

Used for basic security auditing and geographic analysis of access patterns. This value is captured once at session creation and never updated.

href.description:
The current page URL (document location) at the time the session was created.

Captures the entry point or landing page where the guest session was initiated, useful for traffic source analysis and navigation path auditing.

referrer.description:
The HTTP Referer header value at the time the session was created.

Indicates the previous page from which the guest arrived, enabling analysis of navigation paths, marketing attribution, and external traffic sources.

guest.description:
The guest identity that owns this session.

Each session belongs to a single guest record identified by device fingerprint. The guest summary provides essential identifying information about the anonymous visitor who initiated the session.
guest.x-autobe-specification: Join via hrm_time_tracking_guest_id → hrm_time_tracking_guests.id. Rendered as IHrmTimeTrackingGuest.ISummary.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this session was created.

This field is never updated — sessions are append-only records. Used for session age calculation and audit purposes.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_tracking_guest_sessions.created_at.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when this session expires. Sessions past this timestamp are considered invalid and rejected by the authentication system.

Non-nullable by default for security — every session must have a defined expiration. Clients should check this field to determine if re-authentication is required.

IHrmTimeTrackingGuestSession.description:
A guest authentication session record containing the HTTP context captured at session creation time for security auditing.

Each session is associated with a single guest identity and records the client IP address, the current page URL (href), and the HTTP referrer at the moment the session was created. Sessions have a fixed expiration timestamp (expired_at) after which they are rejected by the authentication system.

This is an append-only record — sessions are never modified once created. A single guest may have multiple concurrent sessions across different devices or browsers.
IHrmTimeTrackingGuestSession.x-autobe-specification: Direct column mappings: id → hrm_time_tracking_guest_sessions.id (UUID, PK), ip → ip, href → href, referrer → referrer, created_at → created_at, expired_at → expired_at. Relation: guest via JOIN on hrm_time_tracking_guest_id → hrm_time_tracking_guests.id, rendered as IHrmTimeTrackingGuest.ISummary. Excluded: hrm_time_tracking_guest_id (FK column, exposed via guest relation instead).

total_active_employees.description:
The total number of active employees in the organization.

Calculated by counting employee records within the current organization where the status is 'active' and the record has not been soft-deleted. This provides an accurate headcount of currently operational team members.
total_active_employees.x-autobe-specification: COUNT FROM hrm_time_tracking_employees WHERE hrm_time_tracking_organization_id={orgId} AND status='active' AND deleted_at IS NULL. Returns a non-negative integer representing the headcount of currently active team members in the organization.

total_week_hours.description:
The total hours logged across all employees in the organization this work week.

The work week runs Monday through Sunday, with boundaries determined by the organization's configured timezone. Calculated by summing the duration of all timelog entries created by all employees within this period and converting to decimal hours. Reflects the overall team productivity for the current week.
total_week_hours.x-autobe-specification: SUM(hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60.0 FROM hrm_time_tracking_timelogs JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees ON hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.hrm_time_tracking_employee_id = hrm_time_tracking_employees.id WHERE hrm_time_tracking_employees.hrm_time_tracking_organization_id={orgId} AND hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.date BETWEEN week_start(Monday 00:00:00 in org tz) AND week_end(Sunday 23:59:59 in org tz) AND hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL AND hrm_time_tracking_employees.deleted_at IS NULL. The work week boundaries are determined by the organization's configured timezone. Returns decimal hours.

pending_timesheet_count.description:
The number of submitted timesheets awaiting approval across the organization.

Counts timesheets in the 'submitted' status that belong to employees within the current organization. This metric helps managers quickly identify the review workload pending their attention.
pending_timesheet_count.x-autobe-specification: COUNT DISTINCT hrm_time_tracking_timesheets.id FROM hrm_time_tracking_timesheets ts JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees e ON ts.hrm_time_tracking_employee_id = e.id WHERE e.hrm_time_tracking_organization_id={orgId} AND ts.status='submitted' AND ts.deleted_at IS NULL AND e.deleted_at IS NULL. Returns a non-negative integer representing the review workload pending manager attention.

budget_alerts.description:
Active projects that are approaching or exceeding 80% of their budgeted hours.

Each alert includes the project name, budgeted hours, actual hours logged, and the calculated utilization percentage. Only active projects with a defined budget are considered. This helps managers identify potential budget overruns before they become critical.
budget_alerts.x-autobe-specification: SELECT FROM hrm_time_tracking_projects p WHERE p.hrm_time_tracking_organization_id={orgId} AND p.status='active' AND p.budget_hours IS NOT NULL AND p.deleted_at IS NULL. For each matching project: SUM(hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.duration_minutes) FROM hrm_time_tracking_timelogs WHERE hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.hrm_time_tracking_project_id=p.id AND hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL. Calculate utilization = SUM(duration_minutes) / (p.budget_hours * 60). Filter projects where utilization > 0.80. Return each as IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.IBudgetAlert with project name, budgeted hours, actual hours, and utilization percentage. Sorted by utilization descending.

top_employees.description:
The top 5 employees by total hours logged this week.

Provides visibility into the most active contributors within the organization for the current work week. Each entry includes the employee's display name and their total logged hours. Sorted in descending order by total hours.
top_employees.x-autobe-specification: SELECT e.hrm_time_tracking_member_id, SUM(tl.duration_minutes) / 60.0 as total_hours FROM hrm_time_tracking_timelogs tl JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees e ON tl.hrm_time_tracking_employee_id = e.id WHERE tl.date BETWEEN week_start(Monday 00:00:00 in org tz) AND week_end(Sunday 23:59:59 in org tz) AND tl.deleted_at IS NULL AND e.hrm_time_tracking_organization_id={orgId} AND e.deleted_at IS NULL GROUP BY e.hrm_time_tracking_member_id ORDER BY SUM(tl.duration_minutes) DESC LIMIT 5. JOIN hrm_time_tracking_members m ON e.hrm_time_tracking_member_id=m.id to get display_name. Return as IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.ITopEmployee[] with employee display name and total logged hours, sorted descending.

IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.IOrganization.description:
Organization-wide dashboard metrics providing a high-level overview of team productivity and operational status within the current organization.

This nested object is conditionally included in the dashboard response when the authenticated employee's role includes the report:view permission. It provides enterprise-level insights scoped to the current organization context, with all date calculations respecting the organization's configured timezone.

The total_active_employees count reflects the number of employees with active status in the organization. The total_week_hours aggregates all time logged across the organization for the current Monday-to-Sunday work week, expressed in decimal hours. The pending_timesheet_count shows how many submitted timesheets are currently awaiting review by managers. The budget_alerts array identifies active projects that have reached or exceeded 80% of their budgeted hours, helping managers identify potential budget overruns early. The top_employees section highlights the five employees with the most hours logged this week, providing visibility into team contribution levels.

This section is omitted entirely from the dashboard response when the employee lacks the required report:view permission.
IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.IOrganization.x-autobe-specification:
Computed nested object conditionally included in the dashboard response. All date calculations use the organization's configured timezone. All duration values in decimal hours (minutes/60).

1. total_active_employees: COUNT FROM hrm_time_tracking_employees WHERE organization_id={orgId} AND status='active' AND deleted_at IS NULL.
2. total_week_hours: SUM(duration_minutes) FROM hrm_time_tracking_timelogs JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees ON employee_id=employees.id WHERE employees.organization_id={orgId} AND date BETWEEN week_start(Monday) AND week_end(Sunday in org tz) AND timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL AND employees.deleted_at IS NULL → /60.
3. pending_timesheet_count: COUNT DISTINCT FROM hrm_time_tracking_timesheets ts JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees e ON ts.hrm_time_tracking_employee_id=e.id WHERE e.organization_id={orgId} AND ts.status='submitted' AND ts.deleted_at IS NULL AND e.deleted_at IS NULL.
4. budget_alerts: SELECT FROM hrm_time_tracking_projects p WHERE p.organization_id={orgId} AND p.status='active' AND p.budget_hours IS NOT NULL AND p.deleted_at IS NULL. For each project, SUM timelog.duration_minutes via hrm_time_tracking_timelogs WHERE timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL AND timelogs.project_id=p.id. Calculate utilization = SUM(duration_minutes)/(budget_hours*60). Filter where utilization > 0.8. Return as IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.IBudgetAlert[].
5. top_employees: GROUP BY hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.hrm_time_tracking_employee_id, SUM(duration_minutes) WHERE timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL AND date BETWEEN week_start AND week_end. JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees e ON employee_id=e.id WHERE e.organization_id={orgId} AND e.deleted_at IS NULL. JOIN hrm_time_tracking_members m ON e.hrm_time_tracking_member_id=m.id. ORDER BY SUM DESC LIMIT 5. Return as IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.ITopEmployee[].

Authorization: Only included when the authenticated employee has report:view permission. Check via employee's role's permission set before computing aggregate queries.

project_name.description:
The display name of the project approaching or exceeding its budget.

Maps to the project's configured name and is used for identification in budget alert lists and dashboard widgets.
project_name.x-autobe-specification: Maps from hrm_time_tracking_projects.name. Retrieved from projects filtered by organization, active status, non-null budget, and non-deleted.

budgeted_hours.description:
The total budgeted hours allocated to this project.

Represents the planned effort estimate configured when the project was created. Projects without a defined budget are excluded from budget alert calculations.
budgeted_hours.x-autobe-specification: Maps from hrm_time_tracking_projects.budget_hours. Retrieved from projects filtered by organization, active status, non-null budget, and non-deleted.

actual_hours.description:
The total actual hours logged against this project, converted to decimal hours.

The utilization rate as a percentage, calculated as (actual_hours / budgeted_hours) · 100.

IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.IBudgetAlert.description:
A budget alert for a project whose actual logged hours have exceeded 80% of the budgeted hours.

This computed type helps managers identify potential budget overruns before they become critical. It is derived by comparing the total hours logged against the project's configured budget, considering only active projects that have a defined budget. Alerts are sorted by utilization percentage in descending order so that the most at-risk projects appear first.
IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.IBudgetAlert.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_time_tracking_projects p WHERE p.hrm_time_tracking_organization_id={orgId} AND p.status='active' AND p.budget_hours IS NOT NULL AND p.deleted_at IS NULL. For each qualifying project: project_name maps to p.name, budgeted_hours maps to p.budget_hours, actual_hours = SUM(COALESCE(tl.duration_minutes, 0)) / 60.0 FROM hrm_time_tracking_timelogs tl WHERE tl.hrm_time_tracking_project_id = p.id AND tl.deleted_at IS NULL, utilization_percentage = (actual_hours / p.budget_hours) * 100. Only include projects where utilization_percentage > 80. Results sorted by utilization_percentage descending.

member.description:
The top-performing employee's member profile, providing identity and display name information.

Contains the core member profile fields including the unique identifier, email address, display name, optional avatar URL, optional phone number, and account timestamps (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at). This profile is shared across all organizations the member belongs to, ensuring a consistent identity regardless of which organization context they are currently working in.

Returns IHrmTimeTrackingMember.ISummary with fields: id, email, display_name, avatar (nullable URI), phone_number (nullable), created_at, updated_at, deleted_at (nullable).

total_hours.description:

Calculated by aggregating all timelog durations for the employee during the current Monday-to-Sunday work week. Only active, non-deleted timelogs are included in the calculation. Aggregated across all projects and tasks for the week, returning decimal hours.

IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.ITopEmployee.description:
An employee ranked in the top 5 performers by total hours logged during the current work week.

This type represents an employee who has logged the most hours in the current Monday-to-Sunday work week within the organization. The member property identifies the employee through their member profile, including their display name. The total_hours property contains the aggregated decimal hours logged across all projects and tasks for the week.

IHrmTimeTrackingDashboard.ITopEmployee.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregate type. No direct DB table.

1. member: FROM hrm_time_tracking_members m JOIN hrm_time_tracking_employees e ON e.hrm_time_tracking_member_id = m.id WHERE e.hrm_time_tracking_organization_id = {orgId} AND e.deleted_at IS NULL. Returns IHrmTimeTrackingMember.ISummary.

2. total_hours: SUM(hrm_time_tracking_timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60.0 WHERE timelogs.hrm_time_tracking_employee_id = e.id AND timelogs.date BETWEEN week_start(Monday 00:00:00 in org tz) AND week_end(Sunday 23:59:59 in org tz) AND timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL.

Top 5 performers sorted by SUM(duration_minutes) DESC.
